post.description:
Claim a hostname and return the TXT record proving you control it.

409 when another app already holds the host. Hostnames are globally unique,
and a silent overwrite would let one builder take another's traffic -- which
is why `claim_domain` raises rather than upserting.

Check DNS for the TXT record and advance the domain to `verified`.

Idempotent: verifying an already-verified domain re-checks and stays verified,
so a builder can re-run it after a DNS change without a special path.

delete.description:
Release a claimed hostname.

Hostnames are globally unique across every app
(``uq_developer_app_domains_hostname``), so one typo permanently burned that
host for every builder on the platform with no public way to undo it. The
repository had get, list, claim and set_status, and no delete at all.

A HARD delete, not a `revoked` status. The uniqueness index does not care
about status, so a row left behind in any state keeps the host claimed while
looking to the builder like it was released.

OWNERSHIP IS CHECKED AGAINST THE STORED CLAIM, not just the app in the path.
`_require_own_app` proves the caller owns THIS app; the second check proves
the hostname belongs to that same app. Without it a builder could pass their
own app id and any hostname, and delete a competitor's claim -- the one thing
global uniqueness makes irreversible.

404 for an unknown host or one held by another app, never 403: a 403 would
make a competitor's claim discoverable by probing.

Idempotent within your own app: releasing a host you have already released is
a 404, because after the first call the claim genuinely does not exist. The
delete itself reports whether a row went, and both answers are correct.

get.description:
Caddy on-demand-TLS ask endpoint. PUBLIC, UNAUTHENTICATED, FAILS CLOSED.

Caddy issues a certificate when this returns 2xx. Answering 2xx for a host we
do not own would let anyone who points DNS at our edge have a publicly
trusted certificate minted by us.

2xx ONLY for a hostname that exists AND is `verified`. Everything else is a
bare 404 with no body: distinguishing "unknown" from "known but unverified"
would make this a free oracle for which customers are onboarding.

It IS published in the contract. `include_in_schema=False` was the first
instinct -- it is infrastructure plumbing, not a customer API -- and it broke
an invariant: the operation manifest is derived from the OpenAPI spec while
`operation_tiers` is derived from the route table, so hiding a route makes
the two span different universes.
`test_the_manifest_covers_the_WHOLE_operation_universe` exists to catch
exactly that, and it went red on qa.

Hiding it was never a security control anyway -- the endpoint fails closed on
its own, and its existence is inferable from any Caddy config. Consistency
between the published contract and the route table is worth more than the
tidiness of an unlisted endpoint.

The path is `/pipeline` rather than the app's `/move-pipeline`: the verb is
already in the PUT.

`mashup_company_id` is the CANONICAL company id, not a
`cb_company_extensions` / ABM overlay id. They are different tables with
different ids, and the wrong one attaches the deal to nothing.

Rewrite a note.

`content` is a full REPLACEMENT, not a patch, and `mentioned_users` is who
is mentioned AFTER the edit - omitting someone removes their mention. Send
the whole state you want, not the delta.

`can_manage` comes back WITH the list, resolved by the same rule the
archive endpoint enforces - the app does that deliberately so the control a
UI renders and the permission the endpoint applies cannot drift. A
rebuilder without it has to guess which rows are removable.

LITERAL PATH: registered before `deals_router` so `/deals/{deal_id}` cannot
read "close-reasons" as a deal id.

Add a close reason.

ENTRY GATE: `_REASON_MUTATE_PERMISSIONS`, the SAME route dependency the app
declares - wider than the manager tier (a rep may extend the list inline
while closing their own deal) but NOT open to org members with no deal
access. `can_manage` is still resolved for the handler; `may_seed` is now
enforced by the route gate rather than discarded.

delete.description:
Archive a close reason.

ENTRY GATE: `_REASON_MUTATE_PERMISSIONS`, the SAME route dependency the app
declares. Beyond the gate the decision is CREATOR OR MANAGER, not

rep's typo permanent and org-wide, in a list" a rep is expected to extend

remove.

model call or nothing. 400 when the org's `ai_briefs` switch is off, 502
when the model could not answer.

FAIL-SOFT: with the org's `ai_briefs` switch off it returns a canned answer
and HTTP 200, not an error. A caller that needs to know whether it got a
real answer should look at the payload, not the status code.

SPENDS CREDITS. Transcribe a voice memo and turn it into desk actions.

Multipart, like the app. The memo is transcribed, its actions extracted by
a model, and the result materialised as cards and tasks for this rep - the
credits are charged per memo. 400 on an empty upload, 413 over 5 MB, 403
when `deal_id` names a deal this rep may not write, 502 when transcription
or extraction failed (nothing is materialised then).

SPENDS CREDITS. Gather fresh evidence and write a NEW plan version.

Rep-pressed only; nothing automatic reaches this. It rides the org's
existing `account_plan_replan` switch, the per-account 24-hour cooldown and
the org's daily cap, and a press cannot bypass any of them.

A refusal from a gate is a 409 and costs NOTHING. A failure after the model
answered may already have been charged, and says so in the response. There
is no retry anywhere in this path, so a 409 means stop rather than try
again.

Resolve the dialable number for one contact, after the opt-out check.

ALWAYS 200. "No number on file" and "this person opted out" are ordinary
answers carried in the payload as `is_dialable: false` with a reason, not
errors - a caller that treats a non-200 as the only failure mode will dial
people who asked not to be called.

POST rather than GET is the app's choice: it consults the suppression
ledger, and pressing Call is an intent to contact someone, which should not
be firable by a prefetch. It resolves and writes nothing, which is why it
is tiered a READ.

Resolve the dialable number for a CARD, after the opt-out check.

Same always-200 contract as the contact route above. The difference is
ownership: this one checks the card belongs to the calling rep, because a
card names a specific person to call.

Who this card replies TO, and which mailbox it replies FROM.

ALWAYS 200: no address on file, no authorised mailbox and an opt-out all
come back as `is_sendable: false` with a reason.

Resolving is not sending, and this route does neither a write nor a send.
Call `/desk/decisions/{id}/send-reply` for that - it re-runs the opt-out
check, because this answer is only as fresh as the moment it was asked.

Which number this card texts, and which number it texts FROM.

Always 200, same as the other two targets. Resolves; never sends.

SENDS AN EMAIL to a real person, then resolves the card.

Not idempotent, and it cannot be: the inbox send path carries no request
id and no dedupe key. What protects a caller instead is the CARD: it is
claimed before the send, guarded on still being pending, so only one
request can win and a second gets a 409 having sent nothing.

A retry after a timeout is therefore safe in the usual case and silent in
one: a crash between the claim and the send leaves a resolved card whose
mail never went. That is deliberate - recoverable by a human, unlike a
duplicate email, which cannot be recalled.

The opt-out check runs AGAIN here. `reply-target` already asked, but that
answer is as old as the caller's editing session and a STOP that arrived
meanwhile must not be sent through.

SENDS A TEXT MESSAGE to a real phone, then resolves the card.

Carrier spend, and unrecallable once gone. Same claim-then-send ordering
and the same re-run of the opt-out check as `send-reply` - see that
docstring for why a retry is safe and where it is not.

post.description:
Create a new deal. Defaults to the org's default pipeline and first stage if not specified.

``background_tasks`` carries the ``deal.created`` event only (#16242). Like
the PATCH endpoint's stage fan-out it is injected, not a body field, so it
does not appear in the OpenAPI schema and the request contract is unchanged.
Queuing it there rather than publishing inline keeps the Redis round trip
off the caller's latency budget and makes "strictly after the commit"
structural: the task is queued only once the session context has exited,
and FastAPI attaches background tasks to the SUCCESS response, so a raise
anywhere above publishes nothing.

get.description: Get a single deal by ID.

patch.description:
Update a deal (partial update).

Contact operations run in a fixed order within the single transaction:
``remove_contact_ids`` -> ``add_contact_ids`` -> ``contact_roles``. That
order is what makes the useful combinations work:

* a contact linked by ``add_contact_ids`` in THIS request can be given a
  role by ``contact_roles`` in the same call (roles run last);
* an id in both ``remove_contact_ids`` and ``add_contact_ids`` ends up
  linked (add runs after remove), so a role for it still applies;
* an id in ``remove_contact_ids`` and ``contact_roles`` but NOT in
  ``add_contact_ids`` is unlinked by the time roles run, so it is a 422
  naming that id rather than a role written to a row that no longer
  exists.

A ``contact_roles`` entry for a contact that is neither already linked nor
being added is a 422; the whole transaction rolls back, so a partially
applied batch is not a state this endpoint can produce.

``background_tasks`` carries the ``deal.stage_changed`` fan-out only. It is
injected, not a body field, so it does not appear in the OpenAPI schema and
the request contract is unchanged (pinned by
``developer_api/tests/test_deal_stage_events.py``). Publishing there rather
than inline keeps the Redis round trip off the caller's latency budget and
makes "strictly after the commit" structural: the task is queued only after
the session context has exited, and FastAPI attaches background tasks to the
SUCCESS response, so a raise anywhere above publishes nothing.

delete.description:
Delete a deal.

THE TOMBSTONE RULE (#16242): ``deal.deleted`` has to be self-contained,
because by the time a consumer reads it the row is gone and ``deal_id``
resolves to nothing. The payload therefore comes from ``RETURNING`` on the
DELETE itself — one round trip, and no window in which a concurrent write
could change what a preceding SELECT had read. ``background_tasks`` is
injected (not a body field, so the OpenAPI schema is unchanged) for the

Withdraw an invitation before it is accepted.

Published although its counterpart `POST /invite` is not, and the

The WRITE twin, `PUT /v1/roles/users/{user_id}`, is not published. It
maps a role slug of `owner` or `admin` onto the identity provider's own
Owner/Admin and syncs it, so it can make somebody an administrator of the

A service provider is a non-employee working inside the tenant, and this

Define a new role. It grants nobody anything until it is assigned.

Two of the app's own guards run inside the handler and are not duplicated

not hold, and `_require_teams_manage` refuses `manages_role_slugs` without

This is `write` rather than `destructive` on purpose: a brand-new role is
held by no one, so creating it changes nobody's access. Editing one does -
which is why `PUT /roles/{role_id}` is tiered differently.

left out is a permission taken away from everyone who holds the role. That
is why this operation is tiered `destructive` rather than `write`: it is a
privilege change, and "re-define what the sales team may do" must not ride
along in the same grant as "rename a team".

The app refuses to edit the permissions of its locked system roles
(`admin`, `service_provider`) - stripping `roles:manage` from `admin`
would lock the organisation out with no recovery path - and refuses to
grant anything the caller does not hold. Both reach you as a 403.

leave the building. Gated on `campaigns:launch`, the same permission the
in-app route requires.

published `POST /newsletters/{id}/pause`.

Resuming alone can put mail in real inboxes: pausing reverts scheduled

``scheduled_at`` omitted/null sends immediately; a malformed

A REQUEST, not an instant state: recipients already leased by a worker are
still delivered, and the reported state stays `pausing` until the
reconciler confirms it settled. It does not lie about that, so poll
`GET .../send` rather than assuming.

Deliberately NOT gated on the launch permission. Requiring a launch right
to STOP a send would invert the safety model, and the app leaves it open
for that reason.

Restart a paused send. LAUNCH-CLASS.

This is the one send control that starts delivery again, which is why it
carries the `campaigns:launch` gate its two neighbours do not.

Abandon a send for good.

Unlike pause, there is no resuming from here: whoever has already received
the issue has received it, and nobody else will. Ungated for the same
reason pause is.

4. Rotation PRESERVES the target key's mode, so without this a `test`-mode
caller could rotate a `live` key and receive a brand-new `live` token (while
invalidating the working live key). That is the same escalation the create
route coerces away, so refuse it here rather than coerce: a rotation cannot
be silently downgraded to `test` without destroying a working live key.

get.description:
Poll the status of an enrichment job.

Resolution order:
    1. Redis ``job_state_cache`` (sub-millisecond, written by the
       waterfall worker pipeline).
    2. ``enrichment_jobs`` table in the org schema (written by every
       enrichment handler including AI). DB fallback covers two cases:
       Redis cache eviction for old waterfall jobs, AND AI jobs whose
       handler isn't wired to the cache (see ``AIEnrichmentHandler``).

Returning DB-resolved jobs also populates ``total`` / ``completed``
counters that Redis-only resolutions leave as ``None`` - so callers
polling AI jobs see progress without a separate detail call.

Delegates to ``AIEnrichmentHandler`` (the same handler the UI uses).
Unlike the waterfall endpoint - which queues an async job - this call

been processed (typical: 30-120 s for a handful of contacts on the
web-research usecase). The response therefore returns ``status="completed"``
with the final counters inline, not a queued job_id to poll.

The job_id is still returned for audit / cross-reference - polling it
via ``GET /jobs/{job_id}`` works thanks to the DB fallback on that
endpoint, but most callers will get everything they need from this
response directly.

Credits are charged up-front at the web-research baseline

additionally, so this is the only credit deduction per call.

Not a state change with a side effect - the side effect IS the point: the

Tiered `external` rather than `write` for exactly that reason.

Email the signing link again. ALSO REACHES A REAL PERSON.

Only valid while the envelope is `sent` or `viewed` - a draft has never

Cancel an envelope that is already out.

The signing link stops working, so this is the operation to reach for when

cannot be deleted at all. The audit trail is preserved.

Turn a rule in words into a run condition. SPENDS CREDITS, TOKEN-METERED.

"Only run for CEOs with no work email" becomes an expression you can put in

touch - which is how this pays for itself.

The charge is METERED ON TOKENS rather than flat: a long rule with a large
sample record costs more than a short one. Keep `sampleData` to a single
representative record.

`policy.audience_ids` and writes results onto them, repeatedly, with nobody
in the loop. That is a standing credit cost, which is why this is graded as
a spend rather than a setting.

`policy.default_field.mode` decides what happens to data the customer
already has. `replace` OVERWRITES their values with the source's.
`preserve` never does. `fill_missing` - the default - only fills blanks.
Getting this wrong is not a billing problem, it is a data-loss one.

`expected_version` is the version you READ. A stale value is rejected, so
two editors cannot silently overwrite each other's policy.

profile, so `found: false` with a null profile is the ordinary answer, not
an error - and it is deliberately indistinguishable from the corpus being
unavailable. Never present absence to a user or a model as a fact about the
company.

the organisation's own table as a side effect. That is the app's design -
somebody asking about a domain is the signal that the domain matters - and
it means this read is not perfectly side-effect-free.

balance, and the shortfall if there is one. It also returns the
`operation_id` that `unlock-rows` REQUIRES - so this call is not optional
advice, it is step one of the handshake.

Send this exact body to `unlock-rows` afterwards: the quote prices the
scope the unlock will charge for, and a different body is a different
price.

This is the most expensive operation on the Workbench and the one a script
is most likely to run by accident, because OMITTING `row_ids` UNLOCKS EVERY
LOCKED ROW IN THE TABLE. A 10,000-row table costs 10,000 credits.

`operation_id` is REQUIRED and comes from `unlock-quote`. It is what binds
the charge to a price the caller was shown, and it makes a retried unlock
idempotent rather than charging twice for the same rows. Without it the
request is refused.

Set `approved_max_credits` as well: the run refuses to exceed it, which is
the difference between a bug costing you one request and costing you a
balance.

This queries the licensed people corpus and writes the matches into a
contact table. The rows land LOCKED: the search is what this costs, and
revealing each contact's details then costs a further credit per row
through `unlock-rows`.

`max_total_people` is the real cost control - it is a hard ceiling across
every company row, not a per-company hint. `broad_search_acknowledged` must
be set to run with NO filters, because an unfiltered search returns the
widest and most expensive possible result.

put.description:
Enrich every row that arrives, automatically. STARTS ONGOING SPEND.

The PUT itself charges nothing. What it does is remove the human from the
loop: from the moment this is on, every row that lands in the table - from
an import, a webhook, a scraper or a routing rule - is enriched by the
configured AI passes WITHOUT a further API call, and each one costs.

That is why this is graded as a spend rather than an ordinary setting. It
is the single switch on this surface most likely to produce a bill nobody
asked for, so `enabled` is explicit rather than a toggle: a retried request
cannot silently turn it back on.

Read `GET /workbench/tables/{id}/enrichment-configs` first - that is the
list of passes this will start running.

table with three configured columns that is 30,000 model calls.

Set `approved_max_credits`. The run refuses to exceed it, and a credit
preflight happens before any work starts, so an over-budget request costs
nothing rather than costing until the balance runs out.

Returns 202 and a handle: the work happens in the background. The group's
`skip_existing_values` and `skip_recently_enriched` settings still apply,
so re-running is usually far cheaper than the first pass.

charges for them - nightly, forever, with nobody in the loop. `run_formula`
is local and free; `crm_import` reaches the customer's CRM.

`enabled` defaults to FALSE, so writing a schedule and starting it are two
separate acts. That is deliberate: it lets a caller define the cadence,
read it back, and only then turn it on.

handing out "read my Salesforce".

quota, and again if this table auto-enriches, because every imported row is
then a row that spends.

`provider_type` and `entity_type`. They are mirrored because the app still
accepts them, not because new code should send them.

post.description:
End a sequence for good. Enrolled contacts stop; this is not a pause.

The path drops the app's `-v2` suffix: v1 is gone, so there is nothing
left to disambiguate from on a public surface.

Archive a sequence - a soft delete.

NOT REVERSIBLE THROUGH THIS API TODAY. The app's `unarchive` endpoint is a
reserved stub that unconditionally returns 403 ("Unarchiving is not
available yet"), so it is not published here - archiving is a one-way door
for an API caller until that lands. Contact support to restore one.

A LIVE or WAITING sequence is paused first and wound down in the
background; `is_archived` blocks every worker immediately. Archiving one
that is already archived is a 400, and one mid-transition (scheduling,
pausing) is a 409, so a retry loop cannot corrupt the state machine.

Re-pull the associated list so newly-matching contacts enrol.

This is how a live sequence picks up people added to its list after it
started. It enrols real recipients, so it is a write, not a refresh.

Drive the status machine directly. PREFER THE NAMED TRANSITIONS.

`/launch`, `/pause`, `/resume`, `/terminate` and `/archive` each run the
wind-down, scheduling and event work that belongs to them. This endpoint
only SETS THE STATUS, so a sequence moved to `terminated` this way never
emits its termination event and its workers are never wound down. It is
exposed because the app exposes it and a rebuilt settings panel uses it -
not because it is the way to stop a sequence.

Proxies the same v2 run flow the app's Go-Live button uses, so enrollment,
schedule and consent checks are identical.

WHY THE PATH IS `/launch` AND NOT THE APP'S `/run/v2`
-----------------------------------------------------
Two reasons, and the second is the load-bearing one.

The `v2` suffix is noise: v1 was removed on 2026-04-21, so there is nothing
left to disambiguate from on a public surface.

`launch` rather than `run` is what gets this operation the right SCOPE.
`build_scope_policy.EXTERNAL_PATH_MARKERS` contains `/launch`, `/send` and
`/publish` - the fragments that mean "this reaches the outside world" - and
an external-tier operation resolves to the `run` ACTION, so the key needs
an explicit `sequences:run` grant rather than plain `sequences:write`. As
`/run` this endpoint classified as an ordinary write, one tier below the
identical `POST /sequences/{id}/run`, which is external. Sending real email
to real people is the definition of external, and the customer issuing a
key should be able to grant "edit my nurtures" without granting "start
sending".

get.description:
Load a sequence with its steps and channels, including RESOLVED copy. No enrollment.

Each step carries both:

- ``step_data``: the stored template, exactly as written, spintax braces and all.
- ``rendered``: the same copy with spintax collapsed to one real variant, plus
  ``total_combinations`` and up to three sample ``variants``.

Use ``rendered`` to answer "is my spintax working?". If ``variants`` differ from
each other, per-contact variation is live and each lead gets a different email.
``{{variables}}`` stay visible in ``rendered`` on purpose; they fill in at send
time from contact data, and a preview has no contact to fill them from.

``rendered`` is null for ON_DEMAND steps, whose copy the AI writes per contact
at send time rather than reading from ``step_data``.

delete.description:
Remove this sequence's LinkedIn steps AND its LinkedIn channel, atomically.

Unbinding the channel on its own leaves the LinkedIn steps with no sender,
which makes the sequence impossible to run or resume (400, and the sequence is
reverted to DRAFTED) and pauses it outright if a contact reaches the step. This
endpoint removes both halves in one transaction so that state is never created.

404, so it is safe to call across a batch. It also cleans up sequences already
stranded with orphaned LinkedIn steps.

get.description:
The AI campaign dashboard. A GET THAT CAN SPEND CREDIT.

On a cache hit it is free and instant. On a MISS - or when the cached copy
is stale and the campaign's documents have changed - it dispatches a
background job that generates the assessment with a model, and returns
`is_generating: true`. So the first call for a campaign costs money even
though it is a GET.

`ACTIVE_GET_MARKERS` exist for exactly this shape and none of them matches

polling does not re-dispatch.

post.description:
Create a new campaign from scratch — full Studio "Convert to Campaign" parity.

The original handler only inserted ``cb_campaigns``. That left two
Studio-side gaps:

1. Studio's Campaigns workbench (``frontend/features/studio/components/
   CampaignUnifiedTable.tsx``) filters ``cb_campaign_ideas`` WHERE
   ``converted_to_campaign=true`` and joins back to ``cb_campaigns`` via
   ``converted_campaign_id``. With no paired idea row, MCP-created
   campaigns were invisible in the workbench (only the direct
   ``/studio?campaignId=...`` URL worked).
2. No documents were generated, so the campaign sat in "Not Ready" state
   indefinitely. The launch flow silently produced empty sequences.

This handler now mirrors ``campaign_builder/routers/campaign_conversion.py
:convert_idea_to_campaign`` end-to-end:

* INSERT cb_campaigns (status=``copy_in_progress`` when generating, else ``draft``)
* INSERT paired cb_campaign_ideas row with ``source='mcp'``,
  ``converted_to_campaign=true``, ``converted_campaign_id=<new>``
* INSERT cb_campaign_metadata with ``total_documents`` calculated from the
  target channels
* Scaffold ``sequence`` + ``step_catalog`` stub docs (idempotent)
* Dispatch ``generate_campaign_files_from_idea.delay(...)`` to Celery

Backwards-compatible: original 7-field callers still work AND see
byte-for-byte identical behavior because ``auto_generate_documents``
defaults to ``False``. All Studio-parity behavior (paired idea row,
metadata row, Celery dispatch, status='copy_in_progress') is opt-in
via ``auto_generate_documents=True``. The MCP ``g8_gtm_create_campaign``
tool wrapper sets it to ``True`` so Daniel's GTM agent gets the fix
without affecting any other direct API caller.

post.description:
Launch a campaign through the canonical Sequencer V2 workflow.

This does two things end-to-end:

1. **Push** the campaign to the sequencer. The bridge loads the campaign's
   generated documents (email/LinkedIn/phone/SMS copy), transforms them
   into sequencer steps, and creates a new ``SeqSequence`` row with the
   campaign content attached. A ``CampaignSequenceLink`` row links the two.
2. **Run** the sequence through the same V2 workflow used by Sequencer.
   The response reports ``live`` only after synchronous initialization has
   completed, or ``scheduling`` with job details for background work.

Idempotency: re-launching a campaign that already has an active sequence
returns 409 unless ``force`` is implied via a future query-param. This is
consistent with the UI's bridge/push behaviour.

Pre-flight is mandatory. The deprecated ``validate`` parameter is accepted
only as ``true``; ``false`` is rejected before any sequence is created.

WARNING: this begins sending real outreach to real contacts.

put.description:
Attach (or detach) a saved list to a campaign as its audience.

This is the missing link in Daniel's MCP flow: ``find list → create
campaign → attach audience → launch`` was previously a dead-end because
no REST/MCP path could set ``cb_campaigns.audience_list_id`` (the FE
"Attach Audience" dialog only went through an internal route).

Idempotent — setting the same list twice is a 200, no error. Pass
``list_id=null`` to detach. The launch endpoint reads
``cb_campaigns.audience_list_id`` when enrolling contacts; without it,
launch creates a sequence with zero enrollment.

get.description:
Get campaign execution metrics — sequence status + email sent/replied counts.

Thin wrapper around the existing ``campaigns.metrics`` handler. The
handler queries ClickHouse for per-sequence event aggregates and joins
them to the campaign's linked sequences via ``cb_campaign_sequence_links``.

Read-only. Returns the same shape the handler produces. Each campaign carries
a ``metric_status`` (available | zero | stale | unknown | missing) that
reconciles the ClickHouse engagement rollup against Postgres send receipts
(``seqcontactexecutedsteps``): if analytics are unreachable the status is
``unknown`` (NOT a zero), and if send receipts prove sends the rollup has not
counted the status is ``stale``. Read ``reconciliation`` and ``measured_range``
before concluding anything about delivery — never treat a bare zero as an outage.

Get the **kitchen-sink** campaign payload in one round trip.

Includes: campaign row, attached audience list summary, ALL documents
(with content), sequence + step catalog, and linked sequencer sequences
(so the caller can tell at a glance whether the campaign has been
launched yet).

Designed for the MCP "load entire campaign for editing" path so agents
don't have to chain ``GET /campaigns/{id}`` → ``/documents`` → ``/sequence``
just to see the current state.

patch.description:
Apply a deep-update to a campaign in one round trip.

Behavior:
    - Campaign fields (name/brief/hook/etc.) update the row when present.
    - ``audience_list_id`` attaches; ``detach_audience=true`` clears it.
    - ``documents[*]`` either updates an existing doc by id, or creates a
      new doc when id is omitted (file_type + display_name required).
    - ``sequence_steps`` replaces the sequence ordering verbatim
      (same semantics as PUT /sequence).

Returns the full kitchen-sink payload (same shape as GET /full).
Backwards-compat: omitting any field is a no-op. Existing single-purpose
endpoints (PATCH /campaigns/{id}, PUT /audience, PUT /sequence, etc.)
keep working unchanged.

**Why this exists.** The company profile is the source of truth for Studio
generation. Self-serve orgs that sign up without a domain get a profile seeded
with graph8's own details, so every generated document describes the wrong
company — and the only write path was ``POST /company-profile``, an internal
JWT route absent from both the developer API and MCP. An agent could therefore
detect the problem but never fix it, and could not even read the field back to
confirm a human had fixed it.

post.description:
Regenerate Studio (Global Context) documents against a website.

**Why this exists.** Studio docs are generated once at onboarding from the
company profile's website. If that profile was wrong at the time — the common
case for self-serve orgs, which seed graph8's own profile when no domain is
given — every downstream ICP, persona, TAM and campaign is built on the wrong
company, and there was no machine path to fix it:

* the internal ``POST /global-context/generate-all`` refuses forever once the
  first pipeline completes (``409 ... Contact support to reset and regenerate``);
* ``POST /global-context/generate/{doc_type}`` has no such lock but was
  JWT-only, so an agent or API key could not call it.

This endpoint wraps the per-document path, which means it is **not** subject to
the one-shot pipeline lock and can be run whenever the source of truth changes.

intelligence analyze step first for a newly-changed domain, otherwise this
returns 404 rather than regenerating stale content.

get.description:
Get live warmup analytics for a single mailbox.

Wraps the existing ``GET /warmup/{mailbox_id}/analytics`` flow so MCP
(API-key auth) can read warmup engagement / reputation without going
through cookie-based session auth.

Behavior:
    - Looks up the mailbox in the API user's org schema. 404 if missing
      or deleted. Tenant isolation comes from the per-org schema bind,
      NOT from a row-level predicate.
    - Hits the configured warmup provider (Instantly or SmartLead) over
      HTTP — slow (~300-800ms typical). For warm bulk reads use
      ``list_mailboxes`` and check the cheap DB-level ``warmup_status``.
    - Returns ``{success, warmup_enabled, provider, analytics, warmup_settings}``
      — same shape as the internal /warmup/{id}/analytics endpoint.

Backwards-compat: this is a brand-new route. The internal
/warmup/{id}/analytics (cookie auth) is unchanged.

Historical bug (fixed 2026-05-24, same root cause as list_mailboxes
above): the previous implementation appended
``(t.org_id = :org_id OR m.created_by = :user_id)`` to the WHERE. Both
halves match zero rows in prod — ``mailboxes.team_id`` is NULL on every
row (no team pinning) and ``mailboxes.created_by`` stores email strings,
not propelauth UUIDs. Result: every warmup-analytics call 404'd even
for mailboxes that ``list_mailboxes`` happily returned. Dropping the
predicate restores parity; schema bind is the tenant boundary.

post.description:
Suggest buyable domain names around a keyword. SPENDS NOTHING.

A naming aid, not a reservation: a name returned here can still be gone by
the time you buy it, so `check-availability` remains the authority.

Can this domain be transferred in, and what would it cost? SPENDS NOTHING.

Different question from `check-availability`, which asks whether a domain
is free to REGISTER. This one asks about a domain you already own at
another registrar.

Can this domain be attached as an EXTERNAL sending domain? SPENDS NOTHING.

External means graph8 never owns or bills the registration - you keep the
domain where it is and point its DNS here. The follow-up is
`POST /provider-domains/add-external`.

get.description:
What a mailbox and its warmup cost, in credits. SPENDS NOTHING.

`credits_per_warmup_month` is the RECURRING monthly charge per mailbox
while warmup is on - the number `auto-warmup` commits you to for every
mailbox bought on a domain afterwards.

post.description:
Transfer a domain you own elsewhere into graph8. SPENDS REAL CREDITS.

This is a purchase: it pays the registrar to move the domain and extends
the registration. There is no per-key spend cap, the same as the app.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header so a retry cannot pay twice. 202 means
the transfer was accepted and is now in the registrar's hands - it
completes asynchronously and can take days. 402 if the credit hold cannot
clear, 422 if the org's plan cannot fund a purchase at all.

Get `auth_info` from your current registrar first; a wrong code fails the
transfer at the registrar AFTER the money has moved.

Abort an in-flight transfer.

Refunds are the registrar's business, not graph8's: cancelling stops the
move, it does not guarantee the transfer fee back.

Where an in-flight transfer has got to. Reads only.

POST rather than GET because that is the app's own spelling, kept so the
two surfaces describe one operation rather than two.

Re-send the transfer authorisation mail to the registrant address.

Use when the original never arrived. It reaches a real inbox, so it is not
a free retry loop - the registrar rate-limits it.

The registrar's record for this domain: expiry, nameservers, lock state.

Read-only, and live - it asks the registrar rather than returning the last
thing graph8 stored.

The DNS records an EXTERNAL domain must publish for graph8 to send from it.

Read-only. Add them at whoever hosts the domain's DNS, then confirm with
`POST /provider-domains/{domain_id}/check-propagation`.

Re-send the registrant verification mail.

ICANN suspends a domain whose registrant never verifies, which takes the
mailboxes on it down with it. Worth calling for any domain whose
verification status is not `Verified`.

Forward mail arriving at this domain to another address.

REPLACES the current forwarding configuration rather than merging into it.

delete.description: Stop forwarding this domain's mail. Mail then lands in its own mailboxes.

post.description:
How far this domain has got through managed provisioning. Reads only.

`provider_status` is the connection state; the `provider_*_uid` fields are
opaque references you may need when contacting support.

Pull this domain's current state from the provisioning backend and store it.

Writes: graph8's copy is replaced with what the provider says. Use it when
`provider-status` looks stale against reality.

Mint a fresh set of nameservers for this domain.

For a domain whose propagation window expired or whose nameservers were
changed elsewhere. It issues NEW values - you still have to apply them,
with `set-nameservers` for a graph8-registered domain or at your own DNS
host for an external one.

Point this domain's nameservers at the managed mail backend, at the registrar.

Only meaningful for a domain graph8 registered or transferred in. DNS
propagation is not instant; confirm with `check-propagation`.

Live provisioning step and last error for up to 50 mailboxes. Reads only.

Best-effort by design: a mailbox with no live provisioning run - finished,
never started, or aged out - comes back `null` rather than erroring, so
poll this and fall back to the mailbox's own status.

Re-check one mailbox's provisioning with the provider, and record the answer.

Not a pure read: a mailbox the provider now reports as ready is flipped to
active here, which is what makes it usable for sending.

Set the avatar recipients see on mail from this mailbox.

`profile_picture` must be a URL the provider can fetch; it is downloaded
server-side, not proxied through graph8.

Replace a provider mailbox's password.

Anything already signed in with the old password - including graph8's own
sending connection until it re-reads the mailbox - stops working
immediately. The new password is write-only and is never returned by this
or any other endpoint.

Delete a mailbox at the provider. NOT REVERSIBLE.

The mailbox stops existing upstream and its mail goes with it. Different
from `DELETE /mailboxes/{mailbox_id}`, which removes graph8's record of a
mailbox and leaves the provider's copy alone. A domain's admin mailbox
cannot be deleted - it is what manages the domain.

To stop paying for a purchased mailbox without destroying it, use
`POST /mailboxes/{mailbox_id}/request-cancellation` instead.

Turn automatic warmup enrolment on or off for this domain. ON COMMITS SPEND.

ON: every mailbox bought on this domain from now on is enrolled in warmup
automatically, and warmup is a RECURRING monthly credit charge per mailbox
(`GET /provider-domains/pricing` has the figure). It is the default.

OFF: new mailboxes are not enrolled and not billed for warmup. It does NOT
stop warmup already running on existing mailboxes - use
`POST /warmup/{mailbox_id}/disable` for that - and it does not affect
warmup you start by hand.

dashboard tiles show.

patch.description:
CHANGE WHO MAY READ THE RECORDING OF THIS MEETING.

`private` HIDES the transcript from everyone except the meeting's
participants. `normal` EXPOSES it to the organisation again - and a
transcript that has been read cannot be un-read, so going back to `normal`
is not a reversible edit in any sense that matters.

Only a PARTICIPANT may change it; anyone else gets a 403. Classified
`destructive`, so it needs `inbox:delete` rather than riding along with
`inbox:write` - a key that triages the inbox should not also be able to
publish a private recording.

`sensitivity` is REQUIRED here. The app defaults a missing key to
`normal`, which is the exposing direction, so this contract refuses to
guess.

Platform- and state-dependent: a live Google Search campaign accepts a

Gated on `ads:launch` rather than `ads:view`, as the app gates it: it
describes the money controls, and the app treats that whole surface as one
permission.

post.description:
Re-attempt a launch that failed or stalled.

THIS SPENDS THE CUSTOMER'S ADVERTISING BUDGET when it succeeds - the
campaign goes live on the platform with the budget it was created with.
Like the launch, a refusal comes back as a 200 whose body `status` is
`error` - read it. Check `GET /ad-campaigns/{campaign_id}` first: a
campaign that is already live does not need this, and retrying one whose
creative was rejected will fail the same way until the creative changes.

Re-read one campaign's review state from its platform.

Policy review is ASYNCHRONOUS: a creative can be auto-rejected minutes
after the platform accepted the campaign, and graph8's copy still says it
launched. This promotes the platform's real state - `REJECTED`,
`NEEDS_REVIEW` - into it. A live platform read; nothing is changed on the
platform.

delete.description:
Stop and remove a campaign.

THIS STOPS A LIVE CAMPAIGN ON THE PLATFORM FIRST, then removes graph8's
row. There is no undo: the platform-side removal is the platform's, and the
campaign's history goes with the local row.

502 - not 404 - when the platform refuses the removal, because the campaign
is then still LIVE AND SPENDING and reporting success would be the worst
possible answer.

put.description:
Edit a LIVE campaign: budget, schedule, creative, keywords, ad copy,
targeting, pause or resume.

Omitted fields are left alone; an unknown field is a 422 (the app's model
forbids extras, so a typo cannot silently do nothing). Read
`GET /ad-campaigns/{campaign_id}/editable` first - the platform refuses
some changes on some campaign types and states.

A 200 is NOT blanket success: the response `status` is `partial` whenever
any single change failed, and `changes[]` says which.

post.description:

The app's own checks run unchanged: 10 MB, and the file's MAGIC BYTES decide
its type rather than its name or declared content type. SVG is refused with
a 422 - no ad platform accepts it; rasterise first.

Launch a paid campaign on the platform, targeting this sync's audience.

THIS SPENDS THE CUSTOMER'S ADVERTISING BUDGET. The campaign goes live with
`daily_budget` in `currency` from `start_date`, and the platform starts
charging as soon as it serves. `spend_cap` and `auto_pause_at` are the
guard rails; set them. Upload the creative first with
`POST /ad-campaigns/images`.

READ `status` IN THE BODY. The app answers a refused launch (campaign not
found, the platform rejecting it) with a 200 whose `status` is `error`, and
this route passes that through unchanged rather than guessing an HTTP code
for it. A launch can also partly succeed - the platform accepts the campaign
and then rejects a creative in review - so follow up with
`POST /ad-campaigns/{campaign_id}/status-refresh`.

delete.description:
Permanently stop one ad.

Archive, not hard-delete: Google's remove and LinkedIn's archive are both
one-way, so the ad is retained with ``status="archived"`` and the spend it
already incurred stays attributable. Refuses on a campaign's last remaining
ad — pause or delete the campaign instead of leaving it serving nothing.

post.description:

Returns ``status="partial"`` when any individual ad failed, with per-ad

success — one creative rejected on policy does not stop its siblings.

Changes what the campaign's budget is spent on, so this needs ``ads:run``.
A LinkedIn creative still in policy review cannot be paused; that returns a
400 with an actionable message rather than a raw platform error.

post.description:
Structured search across one of the whitelisted mashup OpenSearch indices.

Use this when the LLM needs to look up enriched person / company records
by attribute (domain, industry, country, hem). For the hot HEM-or-IP
resolve path, prefer ``/opensearch/resolve`` — it's a single round trip
and friendlier to cache. Contact/company mashup searches automatically
apply the authenticated organization's deliverability protection policy.

Bulk HEM -> CONTACT_ID or IP -> COMPANY_ID resolution.

Backed by the existing ``MashupService`` which already batches the OpenSearch
request in chunks of 10k. Returns a dense ``{input: matched_id | null}``
mapping so the caller can iterate the inputs without re-querying for misses.

Exact match count for one of the whitelisted mashup indices.

Same ``index`` + ``filters`` shape as ``/opensearch/search`` but returns
only the count via the native OpenSearch ``_count`` API, so it is NOT
capped at the 10000 ``track_total_hits`` ceiling that ``/search``'s
``total`` saturates at. This is the right call for TAM cell-sizing.

Note: ``mashup_companies`` and ``mashup_contacts`` are the same physical,
contact-grained index — a count over ``mashup_companies`` counts contact
rows, not unique companies. For a unique-company total use
``/opensearch/aggregate`` with ``uniqExact`` on ``COMPANY_ID``. Mashup
counts automatically apply the organization's deliverability policy.

Generic, allowlist-bounded GROUP BY over a whitelisted mashup index.

Translates ``group_by`` into nested OpenSearch ``terms`` aggregations with
metric sub-aggs, then applies ``having`` / ``sort`` / ``limit`` to the
flattened groups. This is the matrix-walk primitive for TAM design (e.g.
count companies by NAICS x state x employee band in one call).

Guardrails: group_by depth is capped at 3, per-level bucket size tapers by
depth (``_AGG_TERMS_SIZE_BY_DEPTH``), the agg list is capped at 10, and
returned groups at ``limit`` (<=1000). Counts from ``terms`` /
``cardinality`` are APPROXIMATE on a sharded index. Since
``mashup_companies``/``mashup_contacts`` share one contact-grained index,
use ``uniqExact`` on ``COMPANY_ID`` for true unique-company counts. Mashup
aggregations automatically apply the organization's deliverability policy.

Enrich UP_IDs / HEMs / domains against the ClickHouse Cloud mashup tables.

Use this for bulk enrichment workflows where the agent already has a
primary key (UP_ID from ``g8_opensearch_resolve_ids``, a HEM from a
visitor row, or a company domain from CRM). For free-form attribute
search prefer ``g8_opensearch_search`` against ``mashup_contacts``.

Per-org visitor + intent analytics from ch3.

The database name is always derived from the authenticated user's
``organization.id`` (lower-cased) — the request body never carries
an org_id. The agent cannot reach another org's data even if it
tries.

post.description:
Buy a number from Twilio or Telnyx. THIS SPENDS CREDITS AND REAL MONEY.

Charged on PURCHASE, not on first use: the handler holds credits, buys the
number from the carrier, stores it, registers it with the voice platform
and only then converts the hold to a charge. A number bought and never
dialled has still cost.

Not idempotent by number - buy the same number twice and the second call
is a 409 rather than a second charge, but a retry after a timeout you
cannot see the outcome of may have already succeeded. Send an
`Idempotency-Key` header; every POST on this API honours it.

`402` means insufficient credits and is the one failure worth handling
distinctly - the number was not bought and nothing was charged.

Give a number back to the carrier. IRREVERSIBLE.

The number returns to the provider's pool and can be bought by anyone,
including a competitor. Inbound calls and messages to it stop reaching
this organisation immediately; there is no grace period and no undo.

Order matters and is not transactional: the carrier release happens first,
then voice deregistration (best-effort), then the local record. A failure
after the carrier release leaves the number gone but the record behind -
which is why this returns the outcome rather than a bare 204.

patch.description:
Move a number to a different person, and tell voice about it.

Not a label: the assignee drives inbound ring targeting, missed-call
notification and which numbers appear in that person's outbound caller-ID
rotation pool.

ADMIN-ONLY through this API. The app also accepts the number's current
assignee or its creator, but an API key is an ORGANISATION credential with
no `user_id`, so it can never be either - leaving it to fall through to the
role check is what made this route 403 for every key before the role was
supplied.

patch.summary: Switch a number between dialer and voice AI
patch.description:
Change what a number is for, and re-provision it to match.

This reaches the voice platform: the LiveKit trunks and the carrier
`voice_url` are re-pointed so inbound calls arrive where the new capability
says they should. A number is briefly answering neither while that happens.

The two flags are not independent. `dialer` set with `voice` unset means
dialer; every other combination means voice AI - which is the app's own
derivation, mirrored rather than reinvented.

Admin-only for the same reason as `update-assignee`.

post.summary: Save A2P brand and campaign details
post.description:
Save the brand and campaign details WITHOUT submitting them.

Nothing reaches a carrier and nothing is charged. This is the draft step -
call it as often as you like, then submit once with `/a2p/register`.

The save REPLACES what was there rather than merging, so send the whole
object each time.

Submit the organisation to the US carrier registry. THIS REACHES A
THIRD PARTY AND CARRIES CARRIER FEES.

Saves the inputs, then starts a durable registration saga and returns its
`workflow_id` immediately - registration takes days, not seconds, and the
carriers can reject it. Without an approved registration, US carriers
filter application-to-person SMS from these numbers, so this is not
optional for messaging.

IDEMPOTENT PER ORGANISATION: the workflow id is derived from the org, so a
second call while one is running is a no-op rather than a second
submission. Call `/a2p/inputs` first if you only want to save a draft.

post.summary: Re-run A2P registration for stuck numbers
post.description:
Re-attach this organisation's pending or failed numbers to its A2P
messaging service.

The repair step, not the registration step. A worker already does this
every six hours; this is how to stop waiting for it after fixing whatever
made a number fail. It re-runs against numbers whose status is pending or
failed and leaves registered ones alone, so it is safe to call repeatedly.

Tiered as an ordinary write rather than a spend: it reconciles state the
`/a2p/register` submission already paid for and starts no new registration.

`503` means the messaging service is not configured for this environment,
which is a deployment fact rather than anything the caller did wrong.

post.summary: Register a number with the voice platform
post.description:
Wire an already-owned number into the voice platform.

BUYS NOTHING. Voice calls this operation `purchase` and it is published
here as `provision` deliberately: it creates SIP trunks and dispatch rules
for a number you already hold, while `POST /phone-numbers/purchase` is the
one that spends credits and buys a DID. Two operations both called
"purchase", one of which takes money and one of which does not, is not a
distinction to leave to a docstring.

IDEMPOTENT: a number already registered comes back as success rather than
an error, and an unverified Telnyx number has its caller-ID verification
re-queued on the way through.

Reach for this to repair a purchase whose voice half failed, or to adopt a
number bought outside graph8. `org_id` is taken from the API key.

delete.summary: Deregister a number from the voice platform
delete.description:
Tear down a number's SIP trunks, dispatch rules and carrier routing.

DOES NOT RELEASE THE NUMBER. The organisation still owns it and is still
billed for it by the carrier - it simply stops being answerable. To give it
back, use `POST /phone-numbers/release`, which does this and the carrier
release and the local record.

Voice's own handler identifies the number by value with no tenant check, so
this route first asserts the caller's organisation owns it. A number that
exists in voice but was never recorded against this organisation is a 404.

post.summary: Verify a Telnyx number as a caller ID
post.description:
Start caller-ID verification for a Telnyx number.

ONLY Telnyx numbers need this, and asking for a Twilio one is a 400 rather
than a silent success - Twilio DIDs are valid callers by construction and
have no verification record at all.

Verification takes minutes, so this returns immediately with either
`already_verified` or `verification_started`; poll
`GET /voice/dialer/numbers` and read `caller_id_verified`. An unverified
Telnyx number is a real number that simply cannot be dialled FROM, which is
why it is kept out of the rotation pool rather than failing mid-session.

Same ownership check as the delete above, for the same reason: voice looks
the number up by bare value.

patch.summary: Change what answers a number's inbound calls
patch.description:
Retype a number between AI answering, SDR answering and the dialer.

NOT a label change, and not free. Moving to `dialer` DESTROYS the LiveKit
dispatch rule and both SIP trunks and repoints the carrier webhook; moving
away from it builds them again. The number answers nothing in between, and
the teardown is best-effort - a failed trunk delete is logged and the
retype continues.

Retyping to the mode it is already in is a no-op, so this is safe to retry.

Voice compares the number's own `org_id` against the one sent, and this
route sends the API key's - so another organisation's number is a 404
rather than a silent retype.

Point a number's voice-side assignment at someone else.

The VOICE half of `PATCH /phone-numbers/update-assignee`, which does this
and updates the CDP record. Published separately because the app's
propagation to voice is best-effort and only logs a warning when it fails -
so the two records can disagree, and this is the way to reconcile them
without re-running the whole reassignment.

Sending `assigned_to: ""` clears the assignment. Assigning a WORK number
also creates the person's phone-directory row, which is what makes them
findable by name to the receptionist.

delete.description:
Clear today's outbound call counters for every number in this
organisation.

THIS REMOVES A CAP, it does not report on one. Each caller ID has a daily
outbound limit (40 for US numbers, 60 international) that exists to keep
carriers from flagging the number; resetting the counter lets those numbers
dial past the limit they have already reached today.

ADMIN-ONLY, and deliberately stricter than voice, which leaves this route
ungated as an internal operations endpoint with no end-user caller. A
customer-facing key that can quietly lift a carrier-reputation control is
not something to publish on the same grant as renaming a number. Machine
keys are refused outright.

Counters reset on their own at midnight US Eastern. `deleted` is how many
counter keys were actually cleared - zero is a normal answer for an
organisation that has not dialled today.

get.description:
Who picks up when this number is called.

A number lives on the company profile as free text while the agent that
answers it is bound on that agent's identity, so the link is not readable
from either side alone. This resolves it.

READ-ONLY by design, and the design is load-bearing: resolving a route for
real marks directory members as engaged, so this deliberately does not.

post.summary: Clone an agent, or instantiate one from a template
post.description:
Copy an agent's whole configuration under a new name.

Persona, identity and knowledge attachments come across. This is one call
where `POST /voice/agents` plus a dozen field copies would be several, and
it is how a template becomes a working agent.

NOT a link: the copy is independent, so later edits to the source do not
reach it.

`source_agent_id` is resolved WITHIN the caller's org, so a template id
from another tenant simply is not found.

post.summary: Save an agent as a reusable template
post.description:
Turn a working agent into a starting point for new ones.

The template is a SNAPSHOT: later changes to the agent do not flow into
it, and instantiating the template with `POST /voice/agents/clone` does
not link back.

post.summary: Record a conversation into an agent's memory of a contact
post.description:
Teach an agent what was said, so the next call is not the first one.

This is how a conversation that happened somewhere ELSE - your own product,
a human rep, another channel - becomes context the agent has. Calls the
agent places itself are recorded already; this route exists for everything
it did not witness.

Written to two places by voice: a durable interaction row and the vector
memory retrieval reads. There is no delete for a memory on this surface.

The agent is named in the PATH for a readable URL. Voice's own handler
scopes the write by `(org_id, contact_id)`, so the memory attaches to the
contact within the caller's org either way.

post.summary: Give an agent skills it can use
post.description:
Attach one or more skills. ADDITIVE, not a replace.

This WIDENS WHAT THE AGENT CAN DO mid-conversation: a skill attached here
is one the agent may decide to run on a live call, including one that
calls an external API. Attach deliberately, and read
`GET /skills/{action_id}` first if you did not author it.

Skills are resolved within the caller's org, so an id from another tenant
is not found.

get.description:
SPENDS NOTHING. Every skill attached to the agent, with its full
configuration - the list `POST /voice/agents/{agent_id}/skills` adds to.

delete.summary: Take a skill away from an agent
delete.description:
Breaks the LINK only - the skill itself survives and other agents keep it.

The narrow way to stop an agent doing one thing without editing the skill
everyone else is using.

post.summary: Extract a LinkedIn profile to seed a twin
post.description:
SPENDS CREDITS. Enriches a LinkedIn profile URL into the headline,
current position, employment history and education a twin is seeded
from. Reaches a paid enrichment provider on your behalf, so it is tiered
`billable`.

Voice binds `linkedin_url` as a FORM field; the JSON body here is
re-encoded as form data. Voice answers `{"success": false, "error": ...}`
with a 200 when the profile cannot be extracted - read `success`.

A two-segment LITERAL under `/voice/twins`, declared before the
`/twins/{agent_id}` routes; `test_voice_stage2_api.py` proves it resolves
and that `/twins/<id>` still reaches its shipped handler.

get.description:
A twin is an agent modelled on a specific person.

It shares the agent id space with `/voice/agents` - a twin IS an agent with
`entity_type: "twin"` - so the same id works on both. This route returns
the twin-shaped view, including the persona sliders and writing-style
references the agent view does not carry.

delete.description:
Delete the twin. NOT REVERSIBLE.

Published beside `DELETE /voice/agents/{agent_id}` rather than instead of
it: both remove the same underlying row, and this one is here so a caller
working against `/voice/twins` does not have to know that.

put.summary: Edit a twin, optionally with a new writing-style document
put.description:
SPENDS NOTHING beyond storage. Partial update: only the fields sent
change. Multipart because voice binds every field as a form field so the
optional writing-style document can travel with them. 404 when the twin
is not this organisation's.

post.description:
Register a Model Context Protocol server agents can call tools on.

`transport_type` decides which other field is required: `sse` needs
`connection_url`, `stdio` needs `command`. It is closed to those two here.

`env_vars` IS A SECRET FIELD. It is write-only by convention on this
surface - the read routes return the server's tools, not its environment -
and anything put here is available to the process voice starts.

`org_id` is not in the body. Voice's own model requires it; it is supplied
from the key, so a caller cannot register a server into another tenant.

put.description:
Partial update. Omitted fields are untouched.

`enabled: false` is the safe way to stop agents using a server: the
configuration survives and the tools stop being offered.

delete.description:
Remove the server and its stored credentials. NOT REVERSIBLE.

Any agent configured to use its tools loses them. To stop the tools
temporarily, update the server with `enabled: false` instead.

get.summary: Last known tool list for an MCP server
get.description:
Read the stored tool list WITHOUT contacting the server.

This is the one to call in a loop: the live route beside it opens a
connection to a third party every time. The two paths differ in LENGTH
rather than in shape, so neither can shadow the other whichever order they
take - `/tools/cached` has a segment `/tools` cannot match.

get.summary: Live tool list from an MCP server
get.description:
Ask the MCP server itself what tools it offers.

THIS REACHES OUTSIDE GRAPH8. The server is one the customer configured, and
the connection is made by our infrastructure on their behalf - the same
reasoning that put `POST /skills/{action_id}/execute` in the `external`
tier. It is an explicit rule in `build_scope_policy.py::classify`, because
a GET otherwise derives `read` unconditionally and this one is not free of
side effects: it can hang on an unreachable server, and `refresh=true`
overwrites the cache the route beside it serves.

Use `/tools/cached` for anything routine.

post.description:
Saving a case RUNS NOTHING. Only `POST .../test-runs` runs the skill.

That separation is the point: building a suite is free, and executing it
is the operation that costs.

put.description:
PARTIAL update despite the verb - voice exposes it as a PUT.

Omitted fields are untouched; an explicit `null` CLEARS the field. Those
are different instructions and only the second one is destructive.

delete.description:
The case goes; its HISTORICAL RUNS SURVIVE, still carrying its id.

So a deleted case leaves readable history rather than orphaning it - past
runs in `GET .../test-runs` keep working.

post.summary: Run every saved test case against a skill
post.description:
RUNS THE SKILL, ONCE PER SAVED CASE. This has real side effects.

For an `llm` skill that is a model call per case. For an `api` skill it is
an outbound HTTP request per case, to the endpoint the skill is configured
with, made AS THE PLATFORM - so a skill that writes somewhere will write
there again, with the fixture's data.

Every case is pinned to ONE version of the skill, so the result is a
regression answer rather than a mix of versions.

Tiered `external` by an explicit rule, for the same reason
`POST /skills/{action_id}/execute` is: it reaches outside graph8 on the
customer's behalf, and nothing in the path name says so.

"Re-run all failed", in one call. EVERY NODE RUNS AGAIN.

Not a resume: a restart begins at the start, so nodes that already
succeeded run a second time - including anything that sent a message,
called an API or spent credits the first time.

Voice applies a 60-second idempotency window to this route, so an
accidental double-submit inside that window does not double-run the batch.

bare string and only its scheduler notices an unknown one, so an invented
value there produces a source that quietly never re-crawls.

patch.summary: Pause, resume, or stop a parallel-dialer session
patch.description:
Lifecycle hook for a dialer session.

- ``PAUSED`` pauses an active session.
- ``COMPLETED`` ends the session (one-way; reopen requires the
  voice frontend's manual-dial flow).

To RESUME a paused session use ``POST /voice/dialer/sessions/{id}/resume``
— the voice service rejects a PATCH to ``ACTIVE`` (the resume flow is a
fresh start-session call), so ``ACTIVE`` is rejected here with a 422 that
points at the correct endpoint rather than forwarding an opaque 400.

``FAILED`` is reserved for system use and is rejected here.

post.summary: Resume a paused parallel-dialer session by auto-fetching next batch
post.description:
Resume a PAUSED parallel-dialer session.

The voice service's ``PATCH /sessions/{id}/status`` rejects
``ACTIVE`` - the real resume flow is to call ``start-session`` again
with the existing ``session_id`` and a fresh batch of contacts. This
route does the lookup + filtering + forwarding in one shot so an MCP
caller only has to supply the session id (and optionally a batch
size).

Steps performed server-side:

1. Fetch the session via ``GET /api/parallel-calls/sessions``
   (filtered to the caller's org). Voice has no per-id GET, so we
   page with ``page_size=200`` and find the row.
2. Verify the session belongs to the caller's org and is in the
   ``PAUSED`` state. ACTIVE / COMPLETED sessions return 422.
3. Read ``list_id`` and the ``list_offset`` cursor from
   ``session_metadata``. Sessions created without a ``list_id``
   (ad-hoc / campaign-mode) cannot be resumed via this route and
   return 422.
4. Page contacts out of the source list starting at the cursor,
   skipping rows already in ``session.contact_ids`` and rows that
   have no usable phone field.
5. Forward up to ``max_contacts`` rows to voice's
   ``/api/parallel-calls/start-session`` with the existing
   ``session_id``. Voice de-duplicates active calls within the
   session and auto-promotes status to ACTIVE on success.

The ``list_offset`` we send back to voice is advanced by the total
number of rows we read from the list (called + skipped + dialed) so
a future resume picks up where we left off, not where the previous
pause cursor sat.

``status="empty"`` indicates the call row exists but the transcript

The voice service is org-scoped server-side: we forward the caller's

Summary rows do NOT include the transcript blob (5-50 KB each).
Use ``has_transcript`` to decide whether to fetch the full
transcript via ``GET /voice/dialer/calls/{room_name}/transcript``.

Org isolation is enforced server-side by the voice route: the org id
on the API key is forwarded as a required query param, so a call row
from another tenant cannot leak into the response.

Create a new voice agent or twin bound to the caller's org.

identifier ``POST /voice/dialer/sessions`` uses for ``user_email``) -

put.description:
Partially update an agent. Only fields present in the body change.

``persona`` / ``identity`` / ``knowledge`` are component-level
replacements, not deep merges - matching voice's own update semantics
(send the field's full sub-object to change any part of it). org_id
is pinned server-side; a cross-org agent_id 404s the same as GET.

delete.description:

and parent settings row all go with it (voice's own cascade, not
something this proxy orchestrates). Requires the ``voice:write``
scope explicitly - see ``require_voice_agent_delete`` above for why
this is self-gated rather than driving a new ``voice:delete`` scope.

org_id is pinned server-side; voice filters by ``(org_id, agent_id)``
so a cross-org agent_id 404s the same as GET/PUT.

post.summary: Dispatch one ad-hoc AI-agent call to a raw number
post.description:
Dispatch a single AI-agent call to an arbitrary number right now.

No dialer session or contact list required - this wraps voice's
``POST /api/call/start`` (`voice/graph8_livekit/routers/call.py:19`),
the one-off "call this number" primitive that previously had no public
surface at all. Places a REAL call and is billable upstream (voice
checks the org's subscription and concurrent-call cap before
dispatching). Send an ``Idempotency-Key`` header to make a retry
safe - every POST on this API already honors it via the app-wide
``IdempotencyMiddleware``, so no extra field is needed here.

Org is pinned server-side; phone numbers are normalized to E.164 by
voice itself (a malformed number 400s with an actionable message).

get.description:

custom ones, and how many of the ``custom_limit`` are used.

post.description:
Create an org-level custom disposition (max 10 per org).

Voice enforces the cap, the preset color palette, and case-insensitive

patch.description:
Edit a custom disposition. Only supplied fields change.

``is_connected`` is locked by voice once any call already references
the disposition (would retroactively re-classify historical calls) -
that 409 is forwarded as-is. A disposition belonging to another org
404s (voice's ``_load_disposition_for_org`` checks the stored row's
org against ``X-Org-Id`` before allowing the edit).

post.description:
CONTACTS NOBODY. Creates a DRAFT session and dials no one.

The safe first step: it resolves the list or sequence, snapshots the
filter, and stops. `POST /dialer/sessions/{id}/next-batch` is what turns a
draft into ringing telephones.

Not idempotent in the way it looks: voice REUSES a live session for the
same list rather than creating a second one, so calling this twice does
not double-dial - it returns the existing session. `from_phone` is
optional here and enforced at dial time.

*** CALLS REAL PEOPLE. *** This is the operation that dials.

Voice's own words for this handler are "the one-and-only dial path for
BE-owned queue sessions" (`dialer_sessions.py:2272`). It picks the next
contacts off the queue and places outbound calls to them, transitioning
the session DRAFT -> ACTIVE or PAUSED -> ACTIVE on the way.

`parallel_count` is HOW MANY PEOPLE ARE CALLED AT ONCE. Sending it with a
session configured for one is how a power-dial becomes a parallel dial.

Each attempt reserves credits and each connected minute charges more, so
this both spends money and reaches strangers. It is tiered `external`
rather than `write` for exactly that reason: "dial the next twenty people"
must not be grantable by the same scope as "rename a session".

`filter_spec` sent here CHANGES WHO IS ELIGIBLE before the batch is
picked. It is not a display filter.

CONTACTS NOBODY NEW. Ends a call that is already up.

This is the STOP button, not a dial. It gates on `voice:dialer:control`
rather than the create permission on purpose: hanging up is the action you
want an operator to be able to take without also being able to start a
session.

The completion record is written by Twilio's status webhook afterwards, so
the disposition and duration appear a moment later, not in this response.

*** REACHES A REAL PERSON. *** Leaves a voicemail on their phone.

The recording is played in the rep's CLONED VOICE and the call is then
hung up with disposition `voicemail`. The person hears it; there is no
undo, and a wrong `call_id` leaves the message on the wrong stranger's
phone.

Tiered `external`, not `write`: it reaches a human outside graph8.

CONTACTS NOBODY. Marks a contact so the queue stops offering them.

Queue bookkeeping. Reversible with `unskip-contact`, which is why this is
an ordinary `write` and not a destructive tier.

CONTACTS NOBODY. Puts a skipped contact back in the queue.

It does NOT call them - it only makes them eligible again, so the next
`next-batch` may.

CONTACTS NOBODY - but it SPENDS. Synthesises voicemail audio in advance.

Text-to-speech is generated per contact and cached so the audio is ready
before a rep clicks Start Dialing. No phone rings and no one hears
anything, but it is real generation work per contact, which is why it is
tiered `billable` rather than a plain `write`.

Returns immediately - the work is fired in the background. Duplicates are
no-ops (Redis in-flight lock plus a per-contact cache). Voice caps the
batch at 20 and so does this contract.

CONTACTS NOBODY NEW. Mutes the rep on a call already in progress.

`muted` is explicit rather than a toggle, so a retried request is
idempotent instead of un-muting someone mid-sentence.

get.description:
CONTACTS NOBODY - but the RESPONSE CAN. Mints a softphone credential.

Returns a short-lived (1 hour) Twilio access token carrying a VoiceGrant,
for a browser running the Twilio Voice SDK. Whoever holds it can register a
device and place and receive calls as `sdr_{user_id}_{org}` until it
expires. TREAT THE RESPONSE AS A SECRET: it is a bearer credential, not a
description of one.

That is why this is the one GET on this router tiered `external` instead of
`read`, and why it gates on `voice:calls:place` rather than a read
permission - a read-only key must not be able to mint the ability to dial.

`user_id` is REQUIRED here although voice defaults it. An organisation API
key has no user of its own, and defaulting would mint a credential for an
identity nobody named. The organisation half of the identity is always the
key's own and cannot be supplied.

parameters.name: user_id

post.description:
CONTACTS NOBODY. Reads a page of the session's contact grid.

A POST because the filter and sort specification is too large for a query
string, not because it changes anything - it mutates nothing and dials
nobody. Tiered `read` by an explicit rule for that reason, so a read-only
key can page through a queue.

patch.description:
CONTACTS NOBODY DIRECTLY - but it decides WHO IS CALLED NEXT.

The filter is the queue's eligibility rule, not a view. Widening it on a
running session adds people who will then be dialed by the next
`next-batch`; narrowing it removes people mid-campaign. No call is placed
by this request itself.

CONTACTS NOBODY. Sets which meeting type a booking on this session creates.

Null clears the selection and falls back to the org default.

CONTACTS NOBODY. Hides columns in the rep's grid. Display only.

PUT semantics: the list REPLACES whatever was hidden before, so send the
whole set rather than the delta. Hiding a field does not remove the data.

get.description: CONTACTS NOBODY. How much of the queue is left, and what has been worked.

CONTACTS NOBODY. The telephony provider's assurance receipt for this org.

Declared BEFORE `/sessions/{session_id}/queue-stats` would be a concern if
the two overlapped; they do not - `assurance/provider-receipt` and
`{session_id}/queue-stats` differ in their second segment, so neither can
swallow the other. The org is the key's own and is not a parameter.

post.description:
CONTACTS NOBODY. Creates a PAUSED parallel session.

The session exists and is configured, and not one telephone rings. This is
the safe half of the pair - `POST /dialer/parallel-calls/sessions/start`
is the half that dials.

Published as a POST to the collection precisely because that is what a
customer will reach for first, and the harmless operation should be the
one they land on by guessing.

*** CALLS REAL PEOPLE. *** Dials every contact in the body, at once.

One request can ring a lot of telephones. The only ceiling is voice's
per-org `MAX_LIMIT_OF_CALLS_PER_ORG_ID`; this contract does not cap
`contacts` itself, because a cap here that disagreed with voice's would
reject batches voice would have accepted.

Contacts whose number cannot be parsed are SKIPPED, not rejected - the
batch proceeds without them and the response names who was dropped. Read
it; do not assume every contact you sent was dialed.

Attempts reserve credits and connected minutes charge more. Tiered
`external`: this reaches strangers on the customer's behalf.

*** CALLS A REAL PERSON. *** Dials `to_phone` immediately.

An arbitrary number, inside an existing PAUSED or COMPLETED session. If
the session is ACTIVE voice refuses rather than dialing over a running
campaign.

The number does not have to belong to a contact: an unknown number is
resolved to an existing contact by phone, or a new contact is created for
it, so the call is attributable afterwards. That means this operation can
CREATE A CONTACT RECORD as a side effect.

Self-dialing is refused. Tiered `external`.

*** CALLS A REAL PERSON AGAIN. *** Redials a contact already tried.

Voice caps attempts per contact (`MAX_REDIAL_ATTEMPTS`) and refuses past
it, which is the guard against a retry loop becoming harassment - so treat
a 400 here as "stop", not as "retry".

It runs the same credit preflight the first dial does and can fail with
`insufficient_credits`, reserving the attempt fee plus connected minutes.
Tiered `external`.

CONTACTS NOBODY NEW. Ends one leg of a parallel session.

The other legs keep ringing. Gated on `voice:dialer:control`, the same
permission voice declares - re-declared here because voice's own gate does
not run for a server-to-server call.

*** REACHES A REAL PERSON. *** Leaves a voicemail and hangs up.

The script is played in the rep's cloned voice and the call is closed with
disposition `voicemail`. The person hears it. There is no undo.

The command is queued for the agent on the call (a 120-second window), so
a 200 means "accepted", not "already played". Tiered `external`.

patch.description:
CONTACTS NOBODY. Marks specific missed callbacks as seen.

Seen is not resolved: it clears the notification, it does not say anyone
called back. `resolve` is the separate, meaningful one.

CONTACTS NOBODY. Clears the whole missed-callback badge for one rep.

The app carries the organisation in the PATH here
(`/missed-callbacks/seen-all/{org_id}`). That segment is NOT published: a
caller must never be able to name the tenant it is clearing, so the org
comes from the key and the path ends at `seen-all`.

CONTACTS NOBODY. Closes a missed callback.

`resolution` is closed to `manual` (someone called them back) or `ignored`
(a decision not to). The two are not interchangeable in reporting, which
is why the field exists at all rather than a single "done" flag.
CONTACTS NOBODY. Reopens a missed callback closed by mistake.

get.description:

Answered from the call rows rather than the storage prefix, because
recordings moved between organisations by the merge migration keep the

that goes wrong answers "not owned".

The organisation asked about is always the key's own - it is not a
parameter, so this cannot be used to probe another tenant's storage.

field you left out. That behaviour is preserved rather than papered over -
but it is a body here, and the defaults are stated, so the reset is at
least visible in the contract. Send both fields every time.

post.description:
CONTACTS NOBODY - but it SPENDS, and it can spend a lot.

With `dry_run=false` this runs AI grading over EVERY ungraded call with a
transcript in the window - a model invocation each, one call every two
seconds, with no ceiling other than how many calls exist. On a busy
organisation over 365 days that is an unbounded bill from one request.

`dry_run` defaults to TRUE and genuinely short-circuits before any grading
(`parallel_calls.py:4602`), returning the eligible count and a sample.
Call it that way first and read the count.

Tiered `billable`, not `write`: it reaches a paid model per record.

The colleague passes on the transfer. The CALLER - a real human - STAYS ON

not tell them anything. Worth knowing before wiring this to an
auto-decline rule.

The app's path is `/preferences/{org_id}/{user_email}` and its handler
reads whichever organisation the path names. The org segment is NOT

configuration.

Voice additionally refuses to read a rep other than the authenticated one
(`dialer_settings.py:23-41`). An organisation API key is not a rep, so it
supplies the rep the caller named: the tenant boundary holds, the
rep-versus-rep boundary does not apply to an org credential.

CONTACTS NOBODY DIRECTLY - but `call_dnc_contacts` decides WHO MAY BE CALLED.

Setting it true lets the dialer call numbers on a do-not-call list. That is
a COMPLIANCE decision, not a convenience toggle, and it applies to every

PATCH semantics despite the verb: only fields you send are changed, and
