delete.description:
CONTACTS NOBODY. Deletes one of the organisation's CUSTOM dispositions.

The gap `voice_router` named as deliberately absent - "voice's own
dispositions router never exposed a delete endpoint" - which is no longer
true: it does, and this publishes it.

REFUSED WITH 409 IF ANY CALL IS ALREADY DISPOSITIONED WITH IT. So this
only ever removes an unused value - history cannot be rewritten by it, and
a 409 means "this one is in use", not "try again".

The organisation is carried in a HEADER, not the path, and voice resolves
the row with it (`_load_disposition_for_org`). It is the key's own org, so
one tenant cannot delete another's vocabulary by guessing an id.

ADMIN ONLY, and that gate is declared HERE. Voice declares
`require_org_admin()` on its own route, and for a server-to-server call
that dependency finds no bearer token and - with
`ENFORCE_VOICE_PERMISSIONS` off, which is everywhere today - ALLOWS the
request. `require_org_admin` from `developer_api.dependencies.admin` is
the one actually protecting this, and it refuses machine keys outright:
deleting shared org vocabulary needs a personal key held by an Admin or
Owner.

get.summary: List valid call disposition values (system + this org's custom)
get.description:
Return every disposition value accepted by ``disposition_filters`` on the
``new_call_disposition`` trigger - system values AND the caller org's own
custom dispositions.

Each entry carries ``origin``: ``system`` for the built-in vocabulary,
``custom`` for an org-defined one (whose ``value`` is the stored
``custom_{id}`` key, never the display name). ``category`` keeps its
existing meaning: ``sdr_selectable`` a rep can pick it, ``system_set`` only
the dialer backend writes it.

Authority for the system half is voice's ``SDR_SELECTABLE_DISPOSITIONS``
(``voice/graph8_livekit/schemas/dispositions.py``) plus the two system-set
values the dialer also emits (``sdr_hangup``, ``failed``). That half is
inlined here and a parity test
(``developer_api/tests/test_workflow_dispositions.py``) fails the build if
voice adds a value that is not mirrored - the previous "mirror the change
here" comment was not enforced and silently went stale when ``busy`` was
added.

The custom half comes from voice's ``GET /api/dialer/dispositions/{org_id}``,
with the org pinned server-side from the authenticated caller and echoed in
the ``X-Org-Id`` header voice's tenant gate requires. Nothing about the
request body or query can influence which org is read.

Degraded mode: if voice is unreachable or errors, this returns the system
vocabulary alone with ``source='static_fallback'`` and logs a warning,
rather than failing the whole call. An agent that sees
``source='static_fallback'`` should say it could not confirm custom
dispositions instead of asserting none exist.

Legacy aliases (``positive``/``neutral``/``negative``) are deliberately
absent: ``normalize_disposition`` rewrites them before storage, so a filter
on them could never match.

get.summary: List AI Inbox tags for the org (resolver helper)
get.description:
Resolve human tag descriptions ("out of office", "interested", "referred
me to a colleague") into the concrete tag IDs required by the
``new_inbox_tag_set`` trigger's ``tag_filters``.

This is the resolver that makes reply-intent workflows authorable. Without
it an agent has no way to turn a tag NAME into a tag ID, so it falls back to
a ``new_email_reply`` trigger plus a condition node grepping the body text -
which is both fragile and duplicates work the inbox AI agent already did
when it tagged the message on arrival.

``ai_applicable_only=true`` narrows to tags whose ``ai_can_apply`` is set,
i.e. the ones an agent applies automatically the moment an email lands.
Those are the tags a ``new_inbox_tag_set`` trigger will actually fire on
without a human touching anything.

Calls the ``ai_inbox`` tag service in-process (no voice round-trip). Org is
pinned from the authenticated caller and used as the Postgres tenant schema;
nothing client-supplied selects the tenant.

Returns ``{tags: [{id, name, description, color, ai_can_apply}], total}``.

``workbench_id`` is the value to paste straight into a node config. It is the

post.summary: Create a workbench (so a workflow has somewhere to write)
post.description:
Create an empty workbench and return its `workbench_id`.

The missing half of the loop: an agent could be TOLD a workbench id but could
never make one, so "build me a workflow that collects X into a new workbench"
always needed a human to go and click New Workbench first.

``entity_type`` is optional and must be ``contact`` or ``company`` when given;
a blank workbench may defer it, which is what the underlying command already
allows. ``created_by`` is the authenticated caller and is never read from the
request, so a key cannot attribute a workbench to someone else.

The webhook API key the browser route returns on create is deliberately NOT
surfaced here. It is a write credential for a different ingestion path, it is
returned exactly once, and nothing in the workflow surface needs it — an agent
that never sees it cannot leak it into a workflow config or a chat transcript.

get.summary: List workflow executions for the caller's org (recover a lost execution_id)
get.description:
List this org's workflow executions, newest first, with SQL-side
pagination - the recovery path for a lost ``execution_id`` (the single
``GET /workflows/executions/{execution_id}`` read below needs an id you
no longer have).

Org is pinned server-side from the authenticated caller and passed to
voice in the PATH; a client-supplied ``org_id`` query param is ignored,
so one tenant can never list another tenant's executions (the voice
backing route trusts its path ``org_id``, so pinning here is the tenant
boundary - getting it wrong is a cross-org IDOR). ``runtime_type`` is
pinned to ``workflow`` so only workflow runs surface here, matching the
sibling ``GET /workflows`` which does not expose raw LLM/API/script
action runs.

Proxies voice's ``GET /api/v1/executions/list/{org_id}`` and returns its
``ExecutionListResponse`` shape unchanged - ``{executions: [...],
total_count: int}`` - consistent with this router's pass-through
convention (voice owns the execution DTO; re-declaring its ~20 fields
here would only drift). Voice also clamps ``limit`` to 1..200 SQL-side;
the bounds here reject an out-of-range page with a clean 422 before the
round-trip.

Read-only and additive: nothing is created, and no existing route changes.

Resolves the ``sender_account_id`` on the Netrion workflow nodes

``linkedin_*`` triggers' ``linkedin_account_id``. Until this existed there was
NO way to discover these ids programmatically: voice's ``_RESOLVER_HINTS``
said "no MCP resolver yet — ask user", and the only listing endpoint
(``GET /v1/linkedin/accounts``) is behind ``get_current_user`` browser auth,
so an MCP/API caller could build the node and then not attach a sender.

string. ``account_resolution.resolve_active_account`` cannot parse the

one is a hard failure rather than a silent send from an arbitrary seat. The
field is emitted as a STRING because that is the node config's own type.

or per-org tables not provisioned all answer an empty list, never a 500.

the caller can say "that seat is disconnected" instead of "no seats".

get.description:
Every routine in this organization's workspace, with its recent run activity.

A routine is a standing instruction to an agent, delivered into one
conversation, on a schedule or on an event. ``503`` when the workspace has
never been provisioned to hold routines — nothing the caller sent is wrong.

post.description:
Create one routine.

``deliveryConversationId`` must be a conversation this credential can read —
otherwise a routine would be a way to post into a room its author cannot
see, and it is refused with the same ``403`` reading that room would give.

``triggerKind: "schedule"`` takes ``weekdays`` + ``localTime`` + ``timezone``;
``triggerKind: "event"`` takes a ``trigger`` config and an optional
``eventPolicy`` instead. The creator comes from the authenticated principal.

patch.description:
Change one routine.

Only somebody who can read the routine's delivery conversation may change
it, and re-pointing ``deliveryConversationId`` is a second grant: the NEW
conversation must be readable too. Omitted fields keep their stored value.

delete.description:
Delete one routine. Same guard as changing it: the delivery conversation decides.

Answers ``200`` with the deleted id rather than the in-app ``204``: every
Developer API operation returns the same ``{"data": ...}`` envelope, and one
route with no body is the exception every generated client has to special-case.

get.description:
The run ledger for one routine: telemetry only, newest first.

A plain list. It is named in ``READ_ONLY_ACTIVE_GET_ROUTES`` so the scope
generator's ``/run`` marker does not escalate reading history into
triggering work.

post.description:
Run one routine immediately, as the caller's own message.

Deliberately not the scheduled path: the instruction is posted into the
delivery conversation as this credential's message and the normal turn
machinery answers it, so a run-now exercises exactly what a live ask would —
approvals and all. An event routine may carry a ``sampleEvent`` to run
against; it is treated as data, never as instructions.

Create one project in one channel.

``channel`` is the channel NAME. The channel is resolved and authorized
exactly the way a send is, so a caller who may not post in a room may not
attach durable state to it: ``403``. The project id, the creator and the
room event come from the server; a body asserting them is refused by name.

Snooze or dismiss one revenue signal.

No ``Idempotency-Key``, matching the app: the key is derived from the
signal and the target state, so it is idempotent by construction. ``404``

The promotion is an ordinary send, and like every send it schedules an
agent turn after the write commits — which is why this is tiered

``source`` is the honesty field: ``live``, ``cached``, ``partial`` (then

Per-rep daily series behind the board. A null day was not measured; it is not zero.

CHANGING `country_code` RECOMPUTES YOUR PAYOUT RAIL and cascades to the

Accept a pending hire offer.

Delegates to ``marketplace.self_service_router.accept_offer`` so the
full side-effect chain runs intact: hiring transitions to ``active``,
the hiring-fee invoice is created, the SDR gains PropelAuth membership
in the client org (Member role; ``service_provider`` for commission-only
hires), the client gets a notification, and the EDA event fires.

Requires a personal API key — the underlying handler scopes ownership
via the SDR profile resolved from the caller's email.

post.description:
Submit a monthly invoice. Computes meeting count + amounts via the
existing ``CreateSdrInvoiceHandler``, transitions to ``pending``, and
starts the client's 5-calendar-day review window.

post.description:
SDR-side approve. Transitions ``sdr_review`` → ``pending``, sets
``submitted_at`` and a 5-day ``due_date``. After due_date the
auto-charge task fires on the client. Different surface from
``/marketplace/org/invoices/{id}/approve`` (which the client uses
to release payment immediately).

get.description: List invoices sent to the caller's org by marketplace SDRs.

Get full detail for one invoice owed by the caller's org. Includes
SDR profile + hiring contract context, so an agent can render the
full "approve or dispute" UI from a single call.

post.summary: Approve an SDR invoice → triggers immediate Stripe charge
post.description:
Approve an SDR invoice and trigger immediate charge via Stripe.

Delegates to ``marketplace.org_invoice_router.approve_invoice`` so the
``ChargeInvoiceHandler`` runs intact: status flips to ``charged``,
Stripe processes the transfer to the SDR's Connect account, and the
SDR gets a "your invoice was approved" notification.

Auth: requires a personal API key whose user has the Admin or Owner
role in the calling org (``require_org_admin``). Org-scoped (machine)
keys are refused — see ``developer_api.dependencies.admin``. The
rationale: this call fires an immediate Stripe charge on the org's
default payment method. Letting a non-admin or a machine key trigger
that would be a meaningful surface for unintended debits.

post.summary: Dispute an SDR invoice within the grace period
post.description:
Dispute an SDR invoice. Must be in ``pending`` state and within the
grace period (the 5-calendar-day review window after submission).

Auth: requires a personal API key whose user has the Admin or Owner
role in the calling org (``require_org_admin``). MBM PR #8575
round-7 review flagged that ``dispute_org_invoice`` is marked
``_DESTRUCTIVE`` at the MCP layer ("decide deliberately") but had
no developer_api gate. We gate it here for the same reason it's
DESTRUCTIVE in MCP: opening a dispute notifies the SDR, escalates to
ops for resolution, damages the engagement, and there is no
un-dispute API. Sibling consistency with ``approve_org_invoice`` and
``terminate_org_hiring`` — every destructive ``/org/*`` route
requires the same role.

get.summary: List active SDR hirings for the caller's org
get.description: List active hiring contracts where the caller's org is the client.

post.summary: Terminate an active hiring contract (org side)
post.description:
Terminate an active hiring. The SDR still receives a final
prorated invoice at the next monthly billing run covering work
through the termination date.

Auth: requires a personal API key whose user has the Admin or Owner
role in the calling org (``require_org_admin``). Org-scoped (machine)
keys are refused — see ``developer_api.dependencies.admin``. The
rationale: termination ends a paid commercial relationship and is not
reversible from this surface (the client must send a fresh hire offer
to re-engage). Restricting the trigger to org admins matches the
org's intent that contract lifecycle is a leadership-level decision.

post.summary: Withdraw a pending hiring offer (org side)
post.description:
Withdraw an offer the talent has not yet accepted (``pending_acceptance``).

The recovery path for an offer sent to the wrong talent or with wrong
terms. Voids the contract envelope so it can no longer be signed. No
invoice is generated — an unsigned offer never created a billable
relationship. Returns 409 if the offer is already active (terminate it
instead) or already terminated.

Auth mirrors terminate: a personal API key with Admin/Owner role in the
calling org (``require_org_admin``); org-scoped machine keys are refused.
Contract lifecycle stays a leadership-level decision.

get.description:
Every payout method you hold, PRIMARY FIRST.

The primary is the one a payout actually lands in. The others are set up

post.description:
Add an ADDITIONAL, non-primary payout method.

REACHES A PAYMENT PROVIDER. Your country decides which: a US person gets a
new Stripe Express account created at Stripe; everyone else gets a new Wise
method, with an already-filed W-8 copied onto it so you never re-certify the
same person.

Created NON-PRIMARY. It receives nothing until you promote it. Refused for

Re-point your payouts at a different method.

THIS CHANGES WHICH BANK ACCOUNT RECEIVES YOUR MONEY. There is exactly one

post.description:

The first-time path, where `POST /methods` adds a second one. Your profile
country picks the rail: a US person gets a Stripe Express account created at
Stripe, everyone else a Wise method. Idempotent - a second call returns the
account that already exists instead of opening another one at Stripe.

400 when your profile has no country (set it with `PATCH /me/profile`
first). Refused for an agency-managed rep - their payout goes to the agency.

NOT A PLAIN READ. It creates the Express account at Stripe if the method
does not have one yet, then mints a short-lived hosted link. Stripe-track

post.description:
Create the payee record money is sent to. REACHES WISE.

The provider has no idempotency key here, so the server holds a row lock
across validation and creation: a retried request short-circuits on the
existing recipient (`already_exists: true`) instead of creating a second
payee. Send `details` exactly as `bank-requirements` asked for it.

Requires a filed W-8 first (400 otherwise).

get.description:
Money that actually moved, plus chargeback deductions.

`net_balance` is the running figure AFTER deductions, which is why it is a
separate field rather than something to sum from the rows.

post.description:
Open a draft statement for one of your engagements.

THE PERIOD IS SERVER-DERIVED and any you send is ignored: an active
engagement bills the previous complete calendar month, a terminated one
bills its earliest unbilled month. The retainer is PRORATED to the days the
engagement was actually live, and the meeting lines are generated from the
engagement's own rate, so `amount` is the sum of the lines and never a typed
figure. Add commission / bonus / expense / discount lines, then submit.

409 when a statement already exists for that period. 403 on an
agency-managed engagement - the agency authors those.

get.description:
Your own statements, newest first.

`billed_period_start` / `billed_period_end` are the days ACTUALLY billed -
the calendar period clamped to the engagement - so a rep who started on the

The softer of the two refusals: it returns the statement to the author to
revise and resubmit, rather than rejecting it outright. Only from
`submitted`; 409 if someone already acted on it.

APPROVE THE BILL. submitted -> approved, and the statement locks.

This is the money call on the client side: approval creates the client
invoice that your organisation is charged, and the talent's payout follows
from it. It cannot be undone from this surface.

Admin-gated, like `POST /marketplace/org/invoices/{invoice_id}/approve`:
the caller must be an Admin or Owner of the org, on a personal key.

should not be able to commit the org to a charge. Only from `submitted`; a
409 means somebody already acted on it.

REFUSE the bill outright, with a reason the talent sees.

The harder of the two refusals (`request-changes` is the softer one): the
statement goes to `rejected`. The talent can still revise and resubmit it,
but nothing is billed from it until they do. Admin-gated for the same
reason approval is - accepting and refusing a bill are the same decision.

get.description:
Every commission plan version your org holds, newest first.

Versions are immutable once written; a change is a NEW version against the
same `plan_id`. Only an `active` version can be snapshotted onto a hire.

post.description:
Write a new plan version. Created as `draft`; activate it separately.

Pass `previous_version_id` to supersede an existing plan - the new row keeps
that plan's `plan_id` and takes the next version number. Omit it to start a
new plan.

Put a plan version IN FORCE.

From here on it is the formula every new engagement snapshots, so it decides
what people are paid. The terms are re-validated on the way in; an
unparseable version cannot be activated.

Dry-run a plan against one collection. Writes nothing, pays nobody.

Send the `terms` you are about to save and a sample `collection`; the answer
is exactly what `POST /commissions/entries` would compute for it. Use it
before activating a plan version, because activation is the act that
decides what people are paid. An unparseable plan is a 422.

get.description: Recorded earnings, newest first, capped at 500 by the app.

post.description:
Record a collection and compute what it earned. MONEY NOW OWED.

Calculated against the plan SNAPSHOTTED on the engagement at signature, not
against whatever is active today, so re-pricing never re-prices history.
Idempotent on `(event_id, invoice_line_id)`: the same collection replayed
returns the existing entry, and the SAME ids with different evidence is a
409 rather than a second payment.

Lands in `review`. It becomes payable when allocated to a statement.

PUT THE EARNING ON A BILL.

Writes the entry as a line item on the statement, which is what turns a
recorded earning into something actually paid. The statement is scoped
through the entry's OWN engagement, never an org id from the body, so an
entry cannot be allocated onto someone else's statement.

Refused once the statement is locked for review or payment, and refused if
the correction would take its total negative. Re-allocating to the same
statement is idempotent; to a different one it is a 409.

RELEASE OR REFUSE A HELD AMOUNT.

Only the quality decision and its evidence may change - resend the original
collection otherwise identical, or it is a 422. If the entry is already on a
statement the release arrives as a NEW reviewable entry rather than editing
a bill in flight, which is why an approved decision can create a second row.

CLAW BACK earnings against a refund. Writes a negative entry.

Never edits the original - the ledger stays append-only, which is what makes
it auditable. Reversals cannot exceed the original in total, and the same
`event_id` replayed returns the existing correction rather than doubling it.

put.description:
Publish the rate card. THIS IS THE PRICE A CLIENT IS BILLED.

The narrow sibling of `PATCH /marketplace/me/profile`, kept because it is
what the rates surface calls; both apply the same agency lock and the same
availability vocabulary. Set `availability_status` to `hidden` to come off
the browse list without deactivating anything.

than as a console in which nothing works.

EVERY contract of yours - pending, active and terminated - with client names.

Wider than the published `/marketplace/me/offers`, which returns only what
is still pending. Rows on an agency-managed engagement have the client's
rate redacted: the agency prices those and the rep is paid by the agency.

put.description:

Only while the invoice is in `sdr_review` - after
`POST /marketplace/me/invoices/{id}/approve` the client's review window is

`sdr_notes` is writable; `client_notes` and `dispute_reason` belong to the
paying side.

get.description:
A fresh Stripe Express onboarding link.

NOT A PLAIN READ: if you have no Express account yet it CREATES one at
Stripe first (idempotency-keyed on your profile id, so a retry does not mint
a second). Refused with a 400 on the Wise rail, where onboarding is the W-8
plus bank-details flow on the payout-account surface instead.

A login link into your Stripe Express dashboard.

THE LINK IS A CREDENTIAL - it logs the holder into the Stripe account your
payouts land in. Pre-checked against live Stripe state: a non-Express or
not-yet-onboarded account is a 400 explaining which, rather than a link that

post.description:
Upload your profile photo. `multipart/form-data`.

A headshot OR a resume is one of the three gates on going live to buyers -
see `completeness.blocking_reasons` on `PATCH /marketplace/me/profile`.
`headshot_source` in the response says whether the stored image is yours or
the generated initials fallback.

Upload your resume and let it fill in your profile. `multipart/form-data`.

The text is extracted and parsed by a model into `work_experience`,
strengths, industries, tools, `summary` and `tagline`. Those AI-derived
fields are OVERWRITTEN on every upload; anything you typed yourself is kept.
graph8 carries the parsing cost - no credits are charged. If extraction
fails the file is still stored and `message` says so.

Upload a video introduction. `multipart/form-data`.

Replacing one leaves the previous object in storage rather than deleting it
first, so the profile never points at nothing mid-upload. The new URL is
stamped as a deliberate edit, which protects it from being overwritten by a
later resume re-import.

Pull the AI assessment of your resume onto your profile.

Idempotent and safe to poll: it finds the LATEST analysed upload (so a
re-upload supersedes the cached one), copies the derived fields across,
and NEVER overwrites a field you edited yourself. `synced: false` with a
message means the pipeline has not finished, not that anything failed.

This is what produces the certification score, and the score is the third
gate on being visible to buyers - which is why the sync is a call you can
make rather than something to wait on.

get.description:
Per-step onboarding progress, computed from the profile each call.

post.description:
Issue verifiable proof of a finished engagement.

IDEMPOTENT: when nothing about the engagement has changed you get the
EXISTING certificate back rather than a second code, so a retry cannot leave
two certificates in circulation for one piece of work. 409 if the engagement
is not a signed active/completed one, or if its certificate was revoked.

The certificate carries a code a third party verifies; the app's public
verification route is deliberately not published here (see the router
docstring in `marketplace_agency_router` for the cross-org rule).

talent it was sent to. Anyone else gets 404 rather than 403, so hiring ids

`envelope.signer_token` is returned to the TALENT only and is the secret the
signing call needs; the client never sees it, because holding it would let
them sign in the talent's stead.

Terms documents waiting on your acknowledgement.

Answers for whichever side you are: a client org's pending rows AND, if the

`request` is forwarded because the handler reads exactly those two things

has hired them, and an AGENCY account replying on a roster thread is signed
as the AGENCY, because presenting the rep's name over words the rep did not
write would misrepresent who the buyer is talking to.

An agency account may reply on any thread of its own roster; everyone else,
only on their own. 404 otherwise.

The mirror of the buyer-side route and a genuinely separate set of columns -
archiving here does not archive it for the buyer.

post.description: Clear your own unread count on a thread. Idempotent.

Log a meeting that happened outside the integrated calendar.

A BILLING INPUT, not just a record: the per-meeting rate bills meetings that
reach `status='taken'`. This creates the row in `scheduled` and attributes
it to the client; moving it to `taken` is a separate, client-owned
transition, so recording a meeting here does not by itself bill for one.

Beside it sits `/marketplace/org/hirings/{hiring_id}`, which is the same
hiring - the meeting is scoped to it and to your org, and a hiring belonging
to another org is refused.

Attach the job description PDF to one of your roles. `multipart/form-data`.

The last missing piece of the already-published `/marketplace/job-posts/*`
lifecycle: a role could be created, edited, published and closed, but the
document candidates actually read could only be attached in the web app.

Ownership is checked BEFORE anything is written to storage, so a post you do
not own cannot leave an orphaned object behind. Talent-side organisations
are refused - they apply to roles, they do not publish them.

get.description:
Campaign Visitors report for the authenticated org (analytics report a23).

Returns, for the resolved window:

  * **summary** — KPI tiles (page events, campaign clicks, unique contacts /
    steps, identified visitors, and the encrypted/plaintext/unparseable
    diagnostic split). Click counters are email-security-scanner filtered
    (humans only) so they match the in-app report — raw scanner traffic
    (Microsoft Defender / SafeLinks) is excluded.
  * **top_campaign_steps** — per sequencer step: clicks, unique contacts, a
    human-readable label, and send-side context (emails sent / with link).
  * **link_engagement** — per clicked destination URL: human clicks, unique
    contacts, the emails-with-link denominator, and CTR% (clamped 0–100).
  * **top_contacts** — who clicked, with resolved name/email (PII; omit via
    `include_contacts=false`).

Enrichment (labels, email, send counts, CTR) is best-effort: a field is
``null`` when it couldn't be resolved, never a fabricated zero. An org with
no visitor-tracking pipeline returns an empty report with
``summary.jitsu_wired = false``.

Agency keys: pass ``X-Target-Org-Id`` to run the report for a specific client
org within your authorized set.

Everyone falls back to whatever sign-in they had before SSO. If your org
has no other sign-in method, this is the call that strands them - check
before running it from a script.

Enforcing it blocks every other sign-in method. That is the point of it,
and it is also the single most effective way to lock an org out of its own
account - enforce only once you have signed in through SSO yourself.

get.description:
Credits currently RESERVED against work in flight.

This is the difference `GET /usage` reports but cannot explain: a hold
subtracts from `available_credits` without appearing in the transaction
ledger, because nothing has been spent yet. An operation that reserves
credits up front and settles later shows up here in between.

A balance that looks lower than the ledger says is almost always this.

The org is the authenticated key's own. There is no customer parameter on
this route.

Whether this organisation's subscription is active.

Worth checking before anything that spends: a charge against an inactive
subscription is refused even when the balance is healthy, so "insufficient
credits" is not the only way spending fails.

`raise_on_unavailable` is set, which is the whole point of answering this
as its own route rather than as a boolean somewhere else: without it an
unreachable billing service and an authoritatively-inactive subscription
both answer `false`, and those two mean opposite things. Unreachable
becomes a 503 here; `false` means false.

What an LLM operation of this size would cost. Charges nothing.

READ `capped` before reading `credits`. Several tiers have a per-operation
ceiling, and for typical prompt sizes the ceiling is what is actually paid
- so `credits` stops moving when the prompt grows, and
`uncapped_credits` is what the token arithmetic alone would have produced.
A caller that shows `credits` without `capped` gets asked why shortening
the prompt changed nothing.

`found` is false for a tier that does not exist or is not currently
active; `credits` is then 0, which is not a price.

post.description: Submit an exact patch using the handoff's selected approval mode.

Open a short-lived edit session against one landing page.

Returns an `edit_session` id to pass to the two routes above. The session is
a LOCATOR, not a credential: it selects which draft the following calls act
on, and `get_api_user` still authenticates every one of them. It carries a
TTL and is bound at creation to this org and this actor.

`actor_email` is `str(user.id)`, byte-identical to what the read and patch
routes pass to `require_edit_session`. That is what closes the loop: a
session minted here resolves for the same key that minted it, and a mismatch
would make every subsequent call 404 against a session that plainly exists.

NO OWNABILITY GUARD, unlike the agent routes. `agent_router` refuses a write
from a key whose `actor_identities()` is empty, because an org key
authenticates as the shared constant `api-key@graph8.com`. The same constant
lands in `actor_email` here, so two org keys in ONE org can read and patch
each other's sessions. That is deliberate parity rather than an oversight:
the two sibling routes already bind on `str(user.id)` and already accept org
keys, so guarding only the create half would break the loop for exactly the
keys the other half still serves. The boundary that matters is unchanged --
`require_edit_session` rejects a session from another ORG. Tightening all
three together belongs with the per-key identity work recorded in
`.claude/agent-context/agent-runtime-api-key-door.md`.

NOT SCOPE-GATED LOCALLY, unlike its two siblings, and that is deliberate
rather than an oversight. They call `require_scope("landing-pages:...")`,
which makes `build_scope_policy` record them as `exempt`; an exempt route
publishes no `x-graph8-scope`, so their requirement is real but invisible in
the contract -- and `landing-pages` is not a resource in
`scope_vocabulary.json` at all, so the scope they name cannot be granted to
a key. It is inert today only because `require_scope` runs in soak mode by
default. Leaving this route ungated puts it in the GOVERNED set, where
`apply_scope_policy` attaches the gate and the bundle publishes
`integrations:write` -- the resource this file is actually mapped to. The
siblings are left alone here: correcting them moves two published operations
and belongs in its own change.

brand_inputs.title: Brand Inputs
brand_inputs.description: The legal business behind the messages: `legal_business_name` (required before registration can start), plus `ein`, `address`, `website`, `business_type`, `vertical` and whatever else the carrier registry asks for.

campaign_inputs.title: Campaign Inputs
campaign_inputs.description: What the messages are: `use_case`, `message_samples` and `opt_in_method` are the three the platform checks for before it considers the inputs complete.

A2pRegisterRequest.title: A2pRegisterRequest
A2pRegisterRequest.description:
Brand and campaign details for A2P 10DLC registration.

Mirrors `phone_numbers.interfaces.fastapi.dtos.A2pRegisterRequest`.

Both dicts are OPEN and forwarded as-is, matching the app, which types
them as bare `Dict[str, Any]` and stores them in JSONB before handing them
to the carrier registry by name. Closing them here would reject a field
the registry added last week.

AIBatchEnrichmentRequest.title: AIBatchEnrichmentRequest
AIBatchEnrichmentRequest.description:
Run a saved AI group over a list. CHARGES per record.

`enrichment_mode: all` runs EVERY record in the list; `specific` runs only
`record_ids`. `dry_run` returns the record count and price and dispatches
nothing.

auto_update.title: Auto Update
auto_update.description: Re-run when new data arrives. ONGOING SPEND when true.

skip_existing_values.title: Skip Existing Values
skip_existing_values.description: Skip rows that already have a value - the main cost control.

skip_recently_enriched.title: Skip Recently Enriched
skip_recently_enriched.description: Skip rows enriched in the last 30 days.

AIConfigDto.title: AIConfigDto
AIConfigDto.description: Execution settings for an AI enrichment group.

AIConfigSummary.title: AIConfigSummary
AIConfigSummary.description:
One saved AI enrichment config attached to (or global for) a list.

`group_id` is the handle the worker uses to load the prompt, model and
output mapping. `usecase` lets the client predict credit cost via
enrichment.constants.AI_USECASE_CREDITS (e.g. web-research = 3 credits/record).

AIConfigsResponse.title: AIConfigsResponse
AIConfigsResponse.description: Paginated (by list_id filter) collection of AI enrichment configs.

AIEnrichmentConfigDto.title: AIEnrichmentConfigDto
AIEnrichmentConfigDto.description: A full AI enrichment group definition.

export_mode.title: Export Mode
export_mode.description: `auto` exports found contacts without a human step; `review` holds them.

AIFindPeopleSettingsDto.title: AIFindPeopleSettingsDto
AIFindPeopleSettingsDto.description: Find-people mode settings for an AI group.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Hint only: fields are read from your data.

AIFormulaGenerateRequest.title: AIFormulaGenerateRequest
AIFormulaGenerateRequest.description: Turn a plain-language description into a formula. One model call.

AIFormulaPreviewRequest.title: AIFormulaPreviewRequest
AIFormulaPreviewRequest.description: Evaluate a formula over sample rows you supply. Local, no model call.

AIFormulaValidateRequest.title: AIFormulaValidateRequest
AIFormulaValidateRequest.description: Check a formula's syntax and field references.

AIOutputFieldDto.title: AIOutputFieldDto
AIOutputFieldDto.description: One field the AI pass is asked to return.

AIPipelineDraftRequest.title: AIPipelineDraftRequest
AIPipelineDraftRequest.description: Draft an enrichment pipeline from a stated goal. Returns a draft only.

AIReviewApplyRequest.title: AIReviewApplyRequest
AIReviewApplyRequest.description: Apply findings DETERMINISTICALLY. Spends nothing - no model runs.

AIReviewFixWithAIRequest.title: AIReviewFixWithAIRequest
AIReviewFixWithAIRequest.description: Send ONE finding to the edit engine. SPENDS CREDIT.

AIReviewRequest.title: AIReviewRequest
AIReviewRequest.description:
Run a review pass over the page. SPENDS CREDIT.

`deep` defaults TRUE, matching the app - the deeper pass is the one worth
running, and quietly defaulting to the cheap one here would make the same
call behave differently through the API than in Studio.

AIRunConditionRequest.title: AIRunConditionRequest
AIRunConditionRequest.description:
Describe in words when an enrichment should run; get back an expression.

The app takes a FREE DICT here, so this model takes one too rather than
narrowing below it - every field is optional and unknown keys are forwarded
untouched. Narrowing would refuse a body the browser accepts, which is the
mirror image of the bug the strict models elsewhere in this file prevent.

company_ids.title: Company Ids
company_ids.description: Company ids, at most 500 per call - the app refuses more; chunk larger sets.

AbmRollupRequest.title: AbmRollupRequest
AbmRollupRequest.description: Intent totals for a named set of accounts.

owner_id.title: Owner Id
owner_id.description: Who owns the deal. Omit to take the app's default - an API key is an ORGANISATION credential, so there is no 'me' to fall back to.

AccountDealCreateRequest.title: AccountDealCreateRequest
AccountDealCreateRequest.description:
Create a deal already attached to an account.

`POST /deals` creates one standalone. This attaches it in the same call,
which is the difference worth having: a two-step create leaves a window
where the deal exists with no account.

AccountPlanApplyRequest.title: AccountPlanApplyRequest
AccountPlanApplyRequest.description:
Persist the approved steps as a NEW plan version.

`proposed_plan` must be non-empty: apply REPLACES the account's steps, so
an empty proposal would blank the plan. The app answers 400 rather than
doing it, and this surface forwards that rather than second-guessing it.

AccountPlanListPayload.title: AccountPlanListPayload
AccountPlanListPayload.description: An open envelope for a LIST result, so a bare list keeps its shape.

AccountPlanPayload.title: AccountPlanPayload
AccountPlanPayload.description: An open envelope for a plan, a context read or a committee result.

instruction.title: Instruction
instruction.description: Free-text note echoed back with the diff.

AccountPlanPreviewRequest.title: AccountPlanPreviewRequest
AccountPlanPreviewRequest.description:
Diff a proposed plan against the current version. Persists NOTHING.

It also does not consume the signal-replanner cooldown, so a caller can
preview as often as it likes before committing with `/plan/apply`.

contact_id.title: Contact Id
contact_id.description: Committee member this step is aimed at.

AccountPlanStep.title: AccountPlanStep
AccountPlanStep.description:
One step in a plan: who to reach, on what channel, when, and why now.

`extra="allow"` mirrors the app's own model, which is also open - the step
shape carries per-channel extras the desk adds as it learns new channels,
and a closed mirror would DROP them on the way in rather than pass them
through.

`approval_status` is closed because it reaches a real `Literal` inside the
handler: a free value would raise there and escape as a 500 instead of a
422 naming the four states.

AccountPlanStepUpdateRequest.title: AccountPlanStepUpdateRequest
AccountPlanStepUpdateRequest.description:
Approve, reject or edit ONE step on the latest plan version.

`action` is closed - it reaches a real `Literal` inside the handler.
`draft_content` is what `edit` edits; sending it with `approve` or
`reject` is accepted and ignored, exactly as the app treats it.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: Optional why-now, recorded in the trigger history.

AccountPlanUpsertRequest.title: AccountPlanUpsertRequest
AccountPlanUpsertRequest.description:
Create the account's plan, or REPLAN it.

There is no update: a replan inserts a new version and bumps
`plan_version`. Prior versions stay readable through
`/desk/accounts/{account_id}/plan/history`.

type.title: Type
type.description: What to draft for this stakeholder.

irreversible.title: Irreversible
irreversible.description: Cannot be undone. Surfaced so a host can confirm before invoking.

ActionDescriptorDto.title: ActionDescriptorDto
ActionDescriptorDto.description: One action a page may invoke on one of its bound sources.

type.title: Type
type.description: string | number | date | bool | enum | json

sensitivity.title: Sensitivity
sensitivity.description: `pii` marks personal data, so a host can treat it accordingly

AdAIReviewRequest.title: AdAIReviewRequest
AdAIReviewRequest.description:
Run a review pass over the creative. SPENDS CREDIT.

`deep` defaults FALSE here and TRUE on the landing-page review. That
asymmetry is the app's and is preserved rather than smoothed over: the two
passes cost differently.

AdBatchCreateRequest.title: AdBatchCreateRequest
AdBatchCreateRequest.description:
Add several ads at once — "launch these four creatives as four ads".

Partial success is expected: one creative rejected on policy does not stop
the others, and the response reports each outcome separately.

status.title: Status
status.description: ok | partial — never render success off a 200 alone

ad_count.title: Ad Count
ad_count.description: Number of live (non-archived) ads in this campaign

AdCampaignResponse.title: AdCampaignResponse
AdCampaignResponse.description:
A launched paid-ad campaign.

Creative fields are NOT published here even though they still exist on the
underlying row for backwards compatibility. They are attributes of an ad,
not of a campaign, and publishing them at campaign level would force either
a breaking change or a permanent duplicate representation once a campaign
holds more than one ad. Read them from ``/ad-campaigns/{id}/ads``.

AdCollection.title: AdCollection
AdCollection.description:
A list of ad-platform objects.

A bare list from the app is surfaced as `items`; a named collection keeps
its own key AND gains `items`, so a caller can page either shape without
knowing which handler produced it.

AdCreateRequest.title: AdCreateRequest
AdCreateRequest.description:
Add one ad to a campaign.

Valid before launch (created with its siblings when the campaign launches)
and after (pushed to the live campaign immediately). ``extra="forbid"`` so a
field we never wired is a 422 rather than a silent success.

AdCreativeChatEditRequest.title: AdCreativeChatEditRequest
AdCreativeChatEditRequest.description: A natural-language edit to one creative. SPENDS CREDIT - a model runs.

AdPayload.title: AdPayload
AdPayload.description: One ad-platform object, or one handler response.

id.title: Id
id.description: graph8 ad id, stable across creative replacements. Null only for a campaign launched before per-ad control, until its first read.

status.title: Status
status.description: draft | launching | active | paused | archived | failed

source_ad_creative_id.title: Source Ad Creative Id
source_ad_creative_id.description: The Studio creative this ad was built from, when it came from Studio

platform_ad_id.title: Platform Ad Id
platform_ad_id.description: Current platform handle. Changes when the creative is replaced.

AdResponse.title: AdResponse
AdResponse.description:
One ad inside a campaign — a creative slot.

``id`` is graph8's, and it is stable: editing an ad almost always mints a new
platform ad (LinkedIn creatives are immutable, and on Google only Search/RSA
is mutable in place), but the slot and its measurement history survive that.
Address an ad by this id, never by ``platform_ad_id``.

AdStatusRequest.title: AdStatusRequest
AdStatusRequest.description: Pause or resume one ad without touching its siblings or the campaign.

AdUpdateRequest.title: AdUpdateRequest
AdUpdateRequest.description:
Edit one ad. Omitted fields are unchanged.

On a live campaign a creative change is applied as a REPLACE, because that
is what the platforms permit. The response reports whether the platform ad
was replaced so a caller knows review and learning restarted.

replaced_platform_ad.title: Replaced Platform Ad
replaced_platform_ad.description: True when the platform ad was recreated; review and learning restart

channel_id.title: Channel Id
channel_id.description: The sender's INTEGER id - a mailbox, number or account.

channel_value.title: Channel Value
channel_value.description: Its address: the email, phone number or profile.

AddChannelItem.title: AddChannelItem
AddChannelItem.description: One sender to attach. Mirrors `AddChannelPayload` minus the client `id`.

AddChannelsRequest.title: AddChannelsRequest
AddChannelsRequest.description: Attach senders to a sequence. Mirrors `AddChannelParams`.

contact_ids.title: Contact Ids
contact_ids.description: List of contact IDs to add

conflict_resolution.title: Conflict Resolution
conflict_resolution.description: Required on retry after a 409 CONFLICT_REVIEW_REQUIRED response: 'add_all' adds ready + every warned contact, 'skip_all' adds only ready contacts, 'custom' adds ready + the ids in include_warned_ids. Blocked contacts are always excluded regardless of this value.

include_warned_ids.title: Include Warned Ids
include_warned_ids.description: With conflict_resolution='custom', the warned contact ids to also add.

AddContactsToListRequest.title: AddContactsToListRequest
AddContactsToListRequest.description: Request body for adding contacts to a list.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the addition came from, for the audit trail.

AddDealsToListRequest.title: AddDealsToListRequest
AddDealsToListRequest.description:
Put deals on a deals list.

Deal ids are STRINGS here while contact, company, suppression and lead ids
are integers. That is the app's own typing and it is mirrored rather than
smoothed over: coercing would make a mistyped id a silent miss.

post_external_id.title: Post External Id
post_external_id.description: Optional echo of the path id. The PATH value is authoritative.

engagement_type.title: Engagement Type
engagement_type.description: Only commenters, or only reactors. Omit for both.

audience_name.title: Audience Name
audience_name.description: Create a new graph8 list with this name.

AddEngagersToListRequest.title: AddEngagersToListRequest
AddEngagersToListRequest.description:
Turn the people who engaged with a post into a graph8 list.

Supply `audience_id` to add to an existing list, or `audience_name` to
create one. Contacts that do not exist yet are created as stubs.

domains.title: Domains
domains.description: Domains already owned outside graph8, e.g. ['acme.com']

AddExternalDomainsRequest.title: AddExternalDomainsRequest
AddExternalDomainsRequest.description: Register domains you already own elsewhere so they can be used for sending.

send_invite.title: Send Invite
send_invite.description: Send the invite email now. TRUE REACHES A REAL PERSON.

AddInterviewMemberRequest.title: AddInterviewMemberRequest
AddInterviewMemberRequest.description:
Add someone to an interview round.

`send_invite=true` EMAILS THAT PERSON immediately. It defaults to false, so
adding a member is a plain write unless the caller asks for the mail.

AddPostToSequenceRequest.title: AddPostToSequenceRequest
AddPostToSequenceRequest.description:
Enrol a post's author into a sequence.

ASYNCHRONOUS. This resolves the author to a contact and publishes an
enrolment request; the sequencer picks it up afterwards. A 200 means the
request was accepted, not that the person is enrolled.

AddRowRequest.title: AddRowRequest
AddRowRequest.description: Add one job to a grid. Spends nothing until the job is run.

contact_ids.title: Contact Ids
contact_ids.description: Contact IDs to add to the sequence

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: List ID the contacts belong to

step_data.title: Step Data
step_data.description: The step's content, the same shape as `step_data` on `GET /sequences/{sequence_id}/steps`: `subject` / `body` for email, `message_body` for SMS and WhatsApp, the `linkedin_*` fields for LinkedIn, `instructions` for AI generation.

AddStepItem.title: AddStepItem
AddStepItem.description: One step to add. Mirrors `CreateStepPayload` minus the client `id`.

AddStepsRequest.title: AddStepsRequest
AddStepsRequest.description: Append steps to a sequence. Mirrors `CreateStepParams`.

AgencyProfileUpdateRequest.title: AgencyProfileUpdateRequest
AgencyProfileUpdateRequest.description:
The agency's own About/branding. Only these six fields are writable.

Never `status`, `owner_org_id`, `agency_profile_id` or `billing_email` -
those decide who gets paid and whether the agency exists.

AgencyStatementCreateRequest.title: AgencyStatementCreateRequest
AgencyStatementCreateRequest.description:
Draft a statement for one of the agency's own reps.

Narrower than the talent-side create: the agency never gets to send a period
or an amount at all, so those fields are absent rather than ignored.

AgentApprovalReceipt.title: AgentApprovalReceipt
AgentApprovalReceipt.description: One signed provenance row attributed to an approval.

receipts.title: Receipts
receipts.description: Empty rather than an error when the approval produced no receipts.

plan_digest.title: Plan Digest
plan_digest.description: The plan this approval was bound to. Compare it to the run's current plan to tell an approval that still describes the work from one that has drifted.

AgentApprovalResponse.title: AgentApprovalResponse
AgentApprovalResponse.description: One approval: the loop asking permission before a consequential step.

AgentBenchListPayload.title: AgentBenchListPayload
AgentBenchListPayload.description: An open envelope for a LIST answer, so a bare list keeps its shape.

AgentBenchPayload.title: AgentBenchPayload
AgentBenchPayload.description:
An open envelope for one approval answer.

Open because an approval carries the plan digest it is bound to, its expiry
and its provenance receipts, and that set has grown twice already. On a
human-in-the-loop surface a dropped field is a guarantee the caller does not
know they lost.

state.title: State
state.description: `approved` accepts the card as proposed, `edited` accepts it with your `edits`, `rejected` sends it back. Re-sending the same state is a no-op; a different state overwrites.

edits.title: Edits
edits.description: Per-field overrides for an `edited` card. The shape is the card's own and varies by card kind.

message.title: Message
message.description: What you say to the agent. Required unless you attach a file.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Continue this session. Omit to start a new one; the answer carries its `session_id`.

client_turn_id.title: Client Turn Id
client_turn_id.description: Your own id for this turn, so a retry is recognised as the same turn rather than said twice. Needs an existing `session_id`.

attachment_ids.title: Attachment Ids
attachment_ids.description: Uploaded file ids to attach, each at most once.

subject_account_id.title: Subject Account Id
subject_account_id.description: Bind a NEW session to this account. Ignored for an existing one.

subject_campaign_id.title: Subject Campaign Id
subject_campaign_id.description: Bind a NEW session to this campaign. Ignored for an existing one.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Bias the agent: `web_search`, `deep_thinking` or `research`. Left open, as the app leaves it: an unknown mode is ignored rather than refused.

page.title: Page
page.description: Where the user is in your product, so 'this' and 'here' resolve.

AgentConversationPayload.title: AgentConversationPayload
AgentConversationPayload.description:
An open envelope for the app's answer.

Open because the chat answer (`kind`, `message`, `chips`, `sources`,
`work_item_id`, ...) and the oversight feed (`approvals`, `blockers`,
`autonomous_fixes`, `states`, `bounds`) are both still growing, and a
dropped field on an agent surface is one the caller does not know they
lost.

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: Agent id from agent settings.

url_filter.title: Url Filter
url_filter.description: URL paths where this agent is active.

default.title: Default
default.description: Used when no URL filter matches.

AgentCreateRequest.title: AgentCreateRequest
AgentCreateRequest.description: Map an AI agent onto the URLs it should answer on.

AgentDocumentSearch.title: AgentDocumentSearch
AgentDocumentSearch.description:
voice binds `query` and `top_k` as FORM fields beside `org_id` and
`agent_id`; the router re-encodes this body as form data.

AgentPayload.title: AgentPayload
AgentPayload.description:
An open envelope for memory, evidence and the proactive opener.

Each carries planner or analysis state that changes as the agent platform
does. On an oversight surface a dropped field reads as an agent doing less
than it did, so nothing here is pinned.

triggered_by.title: Triggered By
triggered_by.description: Attribution; defaults to the key's identity.

AgentRunResponse.title: AgentRunResponse
AgentRunResponse.description: One run. Identical shape whether read from the list or on its own.

title.title: Title
title.description: Optional title; the app derives one when omitted.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: Optional seed messages to open the session with.

AgentSessionListResponse.title: AgentSessionListResponse
AgentSessionListResponse.description: Sessions owned by, or shared with, the principal behind the key.

is_pinned.title: Is Pinned
is_pinned.description: True to pin, false to unpin.

AgentSessionStatePayload.title: AgentSessionStatePayload
AgentSessionStatePayload.description:
An open envelope for a hydration or voice answer.

Open because session hydration returns the agent's STEPS as well as its
messages, and a step's `detail` is whatever the tool that produced it
reported. That set grows with every tool the platform gains, and a pinned
mirror would drop the detail of exactly the newest ones - which on a
transcript surface reads as the agent having done less than it did.

AgentSessionUpdateRequest.title: AgentSessionUpdateRequest
AgentSessionUpdateRequest.description: Both fields are optional; omit one to leave it untouched.

input_context.title: Input Context
input_context.description: Surrounding facts held constant (prior turns, contact, company).

expected_output.title: Expected Output
expected_output.description: What the assertion compares against; a tool name or list for expects_tool.

assertion_config.title: Assertion Config
assertion_config.description: Assertion options: target (resolved_instructions | tool_names | grounding_sources), case_sensitive, tool, collection_id, capability_tools, refusal_markers.

created_by.title: Created By
created_by.description: Attribution; defaults to the key's identity.

AgentTestCaseCreate.title: AgentTestCaseCreate
AgentTestCaseCreate.description:
A saved evaluation case: the user turn under test and what must hold.

`llm_judge` may be SAVED but is skipped by dry runs - a judge needs a real
completion, and a dry run never calls a model.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: preview | dry_run - both resolve configuration only.

AgentTestRun.title: AgentTestRun
AgentTestRun.description:
One dry run. Exactly one source: `test_case_id` (a saved case) or
`input_message` (ad-hoc). Never calls a model, never places a call, never
sends a message - it resolves what the agent WOULD receive and reach for.

AgentUpdateRequest.title: AgentUpdateRequest
AgentUpdateRequest.description:
Partial edit of an agent mapping. `chat_bot_id` stays required.

It is not a field being changed - it is how the app FINDS the row, because
agent ids are unique per bot rather than per org.

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: Which agent owns it. A known id the planner has a template for - `onboarding`, `dialer_setup`, `sequencer_setup`, `campaign_run`, `voice_setup`, `marketplace`, `dev_setup` - or a free-form value, for which the planner falls back to its `full` template. Left as an open string for that reason: an enum here would reject the ad-hoc case the planner explicitly supports.

visibility.title: Visibility
visibility.description: `private` (default) or `shared` org-wide. The default is the safe one: work started through an API key is not visible to the whole org unless asked for.

entry_point.title: Entry Point
entry_point.description: Per-session override. Unset, the planner reads the org's own signup entry point as the long-term truth - so omitting this is usually right.

subject_account_id.title: Subject Account Id
subject_account_id.description: Bind the session to a company.

subject_campaign_id.title: Subject Campaign Id
subject_campaign_id.description: Bind the session to a campaign.

seed_message.title: Seed Message
seed_message.description: First user message, so the session opens on the real request.

skill_mode.title: Skill Mode

AppRuntimeResponse.title: AppRuntimeResponse

Whether an app is ready to be built and run, and what is missing (J9).

A READINESS REPORT, not a promise. It answers from what the control plane

did the last deployment do. It does NOT claim the cluster side is ready,
because the namespace provisioner, the image registry and the runtime objects
are separate work and none of them exist yet.

`blockers` is the useful field and it is deliberately explicit. An agent
driving a build needs to know WHY it cannot proceed, and a bare
`ready: false` sends it guessing.

AppSourceRequest.title: AppSourceRequest
AppSourceRequest.description:
Bind an app to the repository a build should fetch (J1).

PROVIDER IS VALIDATED HERE, NOT BY A CHECK CONSTRAINT. `ensure_public_tables`
emits `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, which cannot add a CHECK to an already
created table, and editing the constraint tuple alone is a silent no-op. So
the vocabulary lives in `SOURCE_PROVIDERS` and this DTO is what enforces it,
the same way `repos_router` already validates its provider.

`credential_ref` is a POINTER, and the description says so on the wire. A
builder who pastes a token here has put it in the control-plane row, in every
backup of it, and in the response body of `GET /apps/{app_id}`. There is no
way to un-send that, so the field is named and documented to make the mistake
hard rather than merely regrettable.

AvailabilityInterval.description: A weekly recurring window. `day` is 0-6 with Monday = 0.

AvailabilityOverride.title: AvailabilityOverride
AvailabilityOverride.description:
A single calendar date whose windows REPLACE that weekday's windows.

An empty `intervals` list means closed all day — that is the whole point of an
override, so it is not treated as "unset". Window `day` values are ignored
here (the date already fixes the day), and a client that sends one has it
dropped by Pydantic's default `extra="ignore"`.

AvailabilityWindow.title: AvailabilityWindow
AvailabilityWindow.description:
One open window inside a single day, as wall-clock `HH:MM`.

`end <= start` means the window crosses midnight into the next day; `"24:00"`
is a legal `end` only and means end-of-day.

Both fields pin an exact LENGTH as well as a pattern, because a container's
`max_length` bounds the element COUNT and never a nested string — the bound on
the string itself has to live here.

The length pin is redundant against today's engine and kept anyway: pydantic
compiles this pattern with the Rust regex crate, whose `$` matches only at the
end of the haystack, so "09:00\n" is already rejected. Python's `re`, which
pydantic falls back to for patterns the Rust engine cannot compile, matches `$`
BEFORE a trailing newline and would let it through. Five characters cannot hold
a newline either way, so the pin makes the guarantee engine-independent.

quote_ids.description: Quote ids. An out-of-scope or unknown id is reported per-row, not fatal.

BatchQuoteActionRequest.title: BatchQuoteActionRequest
BatchQuoteActionRequest.description:
Archive, expire or revoke up to 200 quotes.

Each quote runs in its OWN transaction and reports its own outcome, so one
bad row does not roll back the rest. The per-row result is the whole point
of the endpoint - read it rather than the HTTP status.

BillingListPayload.title: BillingListPayload
BillingListPayload.description:
An open envelope for a LIST result. The rows are always under `items`;
`total` and paging fields ride along when the app reports them.

BillingPayload.title: BillingPayload
BillingPayload.description: An open envelope for one billing result.

mailbox.title: Mailbox
mailbox.description: The mailbox to block them on.

BlockedSenderCreateRequest.title: BlockedSenderCreateRequest
BlockedSenderCreateRequest.description:
Stop a sender reaching one mailbox.

Scoped to the MAILBOX, not the organisation: blocking on one mailbox does
not block the same sender on another.

ticket_ref.title: Ticket Ref
ticket_ref.description: Your reference for the removal ticket.

display_order.title: Display Order
display_order.description: Lower sorts first; ties break newest-first.

BlogCreateRequest.title: BlogCreateRequest
BlogCreateRequest.description:
An article card in the widget's rail.

`url` and `image_url` are validated by the app to be http/https; a scheme
it refuses is a 422 here rather than a broken card later.

url.title: Url
url.description: Page to read og:title / og:description / og:image from.

BlogMetadataRequest.title: BlogMetadataRequest
BlogMetadataRequest.description:
A URL to read Open Graph metadata from.

Persists NOTHING. It fetches the page and returns its `og:title`,
`og:description` and `og:image` so a caller can pre-fill an article card
instead of typing it - which is why it is tiered a read despite the verb.

BlogUpdateRequest.title: BlogUpdateRequest
BlogUpdateRequest.description: Partial edit of an article card. `chat_bot_id` locates the row.

mailbox_id.description: Integer `mailboxes.id` - the database primary key, NOT the cron-job string id. The app is explicit about the difference and so is this.

created_by_email.title: Created By Email
created_by_email.description: The person the twin is modelled on.

entity_data.description: The contact or company record, same shape as an execution input.

entity_id.description: Record id. Used for cache keying only.

research_depth.title: Research Depth

specific_areas.title: Specific Areas
specific_areas.description: Narrow the research to these areas.

max_sources.title: Max Sources

include_contact_info.title: Include Contact Info
include_contact_info.description: False omits emails and phone numbers, which is the expensive part.

api_key.description: The provider credential. WRITE-ONLY: no route on this API returns it. Omitting it on an update leaves the stored key in place.

file.title: File

audio_file.description: MP3, WAV, WebM, OGG or FLAC. 25 MB maximum.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Groups messages into one conversation. Generated when omitted.

linkedin_data.title: Linkedin Data
linkedin_data.description: JSON, as a string, e.g. from `twins/extract-linkedin`.

writing_style_file.title: Writing Style File
writing_style_file.description: A writing sample the twin imitates. 25 MB maximum.
