CreateWorkbenchBindingsRequest.title: CreateWorkbenchBindingsRequest
CreateWorkbenchBindingsRequest.description: Bind a workflow's outputs to columns on one list.

CreateWorkbenchPipelineRequest.title: CreateWorkbenchPipelineRequest
CreateWorkbenchPipelineRequest.description: Create a workbench pipeline. `enabled: true` ARMS it on every new row.

workflow_started.title: Workflow Started
workflow_started.description: False is NORMAL, not an error: the run is stored either way and no worker picked it up on this attempt. Poll the run rather than retrying the create, which would start a second one.

client_secret.title: Client Secret
client_secret.description: Shown ONCE. Store it now — only its hash is kept, so it cannot be retrieved again. Rotate by creating a new credential and revoking this one.

CreatedCredentialResponse.title: CreatedCredentialResponse
CreatedCredentialResponse.description:
The create response, and the ONLY time the secret is ever returned.

Only the SHA-256 is stored — `developer_app_credentials` has no column that
could hold a plaintext secret — so this response cannot be reissued. That is
the point: a secret the platform can re-read is a secret the platform can
leak.

CredentialResponse.title: CredentialResponse
CredentialResponse.description: A service credential. Carries NO secret.

list_name.title: List Name
list_name.description: Audience title. Matched exactly; reused when it exists.

connection_id.title: Connection Id
connection_id.description: The CRM connection this audience is for. Its provider is recorded on the audience as the source and as a `crm-import` tag, which is what lets a later sync tell CRM-imported rows from graph8-native ones.

entity_type.title: Entity Type
entity_type.description: `contacts`, `companies`, `deals` or `leads`. Singular forms are accepted and pluralised by the app; anything unrecognised falls back to `contacts`. Omit for `contacts`.

CrmAudienceRequest.title: CrmAudienceRequest
CrmAudienceRequest.description:
Get, or create, the graph8 audience a CRM import lands in.

Idempotent by TITLE: calling twice with the same `list_name` returns the
same audience with `created: false` rather than making a second one. That is
what makes it safe to call before every import, and it is why this is not
`POST /lists` - that one always creates.

created.title: Created
created.description: True only when THIS call created the audience; false when it already existed.

CrmAudienceResponse.title: CrmAudienceResponse
CrmAudienceResponse.description: The audience, and whether this call is what created it.

CrmCollection.title: CrmCollection
CrmCollection.description:
A list of CRM records.

A bare list from the app is surfaced as `items`; a named collection keeps
its own key AND gains `items`, so a caller can page either shape without
knowing which handler produced it.

CrmCollectionPayload.title: CrmCollectionPayload
CrmCollectionPayload.description: An open envelope for a LIST result, so a bare list keeps its shape.

company_id.title: Company Id
company_id.description: The CRM's company id, not graph8's.

CrmContactCreateRequest.title: CrmContactCreateRequest
CrmContactCreateRequest.description: A new contact, created in the CUSTOMER'S CRM.

CrmContactUpdateRequest.title: CrmContactUpdateRequest
CrmContactUpdateRequest.description:
A partial update. Every field is optional; omitted fields are untouched.

`emails`, `phones`, `custom_fields` and `tags` are optional LISTS rather
than list-with-default here, which is the difference that matters: on the
create model an omitted list means "none", and on this one it means "leave
what is there". Sending `[]` REPLACES with empty.

field_value.title: Field Value
field_value.description: Required, but may be null - which is how a custom field is cleared.

CrmCustomField.title: CrmCustomField
CrmCustomField.description:
One provider-side custom field.

`field_name` is the CRM's API name, not its label. Read the valid names
from `GET /integrations/crm/fields`; a name the provider does not have is
rejected by the provider, not here.

stage.title: Stage
stage.description: Provider's pipeline stage. Omit to take the provider's default stage.

email_type.title: Email Type
email_type.description: Provider's own label, e.g. `work`. Passed through unchanged.

CrmPayload.title: CrmPayload
CrmPayload.description:
One CRM record, or one provider response.

Open-shaped ON PURPOSE. These bodies carry whatever the provider returned,
the field set differs between HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive and SugarCRM,
and it grows every time one of them ships something. Pinning it would drop
whatever a provider reported that this contract had not caught up on -
which on a CRM surface means silently hiding the customer's own data from
them.

records.title: Records
records.description: Records to push to the CRM provider

CrmRecordPayload.title: CrmRecordPayload
CrmRecordPayload.description:
An open envelope for one record, one dashboard or one job receipt.

Open because most of these reads are COMPUTED shapes - an engagement
summary, a next-best-step, an intelligence status - that grow with the
product, and dropping a field from an advisory read makes it say "nothing
to report" rather than "we did not tell you".

csv.title: Csv
csv.description: The full CSV document, header row first.

CsvExportPayload.title: CsvExportPayload
CsvExportPayload.description:
A CSV export, carried inside the JSON envelope.

The app streams these as `text/csv` attachments. Every other operation in
this contract answers with the `ApiResponse` envelope, and an SDK method
that sometimes returns JSON and sometimes a byte stream is a trap, so the
CSV text is returned as a string field instead.

CustomFieldDiConfigItem.title: CustomFieldDiConfigItem
CustomFieldDiConfigItem.description:
One custom-field mapping.

Typed rather than left an open dict: `crm_provider` and `field_id` are
REQUIRED upstream, and an open list let a missing one reach the app's model
as a raw ValidationError from inside the proxy - a 500 for a plain client
error. The 255 caps are the underlying VARCHAR widths, and `display_name`
additionally feeds the Deal Intelligence LLM prompt, so its bound is a
token-budget and prompt-injection concern rather than cosmetic.

CustomFieldDiConfigListResponse.title: CustomFieldDiConfigListResponse
CustomFieldDiConfigListResponse.description:
Deal custom-field mappings for a CRM provider.

This is what a rebuilt deal form needs to know which custom fields exist
and how they map outward - without it a custom UI can render the built-in
columns and nothing else.

CustomFieldDiConfigUpsertRequest.title: CustomFieldDiConfigUpsertRequest
CustomFieldDiConfigUpsertRequest.description:
Replace the deal custom-field mappings.

`items` is the FULL desired set for the providers it names, not a delta -
the app upserts what is sent. Capped at 100 by the app; declared here so an
over-long request is a 422 naming the field rather than a failure deeper
in.

written.title: Written
written.description: Caller keys that resolved to a custom column and were written.

created.title: Created
created.description: Caller keys for which a NEW custom column was created by this request.

ignored.title: Ignored
ignored.description: Caller keys that matched no custom column and were NOT written. Create the column first (POST /fields) or pass create_missing_fields=true.

CustomFieldWriteReport.title: CustomFieldWriteReport
CustomFieldWriteReport.description:
How a write path handled the request's custom (dynamic) column keys.

Shared by every Developer API write surface that accepts custom columns
(``POST /contacts``, ``PUT /contacts/assert[/batch]``,
``PUT /companies/assert[/batch]``).

Every field defaults to empty, so a client that ignores this object sees no
behavioural change. It exists because these keys were previously dropped
with NO caller-visible signal — the only trace was a server-side
``logger.warning`` in ``append_to_audience``.

idea.title: Idea
idea.description: Plain-language description of the page to build.

name.title: Name
name.description: Short title. Derived from the idea when omitted.

attached_assets.title: Attached Assets
attached_assets.description: Images and videos the page must use. Max 5 images and 2 videos.

plan.description: An approved plan from the plan-preview step.

CustomLayoutTemplateRequest.title: CustomLayoutTemplateRequest
CustomLayoutTemplateRequest.description:
Mirrors `campaign_builder.routers.brand_kit.CustomLayoutTemplateRequest`.

`plan` is the object `POST /brand-kit/layout-templates/custom/plan` returns.
Passing it back is how you build the page you previewed rather than a new
interpretation of the same idea.

idea.title: Idea
idea.description: Plain-language description of the page to plan.

attached_assets.title: Attached Assets
attached_assets.description: Images and videos the plan must place.

CustomTemplatePlanRequest.title: CustomTemplatePlanRequest
CustomTemplatePlanRequest.description:
Mirrors `campaign_builder.routers.brand_kit.CustomPlanRequest`.

The preview half of the pair above. Builds nothing and stores nothing.

mashup_company_id.title: Mashup Company Id
mashup_company_id.description: graph8 company id. Null removes the mapping.

CustomerMappingRequest.title: CustomerMappingRequest
CustomerMappingRequest.description: Link a Stripe customer to a graph8 company, or unlink it with null.

folder_name.title: Folder Name
folder_name.description: Folder name, as shown in Drive.

local_folder_key.title: Local Folder Key
local_folder_key.description: Which Library folder the files land in. Derived when omitted.

library_folder_id.title: Library Folder Id
library_folder_id.description: Library folder id. REPLACES any other mapping to the same Library folder.

transcript_id.title: Transcript Id
transcript_id.description: The transcript to attach to this meeting.

account_id.title: Account Id
account_id.description: The account the transcript belongs to.

DataFilePreviewResponse.title: DataFilePreviewResponse
DataFilePreviewResponse.description:
A page of rows as they will be read, with the mapping applied.

Rows are open dicts: they are the customer's own columns, so there is no
schema to pin.

row_count.title: Row Count
row_count.description: Rows detected. The import pre-check budgets against this.

DataFileUploadResponse.title: DataFileUploadResponse
DataFileUploadResponse.description:
The stored file, and how many rows it turned out to have.

`row_count` is the number a caller should budget against: the import
pre-check treats it as the UPPER BOUND on new contacts, so an import is
refused if that many would breach the org's contact limit - even though
some rows will resolve to updates rather than creates.

datafile_id.title: Datafile Id
datafile_id.description: Id of a previously uploaded datafile.

DatafileImportRequest.title: DatafileImportRequest
DatafileImportRequest.description:
Import rows from a datafile that has ALREADY been uploaded.

`datafile_id` refers to an upload made elsewhere; this operation does not
accept file content, which is why it fits the JSON envelope at all.

company_id.title: Company Id
company_id.description: Company ID (match key, combined with name)

DealCollectionPayload.title: DealCollectionPayload
DealCollectionPayload.description: An open envelope for a LIST result, so a bare list keeps its shape.

mashup_company_id.title: Mashup Company Id
mashup_company_id.description: The CANONICAL company id (`mashup_companies`), not a `cb_company_extensions` / ABM overlay id. The two are different tables with different ids and passing the wrong one attaches the deal to nothing.

DealCompanyRequest.title: DealCompanyRequest
DealCompanyRequest.description: Attach or change the company on a deal.

id.title: Id
id.description: Link id, not the person id.

buying_role.title: Buying Role
buying_role.description: General buying role from the contact record.

DealContact.title: DealContact
DealContact.description:
One person linked to a deal.

`role` is the person's role on THIS deal (champion, decision_maker,
influencer, blocker, coach, end_user). `buying_role` is their general
buying role on the contact record and is NOT deal-specific - the two are
separate fields in the app and conflating them loses the distinction
between "who this is" and "what they are to this deal".

person_id.title: Person Id
person_id.description: Contact to link to the deal.

role.title: Role
role.description: Role on this deal: champion, decision_maker, influencer, blocker, coach or end_user. The app does not constrain the value, so it is left open here rather than declaring an enum this surface would then have to keep in lock-step.

role.title: Role
role.description: Buying-committee role for this contact on this deal. One of: champion, decision_maker, influencer, blocker, coach, end_user. Pass null to clear the role.

DealContactRoleUpdateRequest.title: DealContactRoleUpdateRequest
DealContactRoleUpdateRequest.description:
Body for `PUT /deals/{deal_id}/contacts/{contact_id}`.

`role` is REQUIRED but nullable. That combination is the whole point of a
PUT here: `{"role": "champion"}` sets it, `{"role": null}` clears it, and
an empty body `{}` is a 422 rather than a silent no-op — a PUT that says
nothing about the sub-resource it is replacing is a caller bug, and the
alternative (treating omission as "clear") would delete data on a typo.

company_id.title: Company Id
company_id.description: Deprecated: the company is derived from the contacts. If sent, it must match; otherwise omit it.

owner_id.title: Owner Id
owner_id.description: Deal owner (user id or email). Required.

contact_ids.title: Contact Ids
contact_ids.description: mashup_contact_ids to associate with the deal (>=1 required; all must share one company)

allow_duplicate.title: Allow Duplicate
allow_duplicate.description: Set true to create a deal even if one already exists for the company

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: Optimistic-concurrency token. None means this org has no revision tracking, so a save is unconditional - it does NOT mean 1.

DealDetail.title: DealDetail
DealDetail.description:
One deal, with the related data the detail page reads.

`revision` is the optimistic-concurrency token. It is `None` when the org
has no canonical revision tracking provisioned - the app degrades rather
than 503ing a read - and a null there means an unconditional save, NOT
revision 1. Do not default it.

structured_data.title: Structured Data
structured_data.description: The machine-readable half. Replaces, does not merge.

DealDocumentUpdateRequest.title: DealDocumentUpdateRequest
DealDocumentUpdateRequest.description:
Edit a generated deal document in place.

Mirrors `campaign_builder.models.deal_documents.UpdateDealDocumentRequest`.
An omitted field is left alone; `structured_data` REPLACES the stored
object rather than merging into it.

DealFieldOverride.title: DealFieldOverride
DealFieldOverride.description:
Which side of the merge wins one field.

Without an override the app picks per its own rules. Name a field here to
decide it yourself - the only way to keep a value from the deal that is
being merged AWAY.

DealLineItemRecord.title: DealLineItemRecord
DealLineItemRecord.description: A deal line item. Money fields are in cents.

DealLineItemWrite.title: DealLineItemWrite
DealLineItemWrite.description:
One line item in a replace request. Money is in CENTS.

`line_total` is not accepted: the server recomputes it from
`unit_amount`, `quantity` and `discount_pct`.

DealLineItemsPayload.title: DealLineItemsPayload
DealLineItemsPayload.description:
A deal's line items with its derived amount and quote-mismatch flag.

`amount` and `linked_quote_total` are in DOLLARS (the deal's own unit);
line-item money is in cents. `amount_mismatch` is true when the deal amount
and its most authoritative linked quote disagree by more than half a cent.

DealLineItemsReplaceBody.title: DealLineItemsReplaceBody
DealLineItemsReplaceBody.description: The FULL desired set of line items. An empty list clears them.

DealListResponse.title: DealListResponse
DealListResponse.description: A page of deals on one account.

target_pipeline_id.title: Target Pipeline Id
target_pipeline_id.description: Pipeline to move the deal into.

DealMovePipelineRequest.title: DealMovePipelineRequest
DealMovePipelineRequest.description:
Move a deal to a different pipeline.

The deal keeps its identity and history; only its pipeline and stage
change. Its current stage does NOT carry over - the target pipeline has
its own stages, and the app re-seats the deal within them.

content.title: Content
content.description: Full replacement body - this is not a patch.

mentioned_users.title: Mentioned Users
mentioned_users.description: Who is mentioned AFTER the edit. Omitting someone removes their mention, because the list replaces rather than adds.

DealNoteUpdateRequest.title: DealNoteUpdateRequest
DealNoteUpdateRequest.description: Rewrite a note's body and its mentions.

DealOpResponse.title: DealOpResponse
DealOpResponse.description: Whatever the operation returns, carried through whole.

DealPayload.title: DealPayload
DealPayload.description:
An open envelope for a deal, a merge preview or a column result.

Open because the crossfire and merge-preview payloads are computed shapes
that grow with the product, and a closed model would drop a field from an
ADVISORY read - where a missing signal reads as "nothing to worry about"
rather than "we did not tell you".

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: CRM revision after a conditional update

DealStageVelocityBucket.title: DealStageVelocityBucket
DealStageVelocityBucket.description:
Movement through one stage.

`avg_days_in_stage` and `conversion_rate` are null (not 0) when there is no
sample: an average over zero completed dwells is undefined.

DealStageVelocityStuckSummary.title: DealStageVelocityStuckSummary
DealStageVelocityStuckSummary.description: `total_count` is exact; `deals` is capped at 100 (`truncated` says so).

DealSummary.title: DealSummary
DealSummary.description: One deal as it appears in a list.

expected_revision.title: Expected Revision
expected_revision.description: Apply only if the canonical CRM revision still matches; otherwise return 409. Omit for existing PATCH behavior.

owner_id.title: Owner Id
owner_id.description: Reassign deal owner (member id, email, or PropelAuth uid). Cannot be cleared.

add_contact_ids.title: Add Contact Ids
add_contact_ids.description: mashup_contact_ids to add to the deal (must match the deal's company; idempotent)

remove_contact_ids.title: Remove Contact Ids
remove_contact_ids.description: mashup_contact_ids to remove from the deal (idempotent — unlinked skipped)

contact_roles.title: Contact Roles
contact_roles.description: Buying-committee roles keyed by mashup_contact_id, e.g. {"5500429": "champion", "5500914": null}. Valid roles: champion, decision_maker, influencer, blocker, coach, end_user. null clears a role. Each id must already be linked to the deal or be present in add_contact_ids in the same request (422 otherwise).

edit_payload.title: Edit Payload
edit_payload.description: The redirected step, for 'edit_and_approve'. Ignored for the other decisions.

DecideAgentApprovalRequest.title: DecideAgentApprovalRequest
DecideAgentApprovalRequest.description:
Decide directly, or relay a stored human authorization exclusively.

There is no client-supplied version to pass. Double-decide is settled
server-side by `WHERE decided_at IS NULL`, so exactly one caller wins and the
loser gets 409 rather than overwriting the first decision.

DefaultConferencingEnvelope.title: DefaultConferencingEnvelope
DefaultConferencingEnvelope.description:
Envelope for GET/POST conferencing default. Inner fields are all-Optional
(``null`` when nothing is configured), so the envelope is what carries the
real payload through response validation.

DeliverabilityListPayload.title: DeliverabilityListPayload
DeliverabilityListPayload.description: An open envelope for a LIST result, so a bare list keeps its shape.

DeliverabilityPayload.title: DeliverabilityPayload
DeliverabilityPayload.description:
An open envelope for a test, a schedule or a warmup report.

Open because placement results carry one panel per seed provider and the
provider set changes; a closed model would drop a panel, and a missing
panel on a deliverability report reads as "we did not test there" when the
truth may be "you did not land there".

since.title: Since
since.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Omit and the app picks the last successful watermark - which is usually what you want, and always safer than guessing one.

entity_types.title: Entity Types
entity_types.description: Limit to these entity types. Omit for all.

recover_missing.title: Recover Missing
recover_missing.description: Also re-fetch records the previous run should have imported and did not. Slower, and the reason to use it is a suspected gap rather than routine.

DeltaSyncRequest.title: DeltaSyncRequest
DeltaSyncRequest.description:
Import only what changed since a watermark.

The response echoes `since` back as ISO 8601, so the caller learns the
watermark the server actually used rather than assuming its own was
accepted.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the build has reached. `deployed` is not settable here -- taking traffic is a separate, builder-initiated promote.

image_digest.title: Image Digest
image_digest.description: The pushed image digest, once there is one. Reported with `promoting`.

last_error_sanitized.title: Last Error Sanitized
last_error_sanitized.description: A short, ALREADY-SANITIZED failure reason, surfaced to the builder. Build logs carry secrets and other tenants' identifiers, so the controller sanitizes before sending and this field is truncated here.

DeploymentProgressRequest.title: DeploymentProgressRequest
DeploymentProgressRequest.description:
What the in-cluster build controller reports as a build advances (J2).

THE ALLOWED SET IS `building | promoting | failed`, AND `deployed` IS ABSENT
ON PURPOSE. The controller knows when a build started and when an image is
pushed and ready. It does not decide that the app should take traffic; that is
`POST .../promote`, a separate act by the builder. Letting the callback write
`deployed` would collapse "the build finished" and "send users at it" into one
step performed by whichever pod happened to run the build.

`rolled_back` is likewise absent: a rollback is a decision about a deployment
that is already serving, which a builder makes.

last_error_sanitized.title: Last Error Sanitized
last_error_sanitized.description: Sanitized at the write. Build logs carry secrets and other tenants' ids.

build_started_at.title: Build Started At
build_started_at.description: When the build started. `null` means it was not measured.

build_finished_at.title: Build Finished At
build_finished_at.description: When the build ended, at `promoting` or at `failed`. Not at `deployed`: that is reached after traffic is taken, so measuring to it would count promotion and rollout as build time.

build_seconds.title: Build Seconds
build_seconds.description: Measured build duration. `null` means NOT MEASURED, never zero: a build whose transitions were not reported has no duration, and a metering pipeline reading 0 would bill nothing and look correct.

DeprecateKnowledgeRequest.title: DeprecateKnowledgeRequest
DeprecateKnowledgeRequest.description: Retire a concept. `reason` is required and is kept on the record.

DesignTokenColors.title: DesignTokenColors
DesignTokenColors.description:
Color slots consumed by the widget's --wcw-* CSS var vocabulary.

LIGHT-mode and mode-invariant leaves ONLY. Per-mode dark variants live on the
sibling ``DesignTokenColorsDark`` group (``designTokens.colorsDark``), NOT as
``*Dark`` twins here (Phase G). The ``@field_validator("*")`` hex guard below
is exactly WHY the dark palette must be a sibling group rather than a nested
``colors.dark`` object — a nested dict would be fed to ``_require_hex_color``
and 422 the save (the same force that made ``DesignTokenHeader`` separate).
A legacy stored ``colors.<name>Dark`` leaf is lifted into ``colorsDark`` at
parse time by ``DesignTokens._lift_legacy_dark_leaves`` — no data migration.

DesignTokenColorsDark.title: DesignTokenColorsDark
DesignTokenColorsDark.description:
Per-mode DARK colour overrides (``designTokens.colorsDark``, Phase G).

A sibling of ``DesignTokenColors`` holding the dark variant of every colour
leaf that renders differently in dark mode. ABSENT ⇒ the widget renders
exactly as it did before this group existed (the dark literal, or — for a
leaf an org set in ``colors`` and that historically painted both modes — that
``colors`` value). Only leaves with a genuine dark render path live here; a
mode-invariant leaf (launcher, header gradient, send button, hero) has no
entry, so no dead tokens are introduced.

Field names carry NO ``Dark`` suffix — the group is the mode. The 13 leaves
that previously lived as ``colors.<name>Dark`` twins were migrated here; the
upconverter on ``DesignTokens`` lifts any legacy value so no row regresses.

DesignTokenGeometry.title: DesignTokenGeometry
DesignTokenGeometry.description:
RFC Phase E4 — launcher / panel / badge / chip geometry, CLAMPED.

The most locked-down group in the model, because `chat-script` injects these
into the CUSTOMER's page rather than into the widget iframe (RFC §17.1).
Unclamped geometry on a host page is a defacement vector, so every leaf is
whole-pixel-only and range-bounded — see `_require_px_in_range`.

Ranges for `launcherSize` / `launcherOffset*` are INHERITED from the ratified
product decision (RFC §19 decision 4: "launcher geometry in scope with
clamped ranges — size ~36-64px, offsets ~8-48px"), not invented here.

Widget COLLAPSED WIDTH is deliberately absent: it is already plumbed as the
flat `chatWidth` column and read at runtime by the deployed bundle, so a
token would be a second writer for one property.

── TWO CLAMPS ARE ONE-DIRECTIONAL (max pinned at today's value) ────────────
`widgetWidthExpanded` (max 640) and `launcherOffsetX` (max 20) may only ever
SHRINK. This is not conservatism, it is a live constraint:

The expanded panel needs a `widgetWidthExpanded + launcherOffsetX` viewport
to fit, but the mobile veto that hides the expand control is the hardcoded
`MOBILE_BREAKPOINT_PX = 560` (`chat-script/src/components/container.ts`,
mirrored as a literal `@media (max-width: 560px)` in `styles.ts`). Today's
640 + 20 = 660 already exceeds it, so viewports 561-659px ALREADY render an
overflowing panel — a pre-existing defect (GH #12173). Letting either value
GROW would widen that band onto more real devices.

A media-query CONDITION cannot read a custom property, so the guard cannot be
derived the way the panel's `bottom` is; correcting it means making
`MOBILE_BREAKPOINT_PX` config-derived across `container.ts` + `expand.ts` +
the emitted media query. That is GH #12173, and it is what lifts these two
ceilings. Until it lands, 640 and 20 are load-bearing — do not raise them.

THE RULE, so it is applied correctly next time: an axis needs a
one-directional clamp exactly when it has NO viewport clamp. The horizontal
axis has none. The vertical axis has `calc(100dvh - 140px)`, and the worst
case under these ranges is `launcherOffsetY(48) + launcherSize(64) + gap(11)
= 123px`, which stays inside that 140px reserve with 17px to spare at every
viewport height — which is why `launcherOffsetY`, `launcherSize`, `badgeSize`
and `chipGap` are free to grow. Any future range change must preserve
`launcherOffsetY + launcherSize + 11 <= 140`.

DesignTokenHeader.title: DesignTokenHeader
DesignTokenHeader.description:
How the header surface is painted — mode + gradient blend point.

A SEPARATE group, not new `DesignTokenColors` slots, and that is forced:
`DesignTokenColors` hex-validates EVERY field (`@field_validator("*")`), so a
`"solid"` mode or a numeric stop there would 422 the whole save.

Both leaves are ABSENT by default and absence is meaningful — it means
"render exactly as this org rendered before this group existed":

* ``mode`` absent  -> gradient (today's only behaviour).
* ``fromStop`` absent -> no interpolation hint is emitted at all, so the CSS
  is byte-identical to the legacy string (see `buildWidgetCssVars`). The
  50/50 default is therefore expressed as ABSENCE, never as a written 50 —
  existing rows keep rendering without relying on hint-equivalence.

DesignTokenMotion.title: DesignTokenMotion
DesignTokenMotion.description: Interaction motion — one duration (<time>) + one timing-function.

DesignTokenRadius.title: DesignTokenRadius
DesignTokenRadius.description: Border-radius slots (CSS dimensions; launcher is typically 50%).

DesignTokenSpacing.title: DesignTokenSpacing
DesignTokenSpacing.description: Spacing slots — padding shorthand (1-4 dims) and single-dim gaps.

DesignTokenTransform.title: DesignTokenTransform
DesignTokenTransform.description:
RFC Phase E3 — interaction transform SCALES (unitless multipliers).

Motion *timing* (duration + easing) already shipped as `DesignTokenMotion`;
this is the other half of E3. Every leaf is optional and absence means "the
literal `chat-script/src/styles.ts` ships today", so `transform` absent =
byte-identical rendering.

Each leaf carries its OWN range because the ranges are semantic, not
cosmetic: a "grow" interaction above ~1.2 reads as a glitch rather than
feedback, and a "press" interaction must stay at or below 1.0 or the element
grows when pushed.

Rotation is deliberately NOT here. RFC §16 scopes E3 to *scales*, and the
launcher's icon swap uses a ±90deg PAIR that must stay symmetric — one leaf
would invite an asymmetric swap, two would invite a broken one.

DesignTokenTypography.title: DesignTokenTypography
DesignTokenTypography.description: Font family / weights. fontUrl is an optional CSS URL (Google Fonts css2).

autonomy_families.title: Autonomy Families
autonomy_families.description: Map of lane family -> lane (plan_work/outreach/hygiene_and_alerts). Omit to leave family answers untouched; send `{}` to clear them.

DeskAutonomyUpdate.title: DeskAutonomyUpdate
DeskAutonomyUpdate.description:
Which decisions the desk may act on WITHOUT asking the rep first.

A lane of `autopilot` means the desk executes that decision type on the
rep's behalf - including the ones that send. `approve` asks first, `off`
stops the type being raised at all. The app validates both maps against its
own `DecisionType` / `AutonomyLane` / lane-family vocabularies and answers
400 on anything it could not act on, so this surface forwards them as open
maps rather than freezing a copy of three enums that move with the product.

An omitted `autonomy_families` means "I did not touch the family
questions", so a partial save cannot wipe them. An explicit `{}` clears
them and hands every type back to its own lane - the only way back once a
family has been answered.

DeskBatch.title: DeskBatch
DeskBatch.description:
Today's frozen batch.

A batch is FINITE by design: the rep freezes a ranked slice of the queue so
the day has an end. `None` from the app means no batch has been started
today, which is different from a batch with no items left - the response
keeps that distinction rather than flattening both to an empty batch.

item_ids.title: Item Ids
item_ids.description: Decision ids to append. 1-40 - a smaller cap than start, by design.

tz_offset.title: Tz Offset

DeskBatchPullRequest.title: DeskBatchPullRequest
DeskBatchPullRequest.description: Append newly selected cards to today's existing batch.

item_ids.description: Decision ids to freeze into the batch. 1-80 - the cap is the app's.

tz_offset.title: Tz Offset
tz_offset.description: The rep's UTC offset in MINUTES (local = UTC + tz_offset). A batch is scoped to the rep's local day, so a wrong offset returns yesterday's batch or starts a second one.

DeskBatchStartRequest.title: DeskBatchStartRequest
DeskBatchStartRequest.description:
Freeze today's ranked queue into a finite batch.

`item_ids` is typed `list[UUID]`, not `list[str]`, so a malformed id is a
request-validation 422 that NAMES the offending element. Typed as strings,
the app's own `list[UUID]` model raises a pydantic `ValidationError` from
inside the handler body instead - the same class of bare-500 the path
guard exists to prevent, one layer in.

DeskOrgSettingsUpdate.title: DeskOrgSettingsUpdate
DeskOrgSettingsUpdate.description:
Org-level desk settings. PARTIAL - an unset field is left untouched.

Mirrors `desk.interfaces.fastapi.dtos.DeskOrgSettingsUpdate` field for
field, pinned by test, because it is constructed inside the proxy.

THREE KINDS OF FIELD LIVE HERE AND THEY ARE NOT EQUALLY QUIET
---------------------------------------------------------------
Most are thresholds and ids. But `max_auto_account_plans_per_day`,
`max_account_replans_per_day` and `max_skill_plans_per_day` are the org's
DAILY SPEND CAPS on charged model calls, and `desk_acts_on_signals`,
`desk_drafts_with_ai`, `desk_writes_deal_plans`, `reps_may_fire_workflows`
and `stalled_deal_send_email` are the switches that let the desk act - and
email - on its own. That is why this operation is not tiered a plain
`write`; see the router docstring.

Every value is validated by the app's own `validated_payload()` and
`save_desk_org_settings`, which answer 400 with the reason. This surface
does not second-guess either.

DeskPayload.title: DeskPayload
DeskPayload.description:
An open envelope for one desk object.

Open on purpose - see the module docstring. A rebuilder gets every field
the desk returns, including ones added after this contract version.

status.title: Status
status.description: approved, edited, skipped, deferred, snoozed or done_already. A status the app does not accept is a 400 rather than being silently dropped, which is why this is an open string and not an enum this surface would have to keep in lock-step. `done_already` resolves the card AND records the work on its entity.

action_taken.title: Action Taken
action_taken.description: Action payload, e.g. the edited email body.

snoozed_until.title: Snoozed Until

wake_condition.title: Wake Condition
wake_condition.description: Early-wake condition, valid only with status=snoozed: reply | site_visit | stage_change. `snoozed_until` stays required as the fallback timeout. `stage_change` is accepted but only wakes via that timeout today - no deal-stage-change event reaches the desk signal consumer yet.

DeskSendReplyRequest.description:
The rep's reply, as it will arrive in the prospect's inbox.

DeskSendSmsRequest.description:

1600 characters is the app's ceiling, not a display limit - it is the
concatenated-SMS cap, and a longer body is refused rather than truncated.

DialerCallbackRequest.description: The outcome of a dialer call. Mirrors `DialerCallbackPayload`.

DialerNumberInfo.description: One available dialer number with its current health stats.

DialerNumbersListResponse.description:

DialerPayload.description:

Open because voice owns the shape of a session, a call stub and a queue

DialerReportFilters.title: DialerReportFilters
DialerReportFilters.description:

DialerReportMetric.title: DialerReportMetric
DialerReportMetric.description:
One aggregated row in the analytics report.

Schema mirrors ``ParallelDialerMetrics``. The disposition breakdown
is a passthrough dict so that voice-side disposition additions do
not require a coordinated DTO bump here.

from_phone.description: Caller-ID phone number. Must be one of the org's dialer numbers.

list_id.description: Contact list ID the SDR will dial from. Stored in session metadata.

list_title.description: Display title for the list (e.g. 'Q4 ICP'). Stored in metadata.

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: Voice agent UUID. Use GET /voice/dialer/agents to look up.

agent_name.title: Agent Name
agent_name.description: Legacy V1 agent name fallback (defaults to "default_agent" upstream).

entity_type.title: Entity Type
entity_type.description: V2 agent entity type ("agent" or "twin"). Optional.

studio_campaign_id.title: Studio Campaign Id
studio_campaign_id.description: Campaign Builder (Studio) campaign UUID. Optional linkage.

skip_voicemails.title: Skip Voicemails
skip_voicemails.description: Per-session override for voicemail-skip behaviour. None = use SDR default.

parallel_count.title: Parallel Count
parallel_count.description: Legs to dial per batch once the SDR opens the dialer UI (1 = power mode, 2-5 = parallel). None keeps voice's own default (2). Bug fix (graph8-com/g8 dev-API voice parity): this field previously had no effect - it was accepted by neither this DTO nor the upstream call, so any value a caller sent was silently dropped rather than forwarded.

dialing_mode.title: Dialing Mode
dialing_mode.description: Override the session's dialing mode. None keeps voice's default ('power'). Same bug-fix note as parallel_count above - now forwarded instead of dropped.

DialerSessionCreateRequest.title: DialerSessionCreateRequest
DialerSessionCreateRequest.description:
Body for creating a parallel-dialer session in PAUSED state.

The session is created paused so the SDR can open the dialer UI and
start dialing on their own time. Org and user are pinned server-side
from the API key - any value supplied here is ignored.

Required: ``name``, ``from_phone``.
Optional: ``list_id`` / ``list_title`` (carried in session metadata),
``agent_id`` (V2 agent UUID - use ``GET /voice/dialer/agents`` to look up),
``studio_campaign_id`` (Campaign Builder UUID for studio campaign linkage).

DialerSessionCreateResponse.title: DialerSessionCreateResponse
DialerSessionCreateResponse.description:
Echo of the voice service's ``ParallelDialResponse`` for a paused-create.

We deliberately drop ``twilio_token`` from the public shape - it is
SDR-frontend-specific and is regenerated by the dialer UI on join, so
re-publishing it here would only confuse a chat caller.

max_contacts.title: Max Contacts
max_contacts.description: Number of contacts to dial in this batch. Voice caps parallel dialing at 4.

DialerSessionResumeRequest.title: DialerSessionResumeRequest
DialerSessionResumeRequest.description:
Body for resuming a paused parallel-dialer session.

The resume endpoint mirrors what the dialer UI does when the SDR
clicks "Start Dialing" on a paused session: it pages the source list
using the cursor stored in ``session_metadata``, filters out
already-called contacts, and forwards the next batch to the voice
service's ``start-session`` endpoint.

Only ``max_contacts`` is exposed - org / user / from_phone /
list_id / agent / session_metadata are all read off the persisted
session so the caller doesn't have to reconstruct them.

DialerSessionResumeResponse.title: DialerSessionResumeResponse
DialerSessionResumeResponse.description:
Echo of voice's ``ParallelDialResponse`` plus a count of contacts dialed.

``dialed_count`` is the number of calls actually placed in this
resume batch. It can be lower than ``max_contacts`` when the list is
near exhausted, every remaining row is missing a phone, or every
candidate was already called earlier in the session.

``twilio_token`` and ``conference_name`` are deliberately dropped -
they are SDR-frontend specific and an MCP / API caller has no use
for them. The dialer UI regenerates them on join.

DialerSessionStatusUpdateRequest.title: DialerSessionStatusUpdateRequest
DialerSessionStatusUpdateRequest.description:
Body for pause / resume / stop on a parallel-dialer session.

The voice service treats a status PATCH as the lifecycle hook:
- ``ACTIVE`` resumes a paused session.
- ``PAUSED`` pauses an active session.
- ``COMPLETED`` ends the session - one-way, can be re-opened only via
  ``manual-dial`` (which we do not expose here).
- ``FAILED`` is reserved for system use; we reject it on the public
  surface so a caller cannot mis-mark a session.

DialerSessionStatusUpdateResponse.title: DialerSessionStatusUpdateResponse
DialerSessionStatusUpdateResponse.description: Echo of voice's ``SessionUpdateResponse`` for the public surface.

DialerSessionSummary.title: DialerSessionSummary
DialerSessionSummary.description:
One row from the dialer-sessions list.

The voice service returns a flat dict per session built from
``ParallelDialSession`` columns plus an aggregated ``contact_ids``
array. We surface every documented column directly so that read-only
consumers can introspect a session without a follow-up call.

DialerSessionsListResponse.title: DialerSessionsListResponse
DialerSessionsListResponse.description:
List wrapper for dialer sessions.

Top-level matches the voice payload (``data`` + ``pagination``) so the
public API caller sees the exact same shape they would get if voice
were exposed directly. The standard ``ApiResponse`` envelope wraps
THIS object as its ``data`` field.

DialerSettingsUpdate.description: voice `DialerSettingsRequest`, without `org_id`. Only fields sent change.

DialerStatsResponse.description:
Top-level wrapper for dialer analytics.

Field names follow the voice ``ParallelDialerReport`` shape so the
structured response is meaningful both to a Developer API caller and
to an MCP agent rendering it inline.

DiscoveryRatifyRequest.description:

DiscoveryTurnRequest.title: DiscoveryTurnRequest
DiscoveryTurnRequest.description:
Mirror of `DiscoveryTurnRequest`.

There is deliberately NO `history` field, and that is load-bearing rather
than an omission. The app removed one: the panel used to keep the
transcript in browser state and ship it back on every turn, so a reload
destroyed the customer's whole kickoff. The server re-grounds from the
durable record instead. A caller-supplied transcript is not something the
server can verify, and accepting one here would re-open exactly that hole.

DnsRecordsRequest.description: Set the sending DNS records (SPF/DKIM/MX/tracking CNAME) for a domain.

feedback_type.description: Thumbs up or thumbs down on the document.

DocumentFeedbackRequest.description:

DocumentListPayload.description:
An open envelope for a LIST result, so a bare list keeps its shape.

DocumentPayload.title: DocumentPayload

An open envelope for one document, folder or questionnaire.

questionnaire carries per-provider processing detail, and a generated deal
document carries `structured_data` and `highlights` whose shape is the
generator's rather than this contract's. Pinning those would silently drop
whatever the app learned to return that this file had not caught up on.

DocumentPriorityUpdateRequest.title: DocumentPriorityUpdateRequest
DocumentPriorityUpdateRequest.description:
Mirrors `UpdateDocumentPrioritySettingsRequest`.

Both fields have defaults, so a partial body silently RESETS the field you
left out to the product default rather than leaving it alone. Send both.

DocumentRevertRequest.title: DocumentRevertRequest
DocumentRevertRequest.description: Optional note recorded on the revert's own version.

FilterGroupDto.title: FilterGroupDto
FilterGroupDto.description:
One filter group — list of values + optional NOT toggle.

``in_`` is capped at ``MAX_FILTER_VALUES_PER_GROUP`` items of
``MAX_FILTER_VALUE_LENGTH`` characters each. Over-cap input raises during
body parsing, so FastAPI answers 422 with the offending group named in
``detail[].loc`` (``["body", "<group>", "in"]``) and the cap in
``detail[].msg`` — no handler code, and therefore no SQL, runs.

THIS SHAPE DOES NOT NEST. ``in_`` holds scalars and there is no
group-of-groups member, so a caller cannot vary the tree depth: it is fixed
at 2 (query -> group -> values) by construction, and ``extra="forbid"`` on
both models keeps it that way. A depth check here would be validation that
can never fire. Add one WITH the member that introduces nesting, not before
it.

Do not confuse this with ``SegmentFilterGroup``
(``contacts/domain/value_objects/ag_grid_models.py:111``), which IS
recursive and is where AC-3's "tree depth" belongs. Different model,
different route, still unbounded — see the scope note above the constants.

FilterOptionsRequest.title: FilterOptionsRequest
FilterOptionsRequest.description:
Ask what values a set of fields holds, narrowed by a search.

Mirrors the app's `FilteredFilterOptionsRequest` in substance - `fields`
plus an ICP query - but in the PUBLISHED vocabulary.

It SUBCLASSES the published `SearchRequest` rather than restating its
fields, so `filters`, `page` and `limit` cannot drift away from the search
they are meant to describe: a body that works against
`POST /search/contacts` works here with two fields added.

`filters` must be non-empty. That is not this contract being fussy - it is
the same refusal `POST /search/contacts` makes, because an unfiltered
request scans the entire open-data index.

FilterPredicate.title: FilterPredicate
FilterPredicate.description:
One clause of a queue filter. `conditions` nests for AND/OR groups.

`conditions` is typed as a list of plain objects rather than as a list of
`FilterPredicate`, ON PURPOSE. Voice's own model IS recursive, and this
one was too, which made it the only self-referencing schema in the
published contract - and the developer-docs renderer recurses on a
self-referencing schema with no depth limit until Node runs out of memory
(`verify-help-docs` and `User help coverage and rendering` both died with
exit 134 on every head that carried it). The wire format is unchanged:
each entry has this same shape (`field`, `op`, `value`, `values`,
`conditions`) and is forwarded to voice as-is, which validates it against
its recursive model. The parity test compares field NAMES, so it still
pins this model to voice's.

MeetingSensitivityRequest.title: MeetingSensitivityRequest
MeetingSensitivityRequest.description:
WHO MAY READ THE RECORDING OF THIS MEETING.

`private` restricts the transcript to the meeting's participants.
`normal` makes it visible to the organisation again - so moving a meeting
from `private` back to `normal` EXPOSES a transcript that was restricted,
and nobody who reads it in the meantime can be made to un-read it.

The app takes a bare `Dict[str, str]` here and defaults a MISSING or
misspelled key to `"normal"`. That default is the exposing direction, so
this contract makes the value REQUIRED and closed: a typo is a 422 naming
both options rather than a silent un-restrict.

MeetingTaskUpdateRequest.title: MeetingTaskUpdateRequest
MeetingTaskUpdateRequest.description:
Patch a meeting task.

NULLABLE FIELDS ARE THREE-STATE, and that is the whole point of PATCH here:

  * field absent from the body        -> leave unchanged
  * field present and `null`          -> clear it (unassign / drop due date)
  * field present with a value        -> set it (reassignment is re-validated)

The proxy forwards with `exclude_unset=True` so the app's own
`model_fields_set` check still distinguishes "sent null" from "not sent".
Dumping every field would turn every PATCH into a full overwrite that
cleared whatever the caller did not mention.

agg.title: Agg
agg.description: Metric values keyed by alias, e.g. {"count": 1247, "unique_domains": 1184}.

field.title: Field

alias.title: Alias

OpenSearchAggSpec.title: OpenSearchAggSpec
OpenSearchAggSpec.description:
A single aggregate metric over the grouped rows.

``count`` needs no field (it is the bucket doc count). All other functions
require ``field``. ``alias`` keys the value in each group's ``agg`` map;
it defaults to ``function`` when omitted (so two same-function metrics must
each carry a distinct ``alias``).

index.title: Index
index.description: Logical index to aggregate. Maps to a whitelisted physical alias.

filters.title: Filters
filters.description: Pre-aggregation equality filters, identical semantics to /opensearch/search. RAW UPPERCASE field names.

group_by.title: Group By
group_by.description: 1-3 RAW UPPERCASE keyword fields to group on (e.g. ["COMPANY_NAICS", "COMPANY_STATE"]). Must be keyword-type fields -- the canonical COMPANY_* firmographics are. Capped at 3 dimensions to bound cluster cost. ORDER HIGHEST-CARDINALITY FIRST: deeper dimensions get smaller per-level bucket caps (1000 / 100 / 20), so a low-cardinality field placed last keeps full fidelity while a high-cardinality field placed last may be truncated.

agg.title: Agg
agg.description: Metrics to compute per group (max 10). Defaults to a single `count` when omitted.

having.title: Having
having.description: Post-aggregation group filter keyed by metric alias, e.g. {"count": {"gte": 50}}. Operators: eq, gte, lte, gt, lt.

sort.title: Sort
sort.description: Sort the returned groups by a metric alias, e.g. [{"count": "desc"}]. Applied after `having`.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Max number of groups returned (after having + sort). Hard-capped at 1000.

OpenSearchAggregateRequest.title: OpenSearchAggregateRequest
OpenSearchAggregateRequest.description:
Generic, allowlist-bounded GROUP BY over a whitelisted mashup index.

Translates to nested OpenSearch ``terms`` aggregations (one level per
``group_by`` field) with metric sub-aggregations. ``having`` / ``sort`` /
``limit`` are applied to the flattened groups server-side. Counts from
``terms`` buckets / ``cardinality`` are APPROXIMATE on a sharded index.

index.title: Index
index.description: Logical index to count. Maps to a whitelisted physical alias.

filters.title: Filters
filters.description: Field equality filters, identical semantics to /opensearch/search. Scalar -> term, list -> terms (OR). RAW UPPERCASE field names (e.g. COMPANY_INDUSTRY, COMPANY_NAICS, COMPANY_COUNTRY).

OpenSearchCountRequest.title: OpenSearchCountRequest
OpenSearchCountRequest.description:
Exact-count request. Same ``index`` + ``filters`` shape as search; the
page-oriented fields (fields/sort/limit/cursor) are intentionally absent
because a count returns no rows.

ids.title: Ids
ids.description: Up to 500 input IDs (HEMs or IPs).

index.title: Index
index.description: Logical index to search. Maps to a whitelisted physical alias.

filters.title: Filters
filters.description: Field equality filters. Scalar value -> term, list -> terms (OR). Use this to narrow by COMPANY_DOMAIN, COMPANY_INDUSTRY, hem, etc. Field names are the RAW index fields (UPPERCASE, e.g. COMPANY_INDUSTRY) -- not the friendly snake_case names used by /search.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Optional projection. If omitted, returns the full _source. Pass a list to reduce payload size when the LLM only needs a few columns.

sort.title: Sort
sort.description: Optional sort, list of `{field: 'asc'|'desc'}`. Required if you intend to paginate via cursor.

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.description: search_after token returned from a prior page. Pair with `sort`.

track_total_hits.title: Track Total Hits
track_total_hits.description: Exact-count ceiling for the returned `total`. OMIT for the default behaviour (OpenSearch saturates `total` at 10000). Pass an integer ceiling 1-1000000 (e.g. 100000) to get an exact `total` up to that bound in the SAME round trip as the page. For a count with no page payload prefer POST /opensearch/count. Does NOT lift the from+size pagination depth -- use `cursor` (search_after) for that. (0 is rejected: it would mean 'disable tracking' in OpenSearch, which is what omitting it does.)

override.title: Override
override.description: The organisation's operating-model override, REPLACED WHOLE. This is a PUT: keys absent from the body are removed, not left alone. Read `GET /agent/operators/operating-model` first and send it back modified.

OperatingModelRequest.title: OperatingModelRequest
OperatingModelRequest.description:
Mirror of `OperatingModelUpdate`.

`override` is an open object and stays that way. It is the organisation's
operating-model document - which motions it runs, what it calls them - and
it is validated by the service against the live model definition rather
than by a shape frozen into this contract. Pinning it would refuse a key a
newer platform version understands.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: `approved` EXECUTES the finding's proposed fix against your data; `rejected` records the decision and executes nothing.

params.title: Params
params.description: Values a fix needs that the operator could not decide for you, e.g. `{"target_user": "<user id>"}`. Omit for a fully-specified fix. A value the fix refuses is a 400 naming the field, and the task stays open.

OperatorApprovalDecisionRequest.title: OperatorApprovalDecisionRequest
OperatorApprovalDecisionRequest.description:
Mirror of `ApprovalDecision`.

`resolution` is closed to the two values the app accepts. The app answers
anything else with a 400 after lower-casing it; closing it here makes a bad
value a 422 that names the valid ones.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether this operator runs for the organisation. TURNING IT ON STARTS UNATTENDED WORK: the operator's monitors run on their own schedule from then on, without a person asking. Explicit rather than a toggle, so a retried request is idempotent instead of flipping the state back.

OperatorListPayload.title: OperatorListPayload
OperatorListPayload.description: An open envelope for a LIST answer, so a bare list keeps its shape.

OperatorPayload.title: OperatorPayload
OperatorPayload.description:
An open envelope for one operator answer.

Open because an operator's health snapshot, scorecard and catalog are
per-operator documents whose shape follows what that operator monitors -
the revenue operator reports different checks from the deliverability one,
and both grow. On an OVERSIGHT surface a dropped field reads as "nothing to
worry about" rather than "we did not tell you", which is the failure mode
worth designing against.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The person who receives this operator's alerts and owns its approval tasks. One recipient per operator: setting it REPLACES whoever was there.

autonomy.title: Autonomy
autonomy.description: How far this skill may go on its own. `OFF` - do not run it. `DETECT` - look, and record what it finds. `PROPOSE` - look, and raise an approval task a person decides. `AUTO` - act and log, with no human in the loop. THIS IS A REQUEST, NOT A GUARANTEE: the effective level is the MINIMUM of this dial, the skill's own graph8-managed risk cap and the platform ceiling, so a skill capped at `PROPOSE` stays at `PROPOSE` however this is set. Read the response, and `GET /agent/operators/{operator}/skills`, for what the dial actually resolved to.

OperatorTrustDialRequest.title: OperatorTrustDialRequest
OperatorTrustDialRequest.description: Mirror of `TrustDialUpdate`, with `autonomy` closed to the shipped set.

resume_url.title: Resume Url
resume_url.description: Omit to use your profile resume.

OpportunityApplyRequest.title: OpportunityApplyRequest
OpportunityApplyRequest.description:
Easy-apply to a published role.

`resume_url` defaults to the resume already on your profile; with neither,
the app refuses with a 422 naming the missing resume.

note.title: Note
note.description: Connection-request note, POST-RENDER. Null is the NORM for bare-invite plays (intentional strategy) — never report a null note as missing data.

message_text.title: Message Text
message_text.description: Rendered message body. Null for INVITE rows by design.

degree_observed.title: Degree Observed
degree_observed.description: Connection degree arlink observed; only set after a provider round-trip.

failure_reason.title: Failure Reason
failure_reason.description: COALESCE of the executed-step skip_reason (richer) and the queue row's last_error. `skipped_too_distant` = target not 1st/2nd-degree reachable — an ELIGIBILITY skip, not a provider error or account-health problem.

contact_seq_state.title: Contact Seq State
contact_seq_state.description: seqsequencecontacts.state. `waiting_netrion` = parked with a live queue row outstanding. `skipped` = channel skip (e.g. no LinkedIn URL), NOT a send.

OpsActionRow.title: OpsActionRow
OpsActionRow.description: One `linkedin_action_queue` row with its full per-contact drill-down.

OpsActionSummaryRow.title: OpsActionSummaryRow
OpsActionSummaryRow.description: One cell of the sequence × sender × kind × status matrix.

OpsIndex.title: OpsIndex
OpsIndex.description:
Self-describing index so an LLM consumer can discover the surface
without parsing the full OpenAPI document.

account_status.title: Account Status
account_status.description: OK = healthy. Only `deletedAt IS NULL AND status='OK'` counts as connected.

contact_state_counts.title: Contact State Counts
contact_state_counts.description: seqsequencecontacts states for this sequence. Absent state = 0. `waiting_netrion` is the in-flight park state.

OpsUnboundSequenceRow.title: OpsUnboundSequenceRow
OpsUnboundSequenceRow.description:
A live, non-archived sequence with a NETRION step but NO active channel
binding — configured but can never send. This is the population behind
'connected but not sending'.

OpsWebhookEventSummary.title: OpsWebhookEventSummary
OpsWebhookEventSummary.description:
Per-event-type aggregate. The events table stores NO payload (dedupe
ledger only) — to learn *what happened*, read the effects instead:
`linkedin_action_queue.status` and the contact's sequencer state.

`inbox.message_received` is NOT a sequence reply — only `lead.message_received`
carries reply semantics. Never conflate the two counts.

OrderSpec.title: OrderSpec
OrderSpec.description: The order the queue is worked in, and which phone field is tried first.

OrgCostSettingsRequest.title: OrgCostSettingsRequest
OrgCostSettingsRequest.description: Labour cost per rep and the commission model. REPLACES the stored config.

OrgDeliverabilityProtectionRequest.title: OrgDeliverabilityProtectionRequest
OrgDeliverabilityProtectionRequest.description: Which high-risk content categories are blocked before a send.

OrgDepartmentsUpdateRequest.title: OrgDepartmentsUpdateRequest
OrgDepartmentsUpdateRequest.description: The department taxonomy. REPLACES the whole list.

OrgDialerTargetsRequest.title: OrgDialerTargetsRequest
OrgDialerTargetsRequest.description:
Org-wide daily goals. Voice takes these as QUERY params; they are a
body here because they are a record being written, not a filter.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` to fetch the next (older) page. Null when there are no more.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: Whether another page exists within the requested window.

since.title: Since
since.description: Lower bound of the window that was searched (ISO 8601, UTC).

until.title: Until
until.description: Upper bound of the window that was searched (ISO 8601, UTC).

OrgEventFeedPage.title: OrgEventFeedPage
OrgEventFeedPage.description: A page of events, newest first.

id.title: Id
id.description: Event uid. Stable across reads; use it to de-duplicate.

type.title: Type
type.description: Event family, e.g. sequencer, inbox, voiceai, appointments, crm, deals, quotes, newsletter, uui, mcp, internal. Web-tracking rows carry the tracker's type (e.g. page).

name.title: Name
name.description: Event name, e.g. sequence_email_sent, inbox.email_received, sdr.call_ended, booking_created.

actor_email.title: Actor Email
actor_email.description: The event's context email: the acting user, recipient or a system actor address.

contact_id.title: Contact Id
contact_id.description: message.contact_id, when the event carries one.

sequence_id.title: Sequence Id
sequence_id.description: message.sequence_id, when the event carries one.

campaign_id.title: Campaign Id
campaign_id.description: message.campaign_id, when the event carries one.

message.title: Message
message.description: The event payload exactly as produced.

OrgEventItem.title: OrgEventItem
OrgEventItem.description: One event from the org's event store.

OrgGovernancePayload.title: OrgGovernancePayload
OrgGovernancePayload.description: A settings view or the result of a change, as the app returns it.

OrgListPayload.title: OrgListPayload
OrgListPayload.description:
An open envelope for a LIST result, so a bare list keeps its shape.

Most of these handlers return a bare `list[...]`; a few return a named
envelope (`{"team_members": [...], "total": n}`). Both are reachable as
`items`, and a named envelope KEEPS its own key as well so a caller
already reading the app's shape is not broken by the wrapper.

OrgMeetingUpdateRequest.title: OrgMeetingUpdateRequest
OrgMeetingUpdateRequest.description:
The client's edit of a meeting its hire ran. Unset fields are untouched.

Setting `status` to `taken` is the BILLING SIGNAL: that row becomes
chargeable at the engagement's per-meeting rate, and the talent is notified.
Moving `meeting_date` without a `status` flips the row to `rescheduled`.
Both vocabularies are closed here so a typo is a 422 naming the valid values
rather than the app's 400.

OrgOutboundTrackingRequest.title: OrgOutboundTrackingRequest
OrgOutboundTrackingRequest.description: UTM tagging of outbound links, per channel.

OrgPayload.title: OrgPayload
OrgPayload.description:
An open envelope for a single role, team, member or account record.

Open on purpose. The app's own response models on this surface grow with
the product - `RoleResponse` gained `rep_limits` and `manages_role_slugs`,
`TeamResponse` gained channel counts and a campaign count - and a pinned
mirror would SILENTLY DROP whatever it had not caught up on. A dropped
permission in a role read is the worst possible kind of stale: it reads as
"they do not have it".

org_name.title: Org Name
org_name.description: Organization display name. PropelAuth owns it; a rejected rename aborts the whole update.

email_domain.title: Email Domain
email_domain.description: Email domain for auto-join signup (e.g. `graph8.com`). Anyone who signs up with an address at this domain joins this organization with no invite. Normalised: scheme, `www.` and trailing slash are stripped and the value is lowercased.

OrgSettingsUpdateRequest.title: OrgSettingsUpdateRequest
OrgSettingsUpdateRequest.description:
Mirrors `campaign_builder.routers.org_settings.UpdateOrgSettingsRequest`.

`email_domain` is the auto-join domain: anyone signing up with an address
at that domain joins THIS organisation without an invite. It is the widest
blast radius on this surface, which is why the route is admin-gated and the
handler re-checks the caller's org role on top.

OrgVideoPayload.title: OrgVideoPayload
OrgVideoPayload.description: A library video. `generation` carries render progress for generated videos.

copy.title: Copy
copy.description: Copy slot id -> text. The `plain` template renders none.

OutboundTrackingChannels.title: OutboundTrackingChannels
OutboundTrackingChannels.description:
Per-channel UTM injection toggles. email, linkedin, and whatsapp are
wired into their send paths; sms/voice/dialer use booking-link tokens.

OutputColumnDef.title: OutputColumnDef
OutputColumnDef.description: One column an AI pass writes into.

OutreachAddLeadsRequest.title: OutreachAddLeadsRequest
OutreachAddLeadsRequest.description:
People to add to an outreach lead list.

Each object is one person. `linkedInUrl`, `firstName` and `lastName` are the
fields that matter; `companyName`, `position` and similar are passed through.

campaign_id.title: Campaign Id
campaign_id.description: Ignored; the path value is used.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Page size. Values above 1000 are capped at 1000.

OutreachCampaignLeadsQuery.title: OutreachCampaignLeadsQuery
OutreachCampaignLeadsQuery.description:
Page through the people in one campaign. Reads only.

`campaign_id` exists because the app's model has it; the PATH value is
authoritative and overwrites whatever is sent here.

OutreachConnectionStatus.title: OutreachConnectionStatus
OutreachConnectionStatus.description: Whether the org's outreach connection exists and its session is healthy. Never the credentials.

OutreachListCreateRequest.title: OutreachListCreateRequest
OutreachListCreateRequest.description: A new, empty lead list on the outreach platform.

OutreachReconnectResult.title: OutreachReconnectResult
OutreachReconnectResult.description: Outcome of refreshing the session. `requires_login: true` means a person must sign in again in the app.

OutreachSenderAccount.title: OutreachSenderAccount
OutreachSenderAccount.description: A LinkedIn account that sends outreach.

OutreachSequenceMapping.title: OutreachSequenceMapping
OutreachSequenceMapping.description: The outreach campaign and list a graph8 sequence runs through.

OutreachStepCampaigns.title: OutreachStepCampaigns
OutreachStepCampaigns.description: Keyed by sequence step id. Steps with no campaign are absent.

OutreachWorkspaceSelectRequest.title: OutreachWorkspaceSelectRequest
OutreachWorkspaceSelectRequest.description: Which workspace this org sends from. ONE-TIME: it cannot be changed once set.

OutreachWorkspaceState.title: OutreachWorkspaceState
OutreachWorkspaceState.description: The workspace this org sends from, if one is selected.

OutreachWorkspaces.title: OutreachWorkspaces
OutreachWorkspaces.description: Selectable workspaces. Empty once one is selected - `current_workspace_id` then says which.

url.title: Url
url.description: Canonical PAGE_URL, e.g. 'cognism.com/pricing' (no scheme, no www).

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; null when there are no more items. Pass it back as the `cursor` query param to fetch the following page without computing page numbers.

PasteImportRequest.title: PasteImportRequest
PasteImportRequest.description: Import a rectangle of values - the paste path, no file involved.

value.title: Value
value.description: New value. Null CLEARS the cell.

expected_value.title: Expected Value
expected_value.description: Refuse the write unless the cell still holds this. Omit to force.

PatchDynamicValueRequest.title: PatchDynamicValueRequest
PatchDynamicValueRequest.description:
Write one cell of a user-owned dynamic column.

`expected_value` is an optimistic-concurrency check: send what you believe
is there and the write is refused if it has moved. Omit it and the write
wins unconditionally, which on a shared grid means overwriting a
colleague's edit without knowing.

PatchIdeaRequest.title: PatchIdeaRequest
PatchIdeaRequest.description:
Card actions on a mined idea. Spends nothing.

PARTIAL: an absent field is untouched, a field sent as NULL is CLEARED.
Those are different instructions and only the second one erases.

is_active.title: Is Active
is_active.description: False pauses polling without deleting the listener.

PatchListenerRequest.title: PatchListenerRequest
PatchListenerRequest.description:
Partial update. Omitted fields are left alone.

Changing `target_handle` on a `user` listener re-resolves the account
against the platform, which consumes X API quota.

alert_threshold_pct.title: Alert Threshold Pct
alert_threshold_pct.description: Alert at this percentage of the cap.

auto_pause_on_cap.title: Auto Pause On Cap
auto_pause_on_cap.description: Stop polling when the cap is reached, rather than alerting.

other_channels_monthly_credit_cap.title: Other Channels Monthly Credit Cap
other_channels_monthly_credit_cap.description: Org-wide monthly credit ceiling across the non-X channels (LinkedIn, Reddit, Instagram, YouTube) together. 0 means no org-wide ceiling; the per-channel caps in `channel_settings` still apply.

channel_settings.title: Channel Settings
channel_settings.description: Keyed by platform. Keys the app does not recognise are dropped by its own merge - it rebuilds the map from the supported set.

PatchSocialSettingsRequest.title: PatchSocialSettingsRequest
PatchSocialSettingsRequest.description:
Org-wide social listening settings. Omitted fields are left alone.

This is the surface that BOUNDS what the whole feature costs -
`monthly_credit_cap`, the per-channel caps and `auto_pause_on_cap` between
them decide whether an over-eager listener can keep spending.

PaymentSchedulePreviewRequest.title: PaymentSchedulePreviewRequest
PaymentSchedulePreviewRequest.description:
Compute the payment schedule a set of line items WOULD produce.

Reads nothing and writes nothing - it is arithmetic over the body, which
is why it is POST but tiered `read`.

website_url.title: Website Url
website_url.description: Stored on any persona row this creates. Optional: the committees view is org-wide and does not filter on it.

website_url.title: Website Url
website_url.description: The website the personas are researched from.

save_to_database.title: Save To Database
save_to_database.description: Persist the generated personas. False returns a preview only.

PersonaLensRequest.title: PersonaLensRequest
PersonaLensRequest.description:
Read the ad through a persona's eyes. SPENDS CREDIT.

Read-only against the creative - it returns a critique and changes
nothing - but a model still runs, so it still costs.

organization_id.title: Organization Id
organization_id.description: Ignored. The organisation is the API key's own.

PersonaRecommendationRequest.title: PersonaRecommendationRequest
PersonaRecommendationRequest.description:
Recommend target personas from the company's own data. SPENDS CREDIT.

`organization_id` is IGNORED - the org always comes from the key. It is
mirrored because the app's model carries it, and dropping a field a caller
sends would be a silent 422 on a body Studio itself produces.

fact_ids.title: Fact Ids
fact_ids.description: The people (wiki facts) this choice applies to.

connection_revisions.title: Connection Revisions
connection_revisions.description: Per-connection revision tokens, keyed by connection id (UUID).

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: `private` keeps these people to yourself, `shared` offers them to the org's CRM, `default` follows the mailbox-level setting.

expected_revision.title: Expected Revision
expected_revision.description: Concurrency token from the sharing GET.

fact_ids.title: Fact Ids
fact_ids.description: The facts being re-attributed, all to the same person.

contact_id.title: Contact Id
contact_id.description: Who they are really about. NULL DETACHES them from whoever they are attributed to now, rather than being ignored - it is how you say 'this is not about anyone in the CRM'.

expected_version.title: Expected Version
expected_version.description: Optimistic-concurrency token for the relationship record.

contact_id.title: Contact Id
contact_id.description: The CRM contact this contribution is actually about.

expected_canonical_revision.title: Expected Canonical Revision
expected_canonical_revision.description: Digest of the CANONICAL contact record as you read it. Two tokens are required because two records are in play: the contribution and the contact it would change. Either moving means the decision was made against something that no longer holds.

choice.title: Choice
choice.description: `keep_current` - the CRM record wins. `use_proposed` - the contributed value wins and overwrites it.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether what this mailbox knows about a contact is contributed to the organisation's shared CRM record. Explicit rather than a toggle, so a retry is idempotent instead of switching it back.

expected_revision.title: Expected Revision
expected_revision.description: REQUIRED optimistic-concurrency token. Sharing settings decide whether one person's private contact knowledge becomes org-wide, so there is no unconditional write: a blind one could re-enable sharing somebody had just turned off.

id.title: Id
id.description: Drive folder id, as returned by `GET /copilot/personal-wiki/drive`.

auto_sync.title: Auto Sync
auto_sync.description: Keep reading new documents added to this folder later, not just today's.

mailbox_id.title: Mailbox Id
mailbox_id.description: Integer `mailboxes.id` of the connected Google account.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: The sources' `updated_at` from `GET /copilot/personal-wiki/sources`. A mismatch is a 409: someone else changed the selection since you read it.

preview_fingerprint.title: Preview Fingerprint
preview_fingerprint.description: The `fingerprint` from the preview call. When sent, the save is refused (409) if the selection no longer resolves to what you previewed.

expected_revision.title: Expected Revision
expected_revision.description: The `revision` from the GET. A stale value is a 409.

keep_updated.title: Keep Updated
keep_updated.description: Re-import the connection list on a schedule.

share.title: Share
share.description: Offer what is learned from these connections to the shared CRM (reviewed first).

start.title: Start
start.description: Start an import now, rather than only saving the settings.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why. Optional, and worth sending on a forget: it is the only record of why something was removed from what the Copilot knows.

PersonalWikiFactActionRequest.title: PersonalWikiFactActionRequest
PersonalWikiFactActionRequest.description: Mirror of `PersonalWikiFactActionRequest` - used by confirm and forget.

text.title: Text
text.description: What is actually true. Replaces the fact's text.

action_state.title: Action State
action_state.description: For a fact the Copilot is tracking as a TO-DO rather than as a statement, move it to this state at the same time. Omit it for an ordinary correction.

PersonalWikiFactCorrectionRequest.title: PersonalWikiFactCorrectionRequest
PersonalWikiFactCorrectionRequest.description:
Mirror of `PersonalWikiFactCorrectionRequest`.

The app declares it as a SUBCLASS of the action request and restates the
inherited fields. Flattened here because a generated SDK renders
inheritance as a separate schema for no benefit, and the parity test
compares the RESOLVED field set, which is identical.

expected_revision.title: Expected Revision
expected_revision.description: REQUIRED optimistic-concurrency token - a 64-character digest of the document you read. There is no unconditional write here, on purpose: the wiki is edited by the Copilot as well as by people, so a blind write would silently discard something it had just learned.

values.title: Values
values.description: Field-by-field replacement for this item. Open-shaped because the item schema is per-section and defined by the wiki template.

primary_mailbox_id.title: Primary Mailbox Id
primary_mailbox_id.description: The mailbox the wiki draws its email signal from.

email_enabled.title: Email Enabled
email_enabled.description: Whether the Copilot reads your email to build the wiki. Turning this off stops new facts arriving from email; it does not remove what it already learned - use `POST /copilot/personal-wiki/forget` for that.

PersonalWikiSourcesUpdateRequest.title: PersonalWikiSourcesUpdateRequest
PersonalWikiSourcesUpdateRequest.description:
Mirror of `PersonalWikiSourcesUpdateRequest`.

PARTIAL: the handler applies `exclude_unset`, so an omitted field is left
alone and an explicit value changes it. Sending `email_enabled: false` is
not the same instruction as omitting it.

content.title: Content
content.description: The WHOLE wiki document. Replaces what is there.

PhoneA2pStatusPayload.title: PhoneA2pStatusPayload
PhoneA2pStatusPayload.description: The org's A2P brand and campaign registration state.

PhoneDirectoryEntryCreate.title: PhoneDirectoryEntryCreate
PhoneDirectoryEntryCreate.description:
A colleague the receptionist and the in-call transfer picker can reach.

`extension` and `phone_number` are both optional: the number a transfer
actually dials is resolved from the work-number inventory first, and the
stored `phone_number` is only the hand-entered override.

PhoneNumberPayload.title: PhoneNumberPayload
PhoneNumberPayload.description:
An open envelope for a purchase result, a release, or an A2P job.

Open on purpose. A purchase returns the stored row (whose capability and
provider-metadata keys differ per provider), a workflow start returns a
`workflow_id`, and the A2P reconcile returns per-number outcomes that grow
as carriers add statuses. Pinning it would silently drop whatever the
provider reported that this contract had not caught up on.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: The carrier to search - the same values `POST /phone-numbers/purchase` takes.

pattern.title: Pattern
pattern.description: Digits or a phrase the number must contain.

locality.title: Locality
locality.description: City. Use this or `pattern`, not both.

PlanMediaEntry.title: PlanMediaEntry
PlanMediaEntry.description:
One media slot inside a plan section.

``locked=True`` marks items the user explicitly attached (no swap
affordance in the UI). AI-picked items default to ``locked=False``
and can be swapped before approval.

PlanSection.title: PlanSection
PlanSection.description: One section of the landing-page plan.

poll_interval_sec.title: Poll Interval Sec
poll_interval_sec.description: The interval to cost. Shorter intervals cost more.

PreviewCostRequest.title: PreviewCostRequest
PreviewCostRequest.description: Ask what a listener WOULD cost. Charges nothing.

rule_name.title: Rule Name
rule_name.description: Name for the rule being previewed.

template.title: Template
template.description: Platform rule template the rule is built from.

match_mode.title: Match Mode
match_mode.description: How two values are considered equal.

score.title: Score
score.description: Override the platform default score for this rule.

PreviewDetectionRuleRequest.title: PreviewDetectionRuleRequest
PreviewDetectionRuleRequest.description:
Dry-run a duplicate-detection rule. Writes nothing.

Returns how many pairs the rule would match plus a small sample, which is
the only way to size a rule before auto-merge starts acting on it.

PreviewKeywordUrlsRequest.title: PreviewKeywordUrlsRequest
PreviewKeywordUrlsRequest.description: What a keyword WOULD match, without creating it.

PreviewRoutingRequest.title: PreviewRoutingRequest
PreviewRoutingRequest.description: Count what a routing rule WOULD move, without moving anything.

rendered.description: Spintax-resolved view of this step's copy. Populated for template steps that carry subject/body. Null for ON_DEMAND steps, whose copy is written by the AI at send time rather than stored here.

PrewarmVoicemailsRequest.title: PrewarmVoicemailsRequest
PrewarmVoicemailsRequest.description:
Mirrors `DialerPrewarmRequest` minus `org_id`.

SYNTHESISES voicemail audio ahead of time. Contacts nobody, but it is real
text-to-speech work per contact, which is why it is not a plain write.
Voice caps the batch at 20 and that cap is mirrored here so an oversized
batch is a 422 from this API rather than a round-trip.

ProductSettingsUpdateRequest.title: ProductSettingsUpdateRequest
ProductSettingsUpdateRequest.description: How a Stripe product appears in the quote builder. Omitted fields are unchanged.

sync_interval_minutes.title: Sync Interval Minutes
sync_interval_minutes.description: How often the calendar is pulled, in minutes.

pipelines.title: Pipelines
pipelines.description: Rules per pipeline id. Only the pipelines sent are changed; the others, and other people's rules, are never touched.

ProfileDealAutomationsUpdateRequest.title: ProfileDealAutomationsUpdateRequest
ProfileDealAutomationsUpdateRequest.description:
Mirrors `user_profile.DealAutomationsUpdateRequest`.

`sync_interval_minutes` is closed to `SYNC_INTERVAL_CHOICES`. The app's own
validator raises a ValueError for anything else, which - raised while the
proxy builds the app model - would escape as a 500.

website_url.title: Website Url
website_url.description: The org's website - the profile's key.

fields.title: Fields

QuestionNoteRequest.description:
