mashup_company_id.description: Company to link the new contact to.

QuoteContactCreateRequest.title: QuoteContactCreateRequest
QuoteContactCreateRequest.description:
The full CRM contact form for a quote's SIGNER.

Distinct from the billing contact below, which is a finance contact and
takes name and email only. This one links the new contact to the deal and
the company so it is immediately usable as the signer.

QuoteCreateRequest.title: QuoteCreateRequest
QuoteCreateRequest.description:
Create a new quote (always starts in `draft` status).

Mirrors ``CreateQuoteDTO``. At least one of ``signer_contact_id`` or
``signer_email`` is required. ``line_items`` must be non-empty —
zero-line quotes can't be invoiced.

QuoteDetail.title: QuoteDetail
QuoteDetail.description:
Full row + line items + activity + envelope from ``GET /quotes/{id}``.

Open dict because ``_get_quote_detail`` returns the dynamic
``_row_to_dict`` shape plus resolved contact/company/envelope blocks.

QuoteLineItem.title: QuoteLineItem
QuoteLineItem.description:
One priced line, mirroring the app's `LineItemDTO`.

The two REQUIRED fields are required here too, and that is the point: the
app model is built inside the handler, so a missing `product_name` or
`unit_amount` would raise a bare `pydantic.ValidationError` there - not the
`RequestValidationError` `error_handlers.py` registers - and escape as a
500 instead of a 422.

`unit_amount` is in CENTS, like the app. An API that took dollars here
while the app took cents would be wrong by a factor of a hundred on every
quote, silently.

CLOSED (`extra="forbid"`), which makes this stricter than the app on
purpose. `LineItemDTO` uses pydantic's default behaviour and DROPS an
unrecognised field, so an open model here would accept a pricing field,
lose it on the way in, and return a schedule computed without it. On a
money surface a 422 naming the field is worth more than a 200 that quietly
priced something else. Nothing existing is affected - this route is new.

start_month.title: Start Month
start_month.description: Contract month when recurring billing begins; 1 means at contract start. Use billing_start_date instead for an exact date.

billing_start_date.title: Billing Start Date
billing_start_date.description: Exact recurring billing start date within the contract; start_month must remain 1 when supplied.

QuoteLineItemRequest.title: QuoteLineItemRequest
QuoteLineItemRequest.description:
One line item on a quote request body.

Shape mirrors ``integrations_v4.interfaces.fastapi.quote_router.LineItemDTO``
exactly. Pass either ``stripe_product_id`` + ``stripe_price_id`` (for a
Stripe-catalogue product) or ``manual_product_id`` (for an org-owned
manual catalogue entry), or neither (for a custom one-off line).
Authorization is enforced server-side — non-quotable products are
rejected with 400.

QuoteListPayload.title: QuoteListPayload
QuoteListPayload.description: An open envelope for a LIST result, so a bare list keeps its shape.

QuoteListResponse.title: QuoteListResponse
QuoteListResponse.description:
``GET /quotes`` envelope — preserves the original list endpoint's
pagination fields verbatim (the internal handler returns
``{items, total, page, limit}``).

QuotePayload.title: QuotePayload
QuotePayload.description: An open envelope for a quote, template, contact or job result.

QuoteSendPreviewRequest.title: QuoteSendPreviewRequest
QuoteSendPreviewRequest.description:
The same body `POST /quotes/{id}/send` takes - rendered, not sent.

Identical on purpose: previewing with a different body than you send is
how a preview stops predicting anything. `deliver` is accepted because the
app's model has it, and it is INERT here - this handler renders and
returns, and nothing in it reaches a mail transport.

QuoteSendRecipient.title: QuoteSendRecipient
QuoteSendRecipient.description: One recipient of a quote preview.

QuoteSendRequest.title: QuoteSendRequest
QuoteSendRequest.description:
Send (or resend) a quote for e-signature.

Both fields are optional — the server falls back to the quote title
for ``subject`` and a default cover line for ``message``. When the
target quote already has an active envelope (``sent`` / ``viewed``)
this resends without minting a new signing link.

QuoteSettingsResponse.title: QuoteSettingsResponse
QuoteSettingsResponse.description:
``GET /quote-settings`` row. Open dict — settings columns evolve
independently of this API surface.

sender_email.title: Sender Email
sender_email.description: Whose name every quote goes out under. Admin-only for that reason.

auto_close_deal_on_acceptance.title: Auto Close Deal On Acceptance
auto_close_deal_on_acceptance.description: Close the linked DEAL when a quote is accepted. Org-wide, and it changes what every future acceptance does to the pipeline.

auto_advance_deal_on_quote_send.title: Auto Advance Deal On Quote Send

QuoteSettingsUpdateRequest.title: QuoteSettingsUpdateRequest
QuoteSettingsUpdateRequest.description:
Org-wide quote branding, terms and sender identity.

A CLOSED mirror of the app's `QuoteSettingsDTO`, not an open bag. Leaving
it open would have achieved nothing: the app model uses pydantic's default
`extra` behaviour, so an unrecognised branding field is dropped THERE
whatever this one does. Closed, the caller gets a 422 naming the field;
open, they get a 200 and settings that did not change.

Every field is optional, and the app writes with `exclude_none`, so a
field you omit is left alone rather than blanked.

QuoteSummary.title: QuoteSummary
QuoteSummary.description:
List-view row from ``GET /quotes``. ``extra="allow"`` keeps every
backend column flowing through without us re-declaring CBQuote.

document_ids.title: Document Ids
document_ids.description: Legal documents to attach to every quote built from this template. Ids come from `GET /quote-settings/documents`.

QuoteTemplateRequest.title: QuoteTemplateRequest
QuoteTemplateRequest.description:
A reusable quote template. A CLOSED mirror of `QuoteTemplateDTO` - the
app drops an unrecognised field silently, so an open model here would turn
a typo into a template saved without the thing you typed.

QuoteUpdateRequest.title: QuoteUpdateRequest
QuoteUpdateRequest.description:
Partial update for a draft quote.

All fields optional. Passing ``line_items`` replaces them entirely
(and re-runs quotable-product authorization). Quotes in any status
other than ``draft`` reject updates with 400 — use ``edit-as-draft``
on a ``sent`` quote, or ``duplicate`` on a terminal one, to get a
fresh editable copy.

RadarReportListPayload.title: RadarReportListPayload

RateCardUpdateRequest.description: The published rate card. This is the price a client is billed.

owner_email.description: Must agree with the user id - the app verifies both. Typed as an email at the request layer because the app's model is `EmailStr` and is built inside the handler: a malformed address would otherwise raise there and escape as a 500 rather than a 422.

RecordColumnValuesRequest.title: RecordColumnValuesRequest

Read every column value for ONE row, resolved against a list.

website_url.description: Website to generate from. After a company-profile change this must be the NEW domain — intelligence is keyed by URL, so passing the old one silently regenerates the same stale content.

doc_types.title: Doc Types
doc_types.description: Specific Studio doc types to regenerate (e.g. ['icp_research','persona_research']). Omit to regenerate every document that already exists in the org.

rotate_existing.title: Rotate Existing
rotate_existing.description: Acknowledge that the existing credential stops working IMMEDIATELY. Leave false to mint only when there is none.

RegenerateKeyRequest.title: RegenerateKeyRequest
RegenerateKeyRequest.description: Mint a fresh ingest credential for a table.

RegisterLibraryVideoAssetRequest.title: RegisterLibraryVideoAssetRequest
RegisterLibraryVideoAssetRequest.description: Pick a Studio library video (``cb_org_videos`` id) for a Video campaign.

RegisterVideoAssetRequest.title: RegisterVideoAssetRequest
RegisterVideoAssetRequest.description: Register an object uploaded through /upload-url (the key it returned).

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: The carrier that holds it. It must match what the number was bought from - releasing a Telnyx number as `twilio` reaches the wrong provider.

ReleasePhoneRequest.title: ReleasePhoneRequest
ReleasePhoneRequest.description:
Give a number back to the carrier. IRREVERSIBLE.

Mirrors `phone_numbers.interfaces.fastapi.dtos.ReleasePhoneRequest`.

RemoveChannelsRequest.title: RemoveChannelsRequest
RemoveChannelsRequest.description: Detach senders from a sequence. Mirrors `BulkArchiveChannelParams`.

contact_ids.title: Contact Ids
contact_ids.description: List of contact IDs to remove

RemoveContactsFromListRequest.title: RemoveContactsFromListRequest
RemoveContactsFromListRequest.description: Request body for removing contacts from a list.

step_order.title: Step Order
step_order.description: Position the step held before removal

step_type.title: Step Type
step_type.description: Persisted step type, e.g. NETRION or HEYREACH

RemovedStepSummary.title: RemovedStepSummary
RemovedStepSummary.description: One step removed by the LinkedIn-removal operation.

RenameAIColumnRequest.title: RenameAIColumnRequest
RenameAIColumnRequest.description: Rename the column an AI group writes into. Display name only.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: Subject with spintax resolved to one variant

body.title: Body
body.description: Body with spintax resolved to one variant

spintax_blocks.title: Spintax Blocks
spintax_blocks.description: Count of top-level spintax blocks across subject + body. 0 means this step contains no spintax at all, which distinguishes 'nothing to vary' from 'spintax failed to resolve'.

total_combinations.title: Total Combinations
total_combinations.description: Distinct emails this step can produce. Always >= 1; a value of exactly 1 means the copy is too templated to vary, which is a legitimate outcome and not an error.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: Up to 3 distinct body renderings under different selection seeds. This is the proof that spintax works: if these differ, per-contact variation is functioning. Fewer than 3 entries means the copy cannot produce more.

variables_resolved.title: Variables Resolved
variables_resolved.description: False for this endpoint. Spintax is resolved but {{variables}} are left visible on purpose, because a preview has no contact and resolving against an empty contact would delete the token and show a hole in the copy. Variables fill in at send time.

will_send_as_shown.title: Will Send As Shown
will_send_as_shown.description: True when the rendered copy above is what a recipient actually gets. False means content_issues contains errors that make the delivered email differ from this preview, because malformed tokens are silently DELETED at send rather than raising. Do not launch on a false.

content_issues.title: Content Issues
content_issues.description: Findings from the same content-syntax validator that blocks launch, so a caller sees them here instead of discovering them as a 400 on run (or worse, as missing text in a delivered email). Each entry carries code, severity, message, field and snippet. An error-severity entry will block POST /sequences/{id}/run.

RenderedStepContent.title: RenderedStepContent
RenderedStepContent.description:
What a step's copy actually looks like once spintax is resolved.

Exists because ``step_data`` is the stored TEMPLATE, not the delivered email.
A caller reading raw ``{{a|b|c}}`` back out of a field called "preview" has no
way to tell working spintax from broken spintax, which is precisely how a
working feature got reported as broken (see the PR that added this).

reset.title: Reset
reset.description: Delete the override; the role default applies again.

RepLimitsSettings.title: RepLimitsSettings
RepLimitsSettings.description:
Per-role reveal/ownership limits. Mirrors `roles.RepLimitsSettings`.

The three `Literal`s are closed here rather than left as strings because
they reach the app's own `Literal` inside `_apply_rep_limits`.

ReplaceHtmlRequest.title: ReplaceHtmlRequest
ReplaceHtmlRequest.description: Persist a whole-page HTML snapshot. Deterministic, spends nothing.

ReportListPayload.title: ReportListPayload
ReportListPayload.description:
An OPEN envelope for a report that answers with a bare LIST.

A bare list is reachable as `items`; a named list (`{"counts": {...}}`)
keeps its own key AND gains `items`, so a caller can read either shape
without branching.

ReportPayload.title: ReportPayload
ReportPayload.description:
An OPEN envelope around one report's answer.

The app wraps every one of these reports in `{success, data, meta}`, where
`meta` carries the cache state, the window and - on the agency reports -
`failed_org_ids`, the orgs that contributed NOTHING to the totals above.
That field is the difference between "this client sent no email" and "we
could not query this client", so it is forwarded rather than flattened
away.

Open on purpose: `data` is `dict | list` in the app and its contents grow
with the product. A closed model would turn every new metric into a
silently dropped one.

RepurposeAdRequest.title: RepurposeAdRequest
RepurposeAdRequest.description: Derive an ad creative from an existing piece. SPENDS CREDIT.

RepurposeSourceRequest.title: RepurposeSourceRequest
RepurposeSourceRequest.description: Derive a LinkedIn post from an existing piece. SPENDS CREDIT.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Correlation id — matches the X-Request-Id response header

status.title: Status
status.description: HTTP status code of the response

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: Unix seconds when the request completed

slot_start.title: Slot Start
slot_start.description: ISO-8601 start of the slot being held.

slot_end.title: Slot End
slot_end.description: ISO-8601 end of the slot being held.

ReserveSlotRequest.title: ReserveSlotRequest
ReserveSlotRequest.description:
Hold a slot while a booker fills in the form.

The app types both times as bare strings and parses them with
`datetime.fromisoformat` inside the handler with no guard, so a malformed
value is an unhandled 500 there. They are validated as ISO-8601 here and
forwarded unchanged.

ReskinRequest.title: ReskinRequest
ReskinRequest.description: Swap the creative's palette. Deterministic, spends nothing.

ResolveCompanyIdsRequest.title: ResolveCompanyIdsRequest
ResolveCompanyIdsRequest.description:
Turn LinkedIn company ids into graph8 company ids.

This is what makes a Hiring Signals result actionable: the search returns
lcids, and a list or a sequence needs graph8 ids. The handler caps the
input server-side regardless of what is sent.

ResolveThreadRequest.title: ResolveThreadRequest
ResolveThreadRequest.description:
Mark a discussion thread resolved.

Distinct from completing the task: a task can be done with an unresolved
thread and vice versa. Idempotent - re-resolving returns the existing row.

RestoreRevisionRequest.title: RestoreRevisionRequest
RestoreRevisionRequest.description: Roll back to a snapshot. The restore is itself snapshotted first.

RetryResearchReportRequest.title: RetryResearchReportRequest
RetryResearchReportRequest.description: Re-run one failed report. SPENDS CREDIT.

RevenueAnalyticsPayload.title: RevenueAnalyticsPayload
RevenueAnalyticsPayload.description: A dashboard or rollup, as the app computes it.

RevenueRecordPayload.title: RevenueRecordPayload
RevenueRecordPayload.description: An activity, snapshot, plan or result, as the app returns it.

local_id.title: Local Id
local_id.description: The record, as an exact decimal string.

policy.title: Policy
policy.description: Always null on a review; the stored policy applies.

action.title: Action
action.description: `retry` re-applies the change; `preserve` keeps the record as it is.

RewriteFieldRequest.title: RewriteFieldRequest
RewriteFieldRequest.description: Rewrite ONE copy field with AI. SPENDS CREDIT.

instruction.title: Instruction
instruction.description: What to change, in plain words.

RewriteTextRequest.title: RewriteTextRequest
RewriteTextRequest.description: Rewrite ONE element with an AI instruction. THIS SPENDS AI CREDIT.

competitor_id.title: Competitor Id
competitor_id.description: The competitor. Null detaches the current one.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the deal stands against them.

RivalAttachRequest.title: RivalAttachRequest
RivalAttachRequest.description: Record which competitor is on a deal, and how it is going.

RoleCreateRequest.title: RoleCreateRequest
RoleCreateRequest.description:
Define a new role. Mirrors `roles.RoleCreateRequest`.

`permissions` is bounded by the app's own non-escalation guard
(`_assert_can_grant_permissions`): a caller may not mint a role granting a
permission they do not themselves hold. That guard runs INSIDE the handler
and is deliberately not duplicated here - see the router docstring.

RoleUpdateRequest.title: RoleUpdateRequest
RoleUpdateRequest.description:
Replace a role's definition. Mirrors `roles.RoleUpdateRequest`.

`permissions` is a REPLACEMENT, not a merge, and it takes effect for
everyone who already holds the role. That is why the operation is tiered
`destructive` rather than `write`.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Column/value pairs to write on this row. Empty = no-op (counts as ok with 0 writes).

RowFieldValues.title: RowFieldValues
RowFieldValues.description: One row (contact or company) plus the columns to set on it.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: group_id of a saved AI enrichment config (starts with 'ai_enrich')

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: List ID the records belong to

max_records.title: Max Records
max_records.description: Optional cap on records processed (defaults to len(record_ids)).

RunAIEnrichRequest.title: RunAIEnrichRequest
RunAIEnrichRequest.description:
Run a saved AI enrichment config on specific records.

The prompt, model, outputs, and column mapping live on the config
referenced by `group_id`. We accept `record_ids` so callers can target
exactly the contacts they want enriched.

auto_enrich.title: Auto Enrich
auto_enrich.description: Also enrich each scraped row. Charged on top.

RunBuiltinScraperRequest.title: RunBuiltinScraperRequest
RunBuiltinScraperRequest.description:
Describe what to collect; the scraper fills the table. CHARGES.

The price is quoted by `GET /workbench/scraper/credit-estimate`. A quote is
approved by passing `approved_max_credits` and `quote_expires_at` back.

RunFindPeopleRequest.title: RunFindPeopleRequest
RunFindPeopleRequest.description: Which companies a find-people config runs over.

RunFormulaRequest.title: RunFormulaRequest
RunFormulaRequest.description:
Which records a formula column is computed for.

With no ids and no `mode`, the formula runs over the list's records up to
`max_records`. `mode: empty` fills only records whose value is blank.

RunProviderScraperRequest.title: RunProviderScraperRequest
RunProviderScraperRequest.description:
Run a scraper on your connected provider account. CHARGES per result.

One of `preset_id` (from `GET /workbench/scraper/presets`) or
`custom_actor_id`. `auto_enrich` DEFAULTS TO TRUE here: every result is
also enriched, and charged, unless you turn it off.

requalify.title: Requalify
requalify.description: Re-run records that already have a verdict.

RunQualificationRequest.title: RunQualificationRequest
RunQualificationRequest.description: Qualify a list against a template.

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: List (workbench) the workflow belongs to.

record_ids.title: Record Ids
record_ids.description: Rows to run it on, for `selected`.

RunRecordWorkflowRequest.title: RunRecordWorkflowRequest
RunRecordWorkflowRequest.description: Mirrors `RunWorkflowRequest`. `run_mode` is closed to the app's three values.

row_ids.title: Row Ids
row_ids.description: Rows to run. OMIT to run EVERY row in the table.

approved_max_credits.title: Approved Max Credits
approved_max_credits.description: Ceiling the caller approves. The run refuses to exceed it.

RunStagingAIRequest.title: RunStagingAIRequest
RunStagingAIRequest.description:
Which rows a run covers, and the spend the caller approved.

OMITTING `row_ids` RUNS EVERY ROW. `exclude_row_ids` narrows that back down.

column_id.title: Column Id
column_id.description: column_id from a saved waterfall pipeline

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: List ID the records belong to

skip_existing_values.title: Skip Existing Values
skip_existing_values.description: Override the pipeline's skip_existing_values setting. If None (default), the pipeline's saved setting is used.

RunWaterfallEnrichRequest.title: RunWaterfallEnrichRequest
RunWaterfallEnrichRequest.description: Run a saved waterfall pipeline on specific records.

RunWorkbenchFindPeopleRequest.title: RunWorkbenchFindPeopleRequest
RunWorkbenchFindPeopleRequest.description:
Which rows find-people runs over.

`selected` requires `row_ids` or `exclude_row_ids`; the other modes forbid
them.

provider_name.title: Provider Name
provider_name.description: IdP name: okta, azure, google, onelogin, custom.

idp_certificate.title: Idp Certificate
idp_certificate.description: X.509 certificate from the IdP, PEM format.

require_sso.title: Require Sso
require_sso.description: Make SSO the ONLY way in. False here and set it later with `PUT /org/sso/enforcement` once you have signed in through SSO yourself — that ordering is what stops a lockout.

allowed_domains.title: Allowed Domains
allowed_domains.description: Email domains allowed to sign in this way.

SAMLConfigRequest.title: SAMLConfigRequest
SAMLConfigRequest.description:
SAML sign-in configuration.

The certificate and URLs come from the identity provider. Nothing here is
guessable, which is why every one of the first four fields is required —
a half-configured SSO that then gets activated is how an org locks itself
out.

run_immediately.title: Run Immediately
run_immediately.description: Always false. Saving never runs - the app refuses immediate execution so a save can never become an unpriced spend.

SaveAIConfigRequest.title: SaveAIConfigRequest
SaveAIConfigRequest.description: Save an AI enrichment group. Saving costs nothing; running it does.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.description: Only run the pass on rows matching these conditions.

SaveColumnAIConfigRequest.title: SaveColumnAIConfigRequest
SaveColumnAIConfigRequest.description: Configure ONE column's AI pass. Saving costs nothing; running does.

connection_id.title: Connection Id
connection_id.description: The id the OAuth flow returned.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Stable graph8 provider name.

connection_config.title: Connection Config
connection_config.description: Provider-specific configuration captured during the flow.

SaveConnectionRequest.title: SaveConnectionRequest
SaveConnectionRequest.description:
Record a connection the OAuth flow has already established.

This does NOT perform the OAuth handshake - the hosted flow does that, and
this stores its result. `connection_id` is the id that flow handed back,
not one you choose.

force_update.title: Force Update
force_update.description: Overwrite intent metadata already on a contact, rather than only filling gaps.

SaveIntentToMetadataRequest.title: SaveIntentToMetadataRequest
SaveIntentToMetadataRequest.description:
Write each contact's resolved intent onto the contact record.

No `org_id`: the org is the authenticated key's own.

SaveListPipelineRequest.title: SaveListPipelineRequest
SaveListPipelineRequest.description:
Create a list pipeline.

`enabled: true` ARMS it: an enabled pipeline runs its steps over the list,
and every enrichment step charges.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: What the saved search is over - `contacts` or `companies` today. Deliberately a free string rather than a closed enum, matching the app, which is designed to add more.

icp_query.title: Icp Query
icp_query.description: The search itself. Opaque and round-tripped as-is.

id.title: Id
id.description: Send the id of an existing saved search to REPLACE it.

SaveSearchRequest.title: SaveSearchRequest
SaveSearchRequest.description:
Store a search so a person can run it again later.

`icp_query` is OPAQUE and round-tripped verbatim: the app stores it as a
plain JSON blob and does not interpret it at save time, so this contract
does not either. That is also why it is the one place here that does not
go through the field map - translating a blob nobody reads would change
what the caller gets back.

`id` present means UPDATE the saved search rather than create a new one.

execution_id.title: Execution Id
execution_id.description: The skill execution that produced the content.

SaveSkillResultRequest.title: SaveSkillResultRequest
SaveSkillResultRequest.description: Attach the output of a skill run to a record as a document.

SaveStagingAIConfigRequest.title: SaveStagingAIConfigRequest
SaveStagingAIConfigRequest.description: Configure the table-level AI pass. Saving costs nothing; running does.

SaveWaterfallRequest.title: SaveWaterfallRequest
SaveWaterfallRequest.description:
Create or overwrite a workbench waterfall column.

`run_immediately` and `target_records` are carried for parity with the app
model and IGNORED by the workbench save: saving never runs anything. Run it
with `POST /workbench/tables/{table_id}/waterfall/configs/{column_id}/run`.

ScanConfigDTO.title: ScanConfigDTO
ScanConfigDTO.description:
Per-competitor page-selection config (persisted on profile.meta.scan_config).

mode=auto: Firecrawl /map → rank by traffic + pricing/feature paths → scrape
top N (= tier page budget). mode=manual: scrape include_paths (literal or
/wildcard/* patterns), capped to the budget.

ScheduleBuyDomainCheckRequest.title: ScheduleBuyDomainCheckRequest
ScheduleBuyDomainCheckRequest.description: Validate edited candidate names: owned-by-you, and available. SPENDS NOTHING.

count.title: Count
count.description: How many candidate names to return

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Rotate the generator to get fresh candidates

roots.title: Roots
roots.description: Word roots to build names from

ScheduleBuyDomainSuggestRequest.title: ScheduleBuyDomainSuggestRequest
ScheduleBuyDomainSuggestRequest.description: Preview the domain names a plan WOULD buy. SPENDS NOTHING.

target_monthly_volume.title: Target Monthly Volume
target_monthly_volume.description: Contacts you intend to reach per month

idle_mailboxes_snapshot.title: Idle Mailboxes Snapshot
idle_mailboxes_snapshot.description: Idle mailboxes you already hold, from /suggest

warmup_provider.title: Warmup Provider
warmup_provider.description: Warmup engine the bought mailboxes are enrolled with

registrants.title: Registrants
registrants.description: Registrant identities. Required unless persona_ids is set.

mailbox_aliases.title: Mailbox Aliases
mailbox_aliases.description: One alias per mailbox_per_domain. Required unless persona_ids is set.

persona_ids.title: Persona Ids
persona_ids.description: Sender personas to buy for. Excludes the two above.

reuse_domains.title: Reuse Domains
reuse_domains.description: Adopt these owned EMPTY domains instead of buying

domain_names.title: Domain Names
domain_names.description: Approved names to buy, in order

ScheduleBuyPlanRequest.title: ScheduleBuyPlanRequest
ScheduleBuyPlanRequest.description:
Create and LOCK a staggered buying plan. PLACES REAL CREDIT HOLDS.

Mirrors the app's ``CreatePlanRequest`` field for field, including its
mutual-exclusion rule between ``persona_ids`` and the manual
``registrants``/``mailbox_aliases`` pair - the app raises that in a
validator, and it must fire as a 422 here rather than inside the proxy.

target_monthly_volume.title: Target Monthly Volume
target_monthly_volume.description: Contacts you intend to reach per month

ScheduleBuySuggestRequest.title: ScheduleBuySuggestRequest
ScheduleBuySuggestRequest.description:
Size a plan for a target volume: idle capacity, net-new domains and mailboxes, credit cost.
SPENDS NOTHING. Mirrors the app's `SuggestRequest` field for field.

ScheduleConfigRequest.title: ScheduleConfigRequest
ScheduleConfigRequest.description:
Run something on this table on a schedule.

A schedule whose `action_type` is `run_ai` SPENDS CREDITS on every firing,
without a further call. `enabled` defaults to false so creating one is not
the same act as starting it.

day.title: Day
day.description: Lowercase day name: monday | tuesday | wednesday | thursday | friday | saturday | sunday.

ScheduleDayWindow.title: ScheduleDayWindow
ScheduleDayWindow.description:
One day's send window — flattens `{start, end}` from the sequencer.

Days that are absent from the underlying config (= no sending) are
omitted from the response rather than serialized as nulls — keeps
the response compact and matches the picker UI's behaviour.

id.title: Id
id.description: Schedule UUID; pass back to launch / PATCH endpoints.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name as set in the Sequencer schedule UI.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA timezone name applied to every window (e.g. 'Europe/Madrid').

windows.title: Windows
windows.description: Per-day send windows for the schedule. Days with no window are omitted.

is_archived.title: Is Archived
is_archived.description: Archived schedules are excluded by default — pass `include_archived=true` to include them.

ScheduleListItem.title: ScheduleListItem
ScheduleListItem.description: One row in the schedule picker. `id` feeds `schedule_id` on the launch body.

arm.title: Arm
arm.description: TRUE MEANS IT WILL PUBLISH ITSELF at planned_publish_at, with no further human step. False only records the date.

ScheduleRequest.title: ScheduleRequest
ScheduleRequest.description:
Place a piece on the calendar, or ARM it to publish itself.

`arm` is the consequential field: false plans the date for a human, true
hands it to the publish sweep, which will put the piece in front of real
people at `planned_publish_at` with no further confirmation.

SchedulingListPayload.title: SchedulingListPayload
SchedulingListPayload.description:
An open envelope for a LIST result, so a bare list keeps its shape.

A named list (`{"events": [...]}`) keeps its own key AND gains `items`, so
a generic client can page any of these the same way.

SchedulingPayload.title: SchedulingPayload
SchedulingPayload.description:
An open envelope for a filter, a setting, an embed config or a slot grid.

Open because org settings gain branding fields as the booking page does
and the embed config gains styling keys as the widget does. Closing it
would drop a field the app had already started returning.

version.title: Version
version.description: Human-facing ordinal. Nothing keys on it; the digest is the identity.

digest.title: Digest
digest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical schema. Re-publishing the same schema resolves here.

manifest.title: Manifest
manifest.description: The stored canonical schema. Self-describing, so the version needs no other source.

exclude_paths.title: Exclude Paths
exclude_paths.description: URL path patterns to skip while crawling.

max_pages.title: Max Pages
max_pages.description: Pages per crawl. The app's own bounds.

ScrapeConfigUpdateRequest.title: ScrapeConfigUpdateRequest
ScrapeConfigUpdateRequest.description: Change how the org crawls. Only what you send is written.

url.title: Url
url.description: Root URL. Everything under it is followed.

frequency.title: Frequency
frequency.description: How often to re-crawl. `manual` never re-crawls.

max_pages.title: Max Pages
max_pages.description: Ceiling, not a target - a small site only crawls what exists.

ScrapeSourceCreateRequest.title: ScrapeSourceCreateRequest
ScrapeSourceCreateRequest.description:
A site to crawl into a collection on a schedule.

CREATING ONE CRAWLS IMMEDIATELY - it does not wait for the first scheduled
run. That is why this operation is `billable` rather than a plain write.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: False pauses the recurring crawl; the source survives.

ScrapeSourceUpdateRequest.title: ScrapeSourceUpdateRequest
ScrapeSourceUpdateRequest.description: Change a source's cadence, page ceiling, or pause it. Omitted = unchanged.

api_key.title: Api Key
api_key.description: Your provider API token. Never returned.

ScraperConnectionRequest.title: ScraperConnectionRequest
ScraperConnectionRequest.description: Connect your own scraper provider account. The token is write-only.

ScraperConnectionTestRequest.title: ScraperConnectionTestRequest
ScraperConnectionTestRequest.description: Check a token against the provider without saving it.

SdrDialerTargetsRequest.title: SdrDialerTargetsRequest
SdrDialerTargetsRequest.description: One rep's daily goals, overriding the org default.

SearchCompanyItem.title: SearchCompanyItem
SearchCompanyItem.description: Company result from open data search.

SearchContactItem.title: SearchContactItem
SearchContactItem.description: Contact result from open data search.

SearchDiscoveryPayload.title: SearchDiscoveryPayload
SearchDiscoveryPayload.description: An open envelope for an autocomplete or filter-option result.

SearchImportPreviewRequest.title: SearchImportPreviewRequest
SearchImportPreviewRequest.description: Sample what a people search would import. Contact details stay masked.

icp_filters.title: Icp Filters
icp_filters.description: Import EVERYTHING these filters match, up to `max_result`. The unbounded form of this operation.

SearchImportRequest.title: SearchImportRequest
SearchImportRequest.description: Import people directly, either a given set or everything an ICP query matches.

SearchOperator.title: SearchOperator
SearchOperator.description: Supported filter operators for search queries.

SearchPostEngagementsRequest.title: SearchPostEngagementsRequest
SearchPostEngagementsRequest.description: Filters over engagements ALREADY stored against a post.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.description: Grid-style filter expressions, passed through unchanged. Their grammar is the app's, not this contract's - a typed model here would freeze a filter language that still moves.

has_contact.title: Has Contact
has_contact.description: Only posts whose author resolved to a graph8 contact.

hide_low_confidence.title: Hide Low Confidence
hide_low_confidence.description: Hide posts the classifier scored confidently LOW (< 0.5), while keeping never-classified ones visible. Not the same as `min_score=0.5`, which would also hide the unscored.

SearchPostsRequest.title: SearchPostsRequest
SearchPostsRequest.description: Filters over posts ALREADY matched and stored. Fetches nothing live.

SearchResearchPreviewRequest.title: SearchResearchPreviewRequest
SearchResearchPreviewRequest.description: Describe your leads in words; a model writes the search filters.

SearchSaveRequest.title: SearchSaveRequest
SearchSaveRequest.description: Request to search and save results to a list.

negate.title: Negate
negate.description: Match companies WITHOUT the signal (hiring, tech, company_type).

SearchSignalFilter.title: SearchSignalFilter
SearchSignalFilter.description: One signal. Which list must be non-empty depends on `type`.

page_urls.title: Page Urls
page_urls.description: Replace the automatic page selection with exactly these pages.

extra_page_urls.title: Extra Page Urls
extra_page_urls.description: Add these pages to whatever the picker chose.

SectionLibraryRebuildRequest.title: SectionLibraryRebuildRequest
SectionLibraryRebuildRequest.description:
Mirrors `RebuildSectionLibraryRequest`.

The two lists are NOT interchangeable: `page_urls` REPLACES the automatic
page selection, `extra_page_urls` ADDS to it. Sending the first is how you
override the picker; sending the second is how you top it up.

hidden.title: Hidden
hidden.description: Auto-derived tags suppressed for this section.

SectionTagOverridesRequest.title: SectionTagOverridesRequest
SectionTagOverridesRequest.description:
Mirrors `campaign_builder.routers.brand_kit.SectionTagOverridesRequest`.

Durable and UPSERTED by section id - sections you do not mention keep the
overrides they already had.

role_id.title: Role Id
role_id.description: Must match the `role_id` in the path.

team_member_id.title: Team Member Id
team_member_id.description: Team-member id or the person's user id.

user_name.title: User Name
user_name.description: Required when this creates the team member.

user_email.title: User Email
user_email.description: Required when this creates the team member.

SeedChannelsRequest.title: SeedChannelsRequest
SeedChannelsRequest.description: Which channels an auto-seed targets. Defaults to X alone.

SeedContext.title: SeedContext
SeedContext.description:
Optional richer seed for an approved stub — e.g. the target keyword (+ volume/cpc)
to seed an SEO page with. All optional; absent → current behavior unchanged.

SegmentFilterGroup.title: SegmentFilterGroup
SegmentFilterGroup.description:
An AND/OR group of leaves and nested groups, at most three groups deep.

Mirrors `SegmentFilterGroup` in `contacts.domain.value_objects.ag_grid_models`.
`op` is closed because the app REFUSES an unrecognised connector rather
than defaulting to AND - defaulting would silently return a different
result set, and on a destructive route that is a different set of records
acted on.

FIXED DEPTH, NOT RECURSIVE. The app's model is self-referencing; the
published one deliberately is not, because a schema that reaches itself
through `$ref` sends the docs renderer into unbounded recursion. Three
group levels (this one, `SegmentFilterSubgroup`, `SegmentFilterInnerGroup`)
cover every filter the app's own builder produces; the app's larger depth
and leaf budget still applies and surfaces as a 422.

SeoRemovedKeywords.description:

SeoSaveTrackedKeywordsRequest.description:

SeoStartAuditRequest.description:

SequenceDuplicateRequest.description:
Copy a sequence. The copy is owned by the caller and starts drafted.

`user_email` is deliberately absent: the app pins the copy's owner to the
caller, so accepting the field would advertise control it does not grant.

SequenceOpsPayload.title: SequenceOpsPayload
SequenceOpsPayload.description: A sequence contact, report, step list or job status, as the app returns it.

SequenceRecord.title: SequenceRecord
SequenceRecord.description: One sequence, as the lifecycle endpoints return it.

scanned_count.title: Scanned Count
scanned_count.description: How many recipients were actually scanned (capped at 10,000).

SequenceRoutingSummary.title: SequenceRoutingSummary
SequenceRoutingSummary.description:
Approximate provider-routing and suppression breakdown for the list.

Two properties a caller must not lose:

  * APPROXIMATE - computed by scanning up to 10,000 recipients, not all of
    them.
  * FAIL-OPEN - on any error every count is zero, so an all-zero summary
    means "could not compute" just as much as "nothing matched". Do not
    render it as a confident zero.

Each recipient counts toward exactly ONE bucket, suppression taking
precedence over routing (bounce > seg > personal), so the buckets are a
partition and must not be summed alongside each other as if they overlap.

skip_reason_breakdown.title: Skip Reason Breakdown
skip_reason_breakdown.description: Distinct terminal-skipped contacts by raw skip-reason token, e.g. `skipped_too_distant`. Sequence-level, counted once per contact.

SequenceStats.title: SequenceStats
SequenceStats.description:
Per-step delivery and engagement counts for a sequence.

`skip_reason_breakdown` is SEQUENCE-level and counted ONCE per contact, so
its total can be LESS than the sum of the per-step `skipped` tiles: the
durable-LinkedIn-skip cascade writes one receipt per contiguous LinkedIn
step, and a skip with no recorded reason is omitted entirely. Presenting
the two as if they must reconcile is wrong.

status.title: Status
status.description: Target status: drafted, scheduling, live, pausing, paused, resuming, terminating, terminated, completed or waiting. Declared as an open string rather than an enum so a status the sequencer adds is not rejected by a stale copy here - the app's own `SequenceStatus` enum is the source of truth and an unknown value comes back as a 422 that LISTS the valid set.

SequenceStatusRequest.title: SequenceStatusRequest
SequenceStatusRequest.description:
Drive the sequence status machine directly.

Prefer the named transitions (`/launch`, `/pause`, `/resume`,
`/terminate`, `/archive`) - each runs the wind-down, scheduling and event
work that belongs to it. This endpoint SETS THE STATUS, and the app's
state machine is what rejects an illegal transition.

SequenceStepsResponse.title: SequenceStepsResponse
SequenceStepsResponse.description:
Response for ``GET /sequences/{id}/steps``.

404, which sent them to ``/preview`` and its unrendered copy instead.

previous complete calendar month, or a terminated engagement's earliest
unbilled month) so nobody can pick a window that mis-prorates the retainer,
and the amount is the sum of the statement's line items. They are documented
as ignored rather than dropped from the contract, because dropping a field
the app model declares is what makes a proxy 500 on a required one.

StatementDecisionRequest.description: The client's reason when returning a statement to its author.

closes. They stay on the model only because the app model still declares
them.

StudioContentListPayload.title: StudioContentListPayload
StudioContentListPayload.description:
A LIST result, open-shaped, with `items` always present.

The app returns a bare list from some routes and a named key from others
(`pages`, `grids`, `images`, `creatives`, `reports`, `items`). Both are
published: the original key is preserved AND mirrored onto `items`, so a
client can page any Studio collection the same way without a per-route
lookup table.

StudioContentPayload.description: One Studio object, open-shaped. See the module docstring.

StudioListPayload.title: StudioListPayload
StudioListPayload.description:
An open envelope for a LIST result, so a bare list keeps its shape.

A handler that returns `[...]` and one that returns `{"documents": [...]}`
both land on `items`, and the named key is preserved beside it so a caller
reading the app's own spelling is not broken by the normalisation.

StudioPayload.title: StudioPayload
StudioPayload.description:
An open envelope for one settings block, document or brand artefact.

OPEN on purpose. These surfaces are configuration and generated content,
and both grow: a new toggle on a settings block or a new field on a
generated document must reach a caller on the day it ships, not on the day
somebody remembers to widen a mirror. A closed response model here would
silently DROP the new key, which reads to the caller as "the product does
not have that setting".

The request side is the opposite and is mirrored exactly - see the module
docstring for why the asymmetry is deliberate.

StyleNormalizeRequest.description: Text to normalise to the org's writing style.

UpdateAdCampaignRequest.title: UpdateAdCampaignRequest
UpdateAdCampaignRequest.description:
Body for ``PUT /campaigns/{id}`` and ``POST /campaigns/{id}/edit-preview``.

``extra="forbid"`` is load-bearing (PRD hazard H8): the model used to inherit
Pydantic's default ``extra="ignore"``, so the wizard could POST a field the
backend had never wired, get a 200, and render a green "Campaign updated"
toast for an edit that reached nothing. An unknown field is now a 422 —
a phantom control is structurally impossible to ship.

List-shaped fields (``keywords``, ``rsa_headlines``, ``rsa_descriptions``,
``geo_targets``) are COMPLETE desired lists, never deltas. Google replaces
repeated fields wholesale, so a partial list silently deletes the omitted
entries; the handler read-modify-writes against the platform's current state.
``None`` means "not provided / unchanged" — an empty list is a real request
to clear, and is rejected where clearing would break the ad.

/``contact_company``/``contact_linkedin_url`` set) raises SQLAlchemy
"Unconsumed column names" inside the handler and 500s. Lifecycle fields
(status, meeting_date, meeting_type, hiring_id) are intentionally not
editable — those are calendar-driven client-side fields.

WorkReadMarkerRequest.title: WorkReadMarkerRequest
WorkReadMarkerRequest.description:
How far this person has read ONE conversation.

`last_read_at` is the conversation's `latestAt` boundary the reader was
shown, in unix seconds — the same clock `WorkInboxDispositionRequest`
keeps in `latest_activity_at` — not the instant they looked. A newer
inbound message therefore lights the badge again on its own: the
comparison is `latestAt > lastReadAt`, and nothing has to un-mark anything.

Seconds are not a total order: `post_message` truncates event timestamps
to whole seconds, so a message that lands in the SAME second as the one
the reader saw would compare equal and pass as read. `last_read_id` — the
id of the newest message the reader was shown — is the tiebreaker: at an
equal second, only a matching id counts as read (Codex on #16589).

write pattern the org lock exists to serialize, so the batch is the unit.
Bounded so a runaway client cannot hand the server a map to merge.

WorkSidebarPreferencesRequest.description:
How this person wants their own sidebar ordered.

Both halves are required and closed-vocabulary, exactly as
`normalizeSidebarSortMode` requires them (`index.ts:10838`): a partial
write would leave the other half at whatever a previous client wrote and
make the response a lie about the stored state.

WorkSignalPromoteRequest.title: WorkSignalPromoteRequest
WorkSignalPromoteRequest.description: Turn one revenue signal into an accountable Work turn.

message.title: Message
message.description: The stored message that carries the turn

duplicate.title: Duplicate
duplicate.description: True when this signal had already been promoted

WorkSignalPromoted.title: WorkSignalPromoted
WorkSignalPromoted.description: The message a signal promotion sent into `#work`.

event.title: Event
event.description: The room event the write appended

duplicate.title: Duplicate
duplicate.description: True when the signal already held the requested state

WorkSignalState.title: WorkSignalState
WorkSignalState.description: One revenue signal after being snoozed or dismissed.

WorkSignalStateRequest.title: WorkSignalStateRequest
WorkSignalStateRequest.description: Snooze or dismiss one revenue signal.

days.title: Days
days.description: The dates in the window, oldest first

reps.title: Reps
reps.description: Per-rep series; null for a day that was not measured (a gap is not a zero)

WorkTeamHqHistory.title: WorkTeamHqHistory
WorkTeamHqHistory.description: Per-rep daily series behind the board's sparklines, deltas and streaks.

measuredAt.title: Measuredat
measuredAt.description: When the rows were measured; null when unavailable

degradedMetrics.title: Degradedmetrics
degradedMetrics.description: Columns that failed to measure; absent from every row rather than zero

WorkTeamHqLeaderboard.title: WorkTeamHqLeaderboard
WorkTeamHqLeaderboard.description: One Team HQ board over the organization's own SDR analytics.

WorkTickerEvents.title: WorkTickerEvents
WorkTickerEvents.description: Team HQ ticker moments, newest first.

node_id.title: Node Id
node_id.description: The workflow node whose output feeds the column.

output_path.title: Output Path
output_path.description: Dot path into that node's output.

column_type.title: Column Type
column_type.description: How the grid treats the column.

WorkbenchBindingItem.title: WorkbenchBindingItem
WorkbenchBindingItem.description: One workflow output rendered as one grid column.

name.title: Name
name.description: Machine name: lowercase, starting with a letter. This is the key row data is addressed by, which is why it is constrained while `display_name` is not.

field_path.title: Field Path
field_path.description: Path into a raw_json source column.

WorkbenchColumnMappingRequest.title: WorkbenchColumnMappingRequest
WorkbenchColumnMappingRequest.description:
Point a column at a CRM field so export knows where its values go.

`null` clears the mapping, which is why the field is optional rather than
required - an unmapped column is a real state, not a missing argument.

WorkbenchCreditValidationRequest.title: WorkbenchCreditValidationRequest
WorkbenchCreditValidationRequest.description:
Price a run before starting it. FREE.

At most one of `column_id`, `group_id` and `all_columns`. None prices the
table's default AI pass.

list_id.title: List Id
list_id.description: Existing list to export into.

export_verified_only.title: Export Verified Only
export_verified_only.description: Only rows whose email passed verification.

WorkbenchExportRequest.title: WorkbenchExportRequest
WorkbenchExportRequest.description: Export rows to an audience list.

WorkbenchPage.title: WorkbenchPage
WorkbenchPage.description:
A page of rows, or a list of columns, exactly as the app returns it.

Rows and columns stay open dicts: a Workbench table's columns are defined
by the CUSTOMER at runtime. There is no schema to pin, and inventing one
would make the product unusable through this API.

WorkbenchPipelineBranchStep.title: WorkbenchPipelineBranchStep
WorkbenchPipelineBranchStep.description:
A step inside a branch.

Its own `if_steps` / `else_steps` are open objects in this schema: the app
nests steps without limit, and a self-referencing schema is not publishable.
They are still validated as steps by the app.

WorkbenchPipelineStep.title: WorkbenchPipelineStep
WorkbenchPipelineStep.description: One step. A `branch` step runs `if_steps` or `else_steps`.

WorkbenchRowUpdateRequest.title: WorkbenchRowUpdateRequest
WorkbenchRowUpdateRequest.description: Set ONE field on one row - the grid's cell edit.

WorkbenchRowsDeleteRequest.title: WorkbenchRowsDeleteRequest
WorkbenchRowsDeleteRequest.description:
Delete rows by id, or every row EXCEPT a set.

`select_all` is EXPLICIT rather than inferred from an empty `row_ids`,
mirroring the app - so a client bug can never turn "nothing selected" into
"delete the whole table". This surface keeps that guarantee rather than
accepting a bare empty list as a delete-everything.

WorkbenchSearchImportRequest.title: WorkbenchSearchImportRequest
WorkbenchSearchImportRequest.description:
Import people from a search into the table as LOCKED rows.

Each row costs a credit to unlock (`POST .../unlock-rows`).

entity_type.title: Entity Type
entity_type.description: What the rows will become on export. Settable once, at creation.

WorkbenchTableUpdateRequest.title: WorkbenchTableUpdateRequest
WorkbenchTableUpdateRequest.description:
Rename or re-describe. `entity_type` is deliberately absent - it decides
how rows export and is fixed at creation.

WorkspaceMemberInput.title: WorkspaceMemberInput
WorkspaceMemberInput.description: One member in a team's single-save membership list.

WorkspaceSearchPayload.title: WorkspaceSearchPayload
WorkspaceSearchPayload.description: Search results, grouped the way the app groups them.

search_type.title: Search Type
search_type.description: `auto` picks keyword or semantic from the wording of the query.

api_key.title: Api Key
api_key.description: X Developer App API key (consumer key).

XApiCredentialsRequest.title: XApiCredentialsRequest
XApiCredentialsRequest.description:
An X developer app's key and secret.

WRITE-ONLY. Neither value, nor the bearer token derived from them, is ever
returned by any route on this surface - `GET /social-listeners/integrations/x`
reports whether a connection exists, not what it is.

appointments__domain__entities__UpdateSe.title: UpdateSequenceRequest
appointments__domain__entities__UpdateSe.description:
Associate a booking with a sequencer sequence (or detach when null).

`sequence_id` is the `seqsequences.id` UUID. Persisted under
`booking.metadata_['campaignId']` — same key the public booking flow
populates from the `?campaignId=` URL param at create time.

tag_ids.title: Tag Ids
tag_ids.description: Tag IDs to associate with the thread

tag_id.title: Tag Id
tag_id.description: The tag to attach. It must already exist.

developer_api__interfaces__dtos__inbox_c.title: TagRequest
developer_api__interfaces__dtos__inbox_c.description: Attach an existing tag to a conversation.

audience_list_id.title: Audience List Id
audience_list_id.description: If provided, attaches this list ID to cb_campaigns.audience_list_id at create time.

target_channels.title: Target Channels
target_channels.description: Channels the campaign will use, e.g. ['email'], ['email','linkedin']. Drives which copy documents the auto-generator creates. Defaults to ['email'].

execution_targets.title: Execution Targets
execution_targets.description: Execution destinations: sequencer, dialer, or content_only.

secondary_hooks.title: Secondary Hooks
secondary_hooks.description: Additional hook variations to seed the campaign idea with.

auto_generate_documents.title: Auto Generate Documents
auto_generate_documents.description: When True, dispatches the Celery campaign-content generator asynchronously after creation: the paired cb_campaign_ideas row is inserted (so the FE workbench sees the campaign), cb_campaign_metadata is created, the campaign starts in status='copy_in_progress', and flips to 'active' once docs are ready (~60-90s). Default is False to preserve byte-for-byte backwards compatibility with the original bare-bones draft behavior — the MCP tool wrapper sets True explicitly to opt into Studio parity.
